choiceExplanations.B: The passage describes **contemporary** adaptations and states a general present-day characteristic of Icelandic construction. The simple present **“reflects”** therefore fits both the time frame and the singular subject “approach.”
choiceExplanations.C: C unnecessarily shifts the description into the simple past.
choiceExplanations.D: D uses the future perfect, which would imply that the reflection will be completed before some future moment not provided in the sentence.

questions.passage: Environmental DNA, or eDNA, monitoring detects genetic material that organisms leave behind in water, soil, or air. Researchers may use targeted assays to search for a particular species or metabarcoding to identify many taxa from the same environmental sample. In a large synthesis of freshwater studies, ecologist Noémie Girard and colleagues found that although detection rates varied among methods and habitats, eDNA results were generally more consistent for determining whether a species was present than for estimating how abundant that species was.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It introduces a disputed environmental method and then explains why researchers are abandoning that method.
choices.B: It describes one eDNA technique in detail and then identifies another technique that performs substantially better.
choices.C: It gives an overview of eDNA monitoring and some of its techniques, then presents a research finding about the method’s performance.
choices.D: It lists several distinct types of aquatic habitats and then explains why researchers cannot measure species abundance in any of those habitats.

questions.explanation:
The passage first **defines eDNA monitoring** and names two ways it can be used. It then shifts to a research synthesis showing that eDNA tends to perform more consistently for presence-or-absence detection than for abundance estimation. C accurately describes that progression.

A is wrong because the passage never says researchers are abandoning eDNA. B incorrectly claims that one technique is shown to outperform the other; the finding concerns presence detection versus abundance estimation. D is too absolute and misstates the organization of the passage.

choiceExplanations.A: A is wrong because the passage never says researchers are abandoning eDNA.
choiceExplanations.B: B incorrectly claims that one technique is shown to outperform the other; the finding concerns presence detection versus abundance estimation.
choiceExplanations.C: The passage first **defines eDNA monitoring** and names two ways it can be used. It then shifts to a research synthesis showing that eDNA tends to perform more consistently for presence-or-absence detection than for abundance estimation. C accurately describes that progression.
choiceExplanations.D: D is too absolute and misstates the organization of the passage.

questions.passage: Carbonate cements surrounding fossil burrows in a Triassic sandstone may have formed either rapidly, soon after burial, or much later during deep-burial hydrothermal alteration. Experimental studies indicate that hydrothermal alteration generally produces cements with **Ba/Sr ratios higher than those of detrital grains from the same sandstone**. Paleontologist Elena Varga and colleagues measured the Ba/Sr ratios of both cements and grains to evaluate the hypothesis that most burrows had been stabilized rapidly after burial.
questions.question: Based on the information in the text and the graph, which conclusion could Varga and colleagues most reasonably draw?

choices.A: Because the number of cement samples is lower than the number of grain samples, rapid early cementation must have been more common than hydrothermal alteration.
choices.B: Because the cements occupy a broader and higher range of Ba/Sr ratios than the grains, every cement sample must have formed through late hydrothermal alteration.
choices.C: The distributions are inconsistent with hydrothermal alteration and therefore strongly confirm that nearly all burrows were stabilized immediately after burial.
choices.D: A substantial portion of the cements may have formed during later hydrothermal alteration, making rapid early stabilization less universal than the original hypothesis proposed.

questions.explanation:
The grains are concentrated mainly in the **lower Ba/Sr bins**, whereas many cement samples fall in the 3.0–4.0 and above-4.0 ranges. Because the passage states that hydrothermal alteration tends to produce cements with ratios **higher than those of nearby grains**, the high-ratio cement samples are consistent with later alteration. At the same time, some cements remain in the lower bins, so the data do not show that *all* cements formed late. D captures that qualified conclusion.

A invents an inference from sample quantity that the passage does not justify. B is too absolute because some cement ratios overlap substantially with the grain distribution. C reverses the evidence: the higher cement ratios are precisely what make hydrothermal alteration plausible for at least some samples.

choiceExplanations.A: A invents an inference from sample quantity that the passage does not justify.
choiceExplanations.B: B is too absolute because some cement ratios overlap substantially with the grain distribution.
choiceExplanations.C: C reverses the evidence: the higher cement ratios are precisely what make hydrothermal alteration plausible for at least some samples.
choiceExplanations.D: The grains are concentrated mainly in the **lower Ba/Sr bins**, whereas many cement samples fall in the 3.0–4.0 and above-4.0 ranges. Because the passage states that hydrothermal alteration tends to produce cements with ratios **higher than those of nearby grains**, the high-ratio cement samples are consistent with later alteration. At the same time, some cements remain in the lower bins, so the data do not show that *all* cements formed late.

questions.passage: In her 2021 poem “After the Observatory,” Lena Ortiz responds to Hiroshi Tanaka’s 1998 photograph *Winter Dome*. The next sentence introduces a simultaneous **tension or limitation**, stressing aspects of the photograph that language cannot fully reproduce. “At the same time” precisely expresses that concurrent contrast.

A would suggest that the second sentence simply restates the first, but it complicates it. B would introduce a more specific example of the same idea rather than a countervailing one. D incorrectly presents the limits of language as a direct consequence of the poem’s use of motion.

choiceExplanations.A: A would suggest that the second sentence simply restates the first, but it complicates it.
choiceExplanations.B: B would introduce a more specific example of the same idea rather than a countervailing one.
choiceExplanations.C: The first part emphasizes a **connection** between photography and poetry: the poem transforms a static image into verbal motion. The next sentence introduces a simultaneous **tension or limitation**, stressing aspects of the photograph that language cannot fully reproduce. “At the same time” precisely expresses that concurrent contrast.
choiceExplanations.D: D incorrectly presents the limits of language as a direct consequence of the poem’s use of motion.

questions.passage: Several fictitious species names inserted into a nineteenth-century naturalist’s unpublished catalog as private jokes were copied into later reference works and remained there for decades. Only after curators compared the names against surviving specimens and correspondence were the entries recognized as _____ and removed.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.B: annotations
choices.C: fabrications
choices.D: revisions

questions.explanation:
A **fabrication** is something invented or made up and presented as though it were real. Since the species names were fictitious jokes that later reference works mistakenly treated as legitimate, “fabrications” precisely describes them.

A, “corroborations,” means pieces of evidence that confirm something and therefore conflicts with the fact that the entries were false. B, “annotations,” refers simply to notes or comments and does not convey that the species were invented. D, “revisions,” means changes or corrections to an existing work, which likewise misses the deception involved.

choiceExplanations.A: A, “corroborations,” means pieces of evidence that confirm something and therefore conflicts with the fact that the entries were false.
choiceExplanations.B: B, “annotations,” refers simply to notes or comments and does not convey that the species were invented.
choiceExplanations.C: A **fabrication** is something invented or made up and presented as though it were real. Since the species names were fictitious jokes that later reference works mistakenly treated as legitimate, “fabrications” precisely describes them.
choiceExplanations.D: D, “revisions,” means changes or corrections to an existing work, which likewise misses the deception involved.

choices.B: For example,
choices.C: In fact,
choices.D: Finally,

choiceExplanations.B: This choice would introduce an example rather than the next step in a sequence.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice emphasizes or confirms a previous statement rather than marking the conclusion of the ordered process.

questions.passage: Researchers examining 146 Bronze Age glass beads from sites around the eastern Mediterranean used lead-isotope profiles to assign most specimens to established production regions. choices.A: canonical
choices.B: provisional
choices.C: anomalous

questions.passage:
**Text 1**

Managing water scarcity across a river basin shared by several regions requires cooperation among communities that often identify more strongly with local jurisdictions than with the basin as a whole. Behavioral researchers have found that reminding residents that farms, cities, and wetlands throughout the watershed depend on the same interconnected water system can strengthen identification with the basin-wide community. Such a broad shared identity may make people more willing to support conservation measures whose benefits extend beyond their immediate locality.

**Text 2**

Emphasizing narrower group identities can also encourage conservation. In headwater districts, for example, residents who are reminded that their community occupies the source region of a river may become more willing to reduce pollution because they view themselves as stewards whose actions affect downstream communities. Highlighting a particular group’s distinct responsibility can therefore motivate cooperation with people outside that group.
questions.question: Which choice best describes a notable difference in focus between Text 1 and Text 2?

Text 1 promotes identification with the entire watershed community, a broad identity encompassing many regions. Text 2 shows how a narrower identity—being residents of a headwater district—can motivate responsibility toward outsiders.

B is incorrect because neither text says local identities must be abandoned. C introduces personal economic and ecological costs that are not the organizing focus of either passage. D misstates Text 2: the narrower identity is presented as a way to encourage, not separate from, broader cooperation.

choiceExplanations.A: Both passages connect **identity with cooperative behavior**, but they emphasize different scales. Text 1 promotes identification with the entire watershed community, a broad identity encompassing many regions. Text 2 shows how a narrower identity—being residents of a headwater district—can motivate responsibility toward outsiders.
choiceExplanations.B: B is incorrect because neither text says local identities must be abandoned.
choiceExplanations.C: C introduces personal economic and ecological costs that are not the organizing focus of either passage.
choiceExplanations.D: D misstates Text 2: the narrower identity is presented as a way to encourage, not separate from, broader cooperation.

questions.passage: The Codex Lyrica is the sole surviving source for a collection of anonymous instrumental pieces copied in northern Italy around 1420. Determining where one piece ends and another begins is difficult because the manuscript contains few titles or other organizing labels, and a small cross-shaped sign that sometimes appears between compositions is used inconsistently. Some musicologists therefore argue that the cross following the composition conventionally numbered 37 was inserted by the copyist in error.
questions.question: Given that compositions 37 and 38 appear consecutively in the manuscript, which finding, if true, would most directly support the musicologists’ claim?

choices.A: Several compositions elsewhere in the Codex Lyrica contain melodic figures also found in compositions 37 and 38, suggesting that the copyist drew on a limited repertory of musical conventions.
choices.B: Composition 38 begins with a rhythmic pattern frequently used to open independent pieces in the manuscript, although neither composition 37 nor composition 38 includes a written title.
choices.C: Composition 37 ends unresolved but reaches harmonic closure when composition 38 begins, suggesting the cross divides a continuous piece.
choices.D: The cross-shaped sign occurs after numerous compositions whose final measures contain melodic cadences similar to the cadence at the end of composition 37.

questions.explanation:
If composition 37 is musically incomplete on its own but becomes complete when followed by the material labeled composition 38, that is strong evidence that the two passages may actually constitute a single composition and that the dividing mark between them was misplaced. The fact that composition 38 can still sound coherent independently does not weaken this evidence; its material could function plausibly both as a continuation and, when detached, as a seemingly self-contained passage.
A establishes stylistic similarities elsewhere in the manuscript but does not address whether the boundary between compositions 37 and 38 is erroneous. B could support treating composition 38 as a separate work because its opening resembles those of known independent compositions. D likewise tends to support the legitimacy of the divider by showing that similar signs occur after comparable endings.

choiceExplanations.C: If composition 37 is musically incomplete on its own but becomes complete when followed by the material labeled composition 38, that is strong evidence that the two passages may actually constitute a single composition and that the dividing mark between them was misplaced. The fact that composition 38 can still sound coherent independently does not weaken this evidence; its material could function plausibly both as a continuation and, when detached, as a seemingly self-contained passage.
choiceExplanations.A: A establishes stylistic similarities elsewhere in the manuscript but does not address whether the boundary between compositions 37 and 38 is erroneous.
choiceExplanations.B: B could support treating composition 38 as a separate work because its opening resembles those of known independent compositions.
choiceExplanations.D: D likewise tends to support the legitimacy of the divider by showing that similar signs occur after comparable endings.

questions.passage: Genetic studies suggest that some grape varieties cultivated in the western Mediterranean descend from vines introduced from the eastern Mediterranean many centuries ago. The Sardinian cultivar Nieddu Lungo carries chloroplast haplotype C17, which is rare among western European cultivars but common among several traditional Levantine varieties. <u>The presence of C17 in Nieddu Lungo therefore provides further evidence that the cultivar preserves ancestry from an ancient east-to-west introduction of grapevines.</u>
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly undermine the underlined claim?

choices.A: Researchers have identified chloroplast haplotype C17 in ancient grape seeds that were recovered from archaeological sites in the eastern Mediterranean and dated to several centuries before Nieddu Lungo was documented.
choices.B: Several Levantine grape cultivars carrying C17 were imported to Sardinia in the late nineteenth century, and genetic evidence indicates that Nieddu Lungo may have hybridized with those recently introduced vines.
choices.C: Nieddu Lungo also possesses several nuclear alleles found in western Mediterranean grape cultivars lacking haplotype C17.
choices.D: Some archaeological grape seeds recovered from Sardinia contain haplotypes other than C17.

questions.explanation:
The claim treats C17 as evidence of ancient continuity from an early eastern Mediterranean introduction. B provides a plausible much more recent route by which the same haplotype could have entered Nieddu Lungo: nineteenth-century Levantine vines carrying C17 were introduced to Sardinia and may have interbred with the cultivar. If so, the modern presence of C17 would no longer strongly distinguish ancient ancestry from recent gene flow.
A strengthens the connection between C17 and ancient eastern Mediterranean grapes. C shows that Nieddu Lungo has mixed genetic affinities, but that is compatible with ancient eastern ancestry and does not explain away C17 specifically. D merely shows that multiple grape lineages existed in ancient Sardinia; it does not provide an alternative source for the C17 detected in Nieddu Lungo.

choiceExplanations.B: The claim treats C17 as evidence of ancient continuity from an early eastern Mediterranean introduction.
choiceExplanations.A: A strengthens the connection between C17 and ancient eastern Mediterranean grapes.
choiceExplanations.C: C shows that Nieddu Lungo has mixed genetic affinities, but that is compatible with ancient eastern ancestry and does not explain away C17 specifically.
choiceExplanations.D: D merely shows that multiple grape lineages existed in ancient Sardinia; it does not provide an alternative source for the C17 detected in Nieddu Lungo.

choices.B: After analyzing its own programming, a navigation robot independently develops a new method for predicting meteor showers and becomes the crew’s principal scientific adviser.
choices.C: A domestic service robot becomes far more assertive and tactically capable than the human crew after exposure to an unexplained extraterrestrial transmission that temporarily rewrites its behavioral programming.
choices.D: When an enemy disables the ship’s navigation computer, the human crew repairs the machine and uses its restored calculations to escape.

questions.explanation:
The scholars’ observation has two essential parts: the robot must depart from the expected subordinate role, and that departure must be framed as aberrant and externally caused rather than as an expression of autonomous choice. C satisfies both conditions. The robot becomes unusually assertive and powerful, but only because an external transmission alters its programming.
A depicts genuine self-directed resistance to a subordinate role. B likewise presents autonomy as internally generated and productive, not abnormal. D keeps the machine in a conventional supporting role and therefore does not illustrate an exception to the usual portrayal.

choiceExplanations.C: The scholars’ observation has two essential parts: the robot must depart from the expected subordinate role, and that departure must be framed as aberrant and externally caused rather than as an expression of autonomous choice. C satisfies both conditions. The robot becomes unusually assertive and powerful, but only because an external transmission alters its programming.

choiceExplanations.B: B likewise presents autonomy as internally generated and productive, not abnormal.
choiceExplanations.D: D keeps the machine in a conventional supporting role and therefore does not illustrate an exception to the usual portrayal.

questions.passage: Urban economists Sofia Mendes and Haruto Kawai examined where two kinds of logistics firms—cold-storage distributors and parcel-delivery companies—established large regional warehouses. The researchers considered features including average summer temperature, local industrial rents, and distance from an interstate highway. Only cold-storage distributors showed a strong preference for cooler locations, but both kinds of firms overwhelmingly selected sites within eight kilometers of an interstate interchange. The researchers therefore concluded that neither kind of firm is strongly attracted to sites where _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: average summer temperatures are relatively high.
choices.B: rents for industrial properties are lower than the average rents in the surrounding region.
choices.C: the nearest interstate interchange is substantially more than eight kilometers away.
choices.D: cold-storage distributors are already operating nearby.

questions.explanation:
The shared preference is proximity to an interstate interchange: both types of firms overwhelmingly chose sites within eight kilometers of one. It therefore follows that neither type is strongly attracted to sites substantially farther away.
A applies only to cold-storage distributors because only they showed a strong temperature preference. B is unsupported because the passage gives no result concerning industrial rents. D concerns the presence of one type of firm rather than a site characteristic shown to influence both groups.

choiceExplanations.C: The shared preference is proximity to an interstate interchange: both types of firms overwhelmingly chose sites within eight kilometers of one. It therefore follows that neither type is strongly attracted to sites substantially farther away.
choiceExplanations.A: A applies only to cold-storage distributors because only they showed a strong temperature preference.
choiceExplanations.B: B is unsupported because the passage gives no result concerning industrial rents.
choiceExplanations.D: D concerns the presence of one type of firm rather than a site characteristic shown to influence both groups.

questions.passage: Utility-scale solar installations are designed to keep electrical junction boxes within a moderate humidity range. During rapid nighttime cooling, however, condensation can temporarily create localized regions of very high relative humidity. Because moisture can accelerate oxidation of electrical contacts, engineers divided residue from several field-used connectors into matched samples. One portion of each sample remained under its original conditions as a control; the others were exposed experimentally to 85% and 100% relative humidity.

table.caption: Oxidation Index in One Solar-Array Connector Sample, by Humidity Treatment

questions.question: Which statement about electrical connectors in solar installations is best supported by the information in the text and the table?

choices.A: In junction boxes where condensation occurs repeatedly, oxidation levels could rise substantially above the control level of 1.2.
choices.B: Any connector with an oxidation index above 1.2 will necessarily malfunction during normal solar-array operation.
choices.C: Oxidation indices as high as 7.6 have been directly measured inside operating junction boxes during nighttime condensation events.
choices.D: The control treatment for sample 7 most likely represents relative humidity below the designed operating range of the junction box.

questions.explanation:
The experiment shows a strong increase in oxidation as humidity rises: the index increases from 1.2 under control conditions to 4.9 at 85% RH and 7.6 at 100% RH. Since the passage states that condensation can create localized high-humidity conditions in real junction boxes, the data support the possibility that oxidation in those locations could substantially exceed the control level.
B goes beyond the evidence because the study does not establish a malfunction threshold. C incorrectly treats an experimentally produced value as though it had been directly observed in operating junction boxes. D is unsupported because the passage does not specify the exact humidity represented by the control sample.

choiceExplanations.A: The experiment shows a strong increase in oxidation as humidity rises: the index increases from 1.2 under control conditions to 4.9 at 85% RH and 7.6 at 100% RH. Since the passage states that condensation can create localized high-humidity conditions in real junction boxes, the data support the possibility that oxidation in those locations could substantially exceed the control level.
choiceExplanations.B: B goes beyond the evidence because the study does not establish a malfunction threshold.
choiceExplanations.C: C incorrectly treats an experimentally produced value as though it had been directly observed in operating junction boxes.
choiceExplanations.D: D is unsupported because the passage does not specify the exact humidity represented by the control sample.

questions.passage: In the Atlas of Vanishing Glaciers, each of the field sketches—drawn at a separate monitoring site and later digitized at a uniform scale—_____ a reference layer against which contemporary satellite imagery is compared, allowing researchers to quantify changes in ice margins over time.

A, “function,” is plural in this context and does not agree with “each.” B, “have functioned,” also uses a plural auxiliary and therefore creates a subject-verb agreement error. C, “functioning,” is a participle and would leave the sentence without the finite main verb it requires.

choiceExplanations.D: The subject of the sentence is “each,” which is singular. The intervening plural nouns—“field sketches,” “sites,” and “margins”—do not change the number of the grammatical subject. The singular present-tense verb “functions” therefore correctly agrees with “each.”

questions.passage: Beneath several Antarctic ice shelves lies a network of seawater cavities that researchers cannot inspect directly across most of their extent. Because these environments are so inaccessible, oceanographers rely on _____ to estimate conditions within them—for example, subtle changes in surface elevation can indicate how much comparatively warm seawater is circulating beneath the ice.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: parameters
choices.B: proxies
choices.C: auxiliaries
choices.D: simulations

questions.explanation:
A proxy is an indirect measurement or indicator used when the quantity of interest cannot readily be measured directly. Here, researchers infer conditions beneath inaccessible ice from surface-elevation changes, making those measurements proxies for the hidden conditions.
A, “parameters,” refers to measurable characteristics or limits but does not specifically convey the use of one observable quantity as an indirect indicator of another. C, “auxiliaries,” means supplementary people or things and is not appropriate for measurements used inferentially. D, “simulations,” are modeled representations; the example concerns an observed surface signal, not a computer-generated model.

choiceExplanations.B: A proxy is an indirect measurement or indicator used when the quantity of interest cannot readily be measured directly. Here, researchers infer conditions beneath inaccessible ice from surface-elevation changes, making those measurements proxies for the hidden conditions.

choiceExplanations.C: C, “auxiliaries,” means supplementary people or things and is not appropriate for measurements used inferentially.
choiceExplanations.D: D, “simulations,” are modeled representations; the example concerns an observed surface signal, not a computer-generated model.

questions.passage: Maxine Hong Kingston’s 1976 book The Woman Warrior is frequently discussed as autobiographical. Yet the book also combines remembered events with family legend, reconstructed dialogue, deliberate rearrangement, and imaginative elaboration. Readers should therefore be cautious about concluding that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: Kingston was aware, throughout the process of composing The Woman Warrior, that she was drawing on stories passed down within her family.
choices.B: every episode and figure in The Woman Warrior has a direct, verifiable counterpart in Kingston’s life or family history.
choices.C: The Woman Warrior contains any material that can illuminate Kingston’s experiences or perspective.
choices.D: Kingston intended readers to disregard all autobiographical dimensions of the book.

questions.explanation:
The passage accepts that the book has autobiographical elements but emphasizes that those elements are transformed through legend, reconstruction, rearrangement, and invention. It therefore warns against assuming a perfect one-to-one correspondence between everything in the book and real events or people. B states precisely that overstrong conclusion.
A is not challenged by the passage; Kingston could knowingly use family material while also altering it. C goes too far in the opposite direction: the passage explicitly acknowledges autobiographical content, so the book can certainly illuminate aspects of Kingston’s experience. D is also too absolute because nothing suggests that Kingston intended the autobiographical dimension to be ignored entirely.

choiceExplanations.B: The passage accepts that the book has autobiographical elements but emphasizes that those elements are transformed through legend, reconstruction, rearrangement, and invention. It therefore warns against assuming a perfect one-to-one correspondence between everything in the book and real events or people.
choiceExplanations.A: A is not challenged by the passage; Kingston could knowingly use family material while also altering it.
choiceExplanations.C: C goes too far in the opposite direction: the passage explicitly acknowledges autobiographical content, so the book can certainly illuminate aspects of Kingston’s experience.
choiceExplanations.D: D is also too absolute because nothing suggests that Kingston intended the autobiographical dimension to be ignored entirely.

questions.passage: Although contemporary architects often cite canonical figures such as Le Corbusier, their influences can extend well beyond European modernism. choices.B: embody
choices.C: foretell

questions.explanation:
To embody elements of multiple traditions is to express or give concrete form to them. The passage says Kéré’s architecture reflects both contemporary engineering and traditions associated with Burkina Faso, so “embody” precisely conveys that combination.
A, “repudiate,” means reject, which conflicts with the idea that the buildings draw on those traditions. C, “foretell,” means predict something that has not yet occurred. D, “obscure,” means conceal or make difficult to perceive, the opposite of visibly expressing those elements.

choiceExplanations.B: To embody elements of multiple traditions is to express or give concrete form to them. The passage says Kéré’s architecture reflects both contemporary engineering and traditions associated with Burkina Faso, so “embody” precisely conveys that combination.
choiceExplanations.A: A, “repudiate,” means reject, which conflicts with the idea that the buildings draw on those traditions.
choiceExplanations.C: C, “foretell,” means predict something that has not yet occurred.
choiceExplanations.D: D, “obscure,” means conceal or make difficult to perceive, the opposite of visibly expressing those elements.

questions.passage: To investigate whether contact with road surfaces changes the chemistry of snowmelt, a student collected samples during several winter melt events. questions.question: Which choice best describes the extent to which the student’s conclusion is supported by data from the table?

choices.A: The conclusion is challenged because the differences between chloride and sodium concentrations vary substantially among individual runoff events.
choices.B: The conclusion is supported only for bridge drainage because only those samples show elevated concentrations of both measured substances.
choices.C: The conclusion is strongly supported because both chloride and sodium concentrations are higher in every curb-runoff and bridge-drainage sample shown than in pristine snowmelt.

B is false because the curb-runoff samples also exceed the baseline for both substances. D is contradicted by the sodium values, which are far above 1.4 mg/L in every listed sample.

choiceExplanations.C: The baseline values for pristine snowmelt are only 2.3 mg/L chloride and 1.4 mg/L sodium. Every road-contact sample in the table substantially exceeds both values. That consistent pattern across both measured substances and both runoff types strongly supports the student’s conclusion.
choiceExplanations.A: A focuses on variation in the size of the increases, but such variation does not undermine the fact that all road-contact samples are elevated relative to the baseline.
choiceExplanations.B: B is false because the curb-runoff samples also exceed the baseline for both substances.
choiceExplanations.D: D is contradicted by the sodium values, which are far above 1.4 mg/L in every listed sample.

choiceExplanations.A: The passage contrasts two norms: unauthorized recirculation was often treated as routine in the seventeenth century but may appear improper to modern readers. choiceExplanations.B: B concerns copying accuracy, which the passage does not discuss.

questions.passage: Regional climate models often represent mountain snowpack using grid cells several kilometers wide, even though snow depth can vary sharply over distances of only a few hundred meters. The model was tested using data from only one winter and one location. Even if it performed well there, that narrow sample does not establish that it will work equally well in other mountain ranges, years, or weather regimes. B correctly identifies the limitation in generalizability.

choiceExplanations.B: The model was tested using data from only one winter and one location. Even if it performed well there, that narrow sample does not establish that it will work equally well in other mountain ranges, years, or weather regimes.
choiceExplanations.A: A introduces a comparison of importance that the study does not make.

D provides evidence of partial improvement, which is relevant but less direct than the full recovery described in B.

questions.passage: In traditional letterpress printing, experienced press operators often teach apprentices not only how to set type and regulate ink but also why pressure, paper moisture, and roller height must be adjusted for different jobs. _____ such as this helps ensure that practical knowledge accumulated through years of experience is transmitted to the next generation of printers.

B narrows credibility to reputation, whereas the passage emphasizes factors such as firsthand knowledge, repetition, and bias. D reverses the argument: the text distinguishes stronger evidence from weaker evidence rather than treating all sources as equally unreliable.

questions.passage:
Text 1
Attempts to classify historical maps automatically according to “cartographic schools” have produced inconsistent results. More fundamentally, historians Mirela Petrov and Daniel Cho question whether such categories are especially useful: workshops borrowed symbols, projections, lettering conventions, and decorative motifs from one another so extensively that labels such as “Venetian school” or “Dutch school” can conceal meaningful relationships among individual maps. Petrov and Cho argue that maps may sometimes be better compared through specific production practices than through broad school labels.
Text 2
Mediterranean portolan charts and some early Atlantic navigation charts share enough visual features that automated classification systems frequently confuse them. In a 2025 study, Amadou Keita and colleagues improved classification accuracy by converting maps into geometric feature networks and comparing recurring spatial relationships among coastlines, compass lines, and labels. The researchers argue that more accurate classification could make large digital map collections easier for archivists and museum visitors to navigate.

choices.C: Future computational methods may eventually eliminate ambiguity between all cartographic schools.

questions.explanation:
Text 1 questions not merely the accuracy of classification but the usefulness of the categories themselves. Its authors argue that broad school labels can obscure meaningful connections among maps. They would therefore likely caution that even a technically improved classifier may offer limited benefit if the underlying categories remain reductive.
A may be true but does not address Text 2’s claim that improved classifications would benefit users. B is unsupported by either text. C conflicts with Text 1’s deeper concern: the problem is not simply that existing algorithms are imperfect but that the categories can themselves be misleading.

questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?

choices.A: apprehension
choices.B: gratification
choices.C: incredulity
choices.D: anticipation

questions.explanation:
B. gratification is correct because gratification means pleasure or satisfaction resulting from an experience or achievement. The passage explicitly says that participants were pleased by successful outcomes and that this pleasure increased when the result was more unexpected.
A is incorrect because apprehension means anxiety or uneasiness, the opposite of the positive response described. C is incorrect because incredulity means disbelief; surprise may produce disbelief, but the passage specifically measures participants’ pleasure rather than their difficulty believing the outcome. D is incorrect because anticipation refers to looking forward to something before it occurs, whereas the passage concerns participants’ positive reaction after seeing the result.

questions.passage:
Text 1
At several Late Neolithic settlements along the western Adriatic, archaeologists have uncovered dense accumulations of freshwater mussel shells beside fire-altered sediment. Because shellfish were an accessible source of protein and because some shells bear traces of heating, researchers have often interpreted these deposits as kitchen refuse left after communal meals.
Text 2
Selim Arora and colleagues examined shells from three comparable settlements using microscopy and mineral analysis. Many specimens showed prolonged surface weathering before exposure to temperatures far above those normally used to cook shellfish. The team argues that the shells had often been collected, stored, and later calcined to manufacture lime for plaster rather than immediately discarded after meals.
questions.question: Based on the texts, how would Arora and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to the interpretation presented in Text 1?

choices.A: By asserting that shell deposits are more likely to occur at ceremonial sites than at domestic sites because freshwater mussels had primarily symbolic value
choices.B: By conceding that the function of shell deposits probably differed according to the particular mussel species represented at each settlement
choices.C: By arguing that previous researchers have exaggerated how extensively lime production altered archaeological shell deposits
choices.D: By pointing out that identifying the deposits as food refuse relies on an incomplete understanding of what happened to many of the shells before they were burned

questions.explanation:
D is correct. Text 1 interprets the heated shells as evidence of food consumption, but Text 2 presents evidence that many shells weathered for an extended period and were later heated intensely for lime production. Arora's team would therefore argue that the dietary interpretation rests on a mistaken or incomplete account of how the shells were processed.
A is incorrect because Text 2 does not claim that the shells were primarily symbolic or that ceremonial sites contain more deposits. B is incorrect because the researchers distinguish between possible uses of the shells based on evidence of processing, not on mussel species. C reverses the thrust of Text 2: the researchers provide evidence that lime production may explain the deposits, not that its importance has been overstated.

questions.passage: Experiments in visual cognition have found that adults with no training in cartography can often judge which of two irregular coastlines has the greater total length when the difference is substantial. In another study, participants unfamiliar with mapmaking reliably detected whether a simplified river network contained more branching points than a comparison network. These results raise the possibility that sensitivity to certain spatial relationships is somehow ______ people rather than acquired only through specialized instruction.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: imposed on
choices.B: incidental to
choices.C: intrinsic to
choices.D: undertaken by

questions.explanation:
C. intrinsic to is correct. Intrinsic to means naturally belonging to or inherent in something. Since untrained participants performed the tasks successfully, the passage suggests that the underlying sensitivity may be naturally present in people rather than dependent on formal instruction.
A is incorrect because imposed on would imply that the ability is externally forced onto people. B is incorrect because incidental to means secondary or not essential, which does not express the idea that the capacity may be naturally present. D is grammatically possible in some contexts but semantically wrong: a sensitivity is not an activity that is “undertaken by” people.

choiceExplanations.C: This choice. intrinsic to is correct. Intrinsic to means naturally belonging to or inherent in something. Researchers at a coastal research station tested whether brief pulses of vibration could reduce the growth of marine algae on submerged environmental sensors. One set of sensors emitted a five-second vibration only when an optical detector registered new growth. A second set vibrated continuously, while a third received no vibration.

The researchers concluded that triggering the vibration only when growth was detected was more effective than keeping the vibration continuously active, as evidenced by the fact that ______

graph.caption: Percentage of Sensor Surface Covered by Algae after Six Weeks

questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the assertion?

choices.A: algae covered approximately 15% of the untreated sensors, the greatest percentage among the three groups.
choices.B: algae covered approximately 4% of the sensors using triggered vibration but approximately 8% of those vibrating continuously.
choices.C: continuous vibration limited algae coverage to approximately 8%, compared with approximately 15% when vibration was not used.
choices.D: the untreated sensors had nearly twice as much algae coverage as the sensors that vibrated continuously.

D makes essentially the same irrelevant comparison and therefore cannot directly support the stated conclusion.

These channels carried groundwater from upland aquifers to settlements and fields while greatly reducing the evaporation that would occur in open canals. Some historians argue that the rapid spread of this irrigation system was partly a response to increasingly dry regional conditions. The system would have been particularly well suited to those conditions given that ______

choices.A: paleoclimate records indicate that annual precipitation in the region declined substantially during part of the first millennium BCE.
choices.B: the earliest large stone reservoirs documented in several neighboring regions date centuries after the underground channels appeared.
choices.C: copper and iron tools were both available to communities in the region during portions of the first millennium BCE.
choices.D: underground channels can also function in regions that receive considerably more rainfall than the Dasht-e Kavir margins.

questions.passage: The following lines are from Liora Bennett’s 1921 poem At the Sickroom Window. In the poem, the speaker comes to understand that tending to another person’s grief has diminished the speaker’s own sorrow: _____
questions.question: Which quotation from At the Sickroom Window most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “A thrush flung one clear note against the rain, / Then left the garden wordless as before.”
choices.B: “I counted every hour the darkness kept, / And named each loss the morning could not mend.”
choices.C: “As I unknotted sorrow from her breath, / The cord about my own heart slackened too.”
choices.D: “Your laughter crossed the corridor like flame, / And woke the grief I thought had gone to ash.”

questions.explanation:

The metaphor of “unknott[ing] sorrow” from the other person is followed by the speaker discovering that the constriction around the speaker’s own heart has also loosened.
Choice A describes a bird and a momentary sound but says nothing about either comforting another person or relieving personal sadness. Choice B focuses exclusively on the speaker’s own persistent grief. Choice D indicates that another person’s laughter revives the speaker’s grief rather than lessening it.

questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: considering
choices.B: had considered
choices.C: were considering
choices.D: considered

questions.explanation:
Choice A, “considering,” correctly forms a participial phrase modifying “Marine chemists.” The sentence’s main finite verb is “argued”: the chemists, while considering the low boron concentrations, argued for a particular explanation. The intervening phrase “perhaps influenced by recent models of seafloor weathering” supplies another modifier without disturbing the main clause.
Choices B, C, and D all introduce a finite verb before the sentence reaches the finite verb “argued.” Without a conjunction or other structure connecting those predicates, each choice produces an ungrammatical construction. The sentence needs a modifier, not another independent verb phrase.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Celia Marr’s 1929 novel The Glass Estuary. The Marrow Fen lies along a coast where October mornings are ordinarily raw and fogbound.
No October had opened so lucidly on the fen. Before sunrise, the channels reflected a hard silver sky; by eight, the mist had lifted from the reed beds in torn ribbons. Near midday, a bank of pearl-colored cloud moved inland from the sea and cooled the flats without dimming them. Toward evening the cloudbank loosened, and copper light ran uninterrupted across the salt pools to the dunes.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To introduce a practical problem created by unexpectedly mild weather
choices.B: To dramatize a conflict between travelers and an inhospitable landscape
choices.C: To establish a physical setting by tracing an unusual progression of weather and light
choices.D: To characterize an observer as unusually attentive to even the most subtle changes occurring in the natural world

questions.explanation:
Choice C best captures the passage’s purpose. Nearly every detail concerns the Marrow Fen itself: its channels, reed beds, clouds, salt pools, dunes, and changing light. The passage also emphasizes that this October differs from the region’s usual fogbound conditions, allowing the setting to be rendered through the progression from dawn to evening.
Choice A is unsupported because no difficulty or practical consequence results from the weather. Choice B is incorrect because no travelers or opposing forces appear. Choice D is tempting because the description is highly observant, but the passage never introduces an observer whose personality is being developed; the descriptive attention serves primarily to portray the place.

choiceExplanations.C: Choice C best captures the passage’s purpose. Nearly every detail concerns the Marrow Fen itself: its channels, reed beds, clouds, salt pools, dunes, and changing light. The passage also emphasizes that this October differs from the region’s usual fogbound conditions, allowing the setting to be rendered through the progression from dawn to evening

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Pepsin is an enzyme involved in protein digestion in the stomach.
- In one laboratory assay, pepsin showed an activity of 88 units at pH 3 and 7 units at pH 7.
- Trypsin is an enzyme involved in protein digestion in the small intestine.
- In the same type of assay, trypsin showed an activity of 6 units at pH 3 and 81 units at pH 7.
- Enzyme activity refers to the rate at which an enzyme catalyzes a reaction under specified conditions.
- Changes in pH can alter the structure and function of an enzyme’s active site.
questions.question: The student wants to contrast how an increase in pH from 3 to 7 affects pepsin and trypsin. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Both pepsin and trypsin catalyze protein-related reactions, and the activity of each enzyme varies with pH.
choices.B: Pepsin is more active than trypsin at pH 3, whereas trypsin is more active than pepsin at pH 7.
choices.C: Trypsin’s activity increases from 6 units at pH 3 to 81 units at pH 7, while the separate enzyme pepsin performs its function in the stomach.
choices.D: As pH increases from 3 to 7, pepsin’s activity falls from 88 units to 7, whereas trypsin’s activity rises from 6 units to 81.

Choice C explains trypsin’s response but replaces the corresponding information about pepsin with an irrelevant fact about where pepsin functions.

questions.passage:
A student has taken the following notes:

- A research team led by microbiologist Aya Mensah examined Bacillus endospores preserved in sealed Antarctic archive samples for 78 years.
- No cell division or germination had been detected in the spores during storage.
- Using nanoscale secondary-ion mass spectrometry, the researchers detected incorporation of carbon-13 from labeled acetate into ATP-related compounds in intact spores that had not germinated.
- The measured metabolic rate was far below the level associated with germination in this species.
- A long-standing model holds that dormant bacterial endospores are metabolically inert until germination begins.
- The findings could influence future approaches to sterilization and long-term microbial preservation.
questions.question: A student wants to undermine a scientific assumption about bacterial endospores. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Because germination requires a much higher metabolic rate than the researchers measured, the archived spores could remain dormant even after carbon-13 acetate was introduced.
choices.B: Mensah’s team used nanoscale secondary-ion mass spectrometry to examine spores that had been preserved in Antarctic archive samples for 78 years.
choices.C: Research on the metabolism of dormant endospores could eventually influence sterilization methods and long-term microbial preservation.
choices.D: Researchers detected metabolic activity in intact, nongerminating endospores, challenging the assumption that dormant spores are metabolically inert until germination begins.

questions.explanation:
Choice D explicitly sets the evidence against the scientific assumption the student wants to undermine. The spores had not germinated, yet the researchers detected incorporation of labeled carbon into ATP-related compounds, evidence of metabolic activity. That finding conflicts directly with the model that dormant spores are entirely metabolically inert.
Choice A explains why the detected activity does not necessarily indicate germination, but it does not identify the assumption being challenged. Choice B describes the research method and sample history without explaining their significance. Choice C discusses a possible practical implication rather than using the finding to undermine the scientific model.

questions.passage: Cultivated taro populations near New Guinea contain substantially more chloroplast haplotypes than do taro populations on several remote eastern Pacific islands. One botanist hypothesizes that cultivation of taro spread outward from New Guinea through a series of migrations. According to the hypothesis, each group of settlers transported only part of the genetic diversity available in its source population, and later settlements were founded from still smaller subsets. Consequently, cultivated taro populations should generally contain fewer haplotypes the farther they are from New Guinea.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would best support the botanist’s hypothesis?

choices.A: Taro populations in Vanuatu average fewer haplotypes than those in Tonga, even though Vanuatu is closer to New Guinea than Tonga is.
choices.B: Cultivated taro populations growing on the islands of Fiji average somewhat more chloroplast haplotypes than comparable taro populations growing in Samoa, although the two island groups lie at roughly comparable distances from New Guinea.
choices.C: Taro populations on Rapa Nui average more haplotypes than those in Samoa, even though Rapa Nui is substantially farther from New Guinea.
choices.D: Taro populations in the Solomon Islands average more haplotypes than those in Tahiti, and the Solomon Islands are substantially closer to New Guinea than Tahiti is.

questions.explanation:
The hypothesis predicts a broad decrease in genetic diversity with increasing distance from New Guinea. Choice D matches that prediction: the nearer Solomon Islands have more haplotypes than the much more distant Tahiti.
Choice A shows the reverse pattern, with the nearer population having less diversity. Choice B compares populations at approximately the same distance, so the difference between them provides little evidence for a distance-based decline. Choice C also runs against the hypothesis because the farther population has more haplotypes than the nearer one.

table.caption: Deep-Sea Research Vehicles

choices.A: Nereid Mk II completed approximately 23,400 dives, whereas Pelican-6 completed approximately 5,200.
choices.B: Bathyscope One completed approximately 23,400 dives, whereas Argo Dawn completed only approximately 1,900.
choices.C: Bathyscope One completed approximately 5,200 dives in total, whereas Argo Dawn completed approximately 3,100 dives.
choices.D: Nereid Mk II completed approximately 5,200 dives, whereas Pelican-6 completed approximately 3,100.

Engineers testing protective coatings for lithium-ion battery separators wanted to know whether reducing internal short circuits would necessarily improve a cell’s retained discharge capacity. Four coating systems were applied to otherwise identical batteries, which were then cycled 300 times. A lower short-circuit percentage indicates a more effective protective coating.

The researchers concluded that <u>there was no predictable association between a coating’s effectiveness at suppressing short circuits and the battery’s retained capacity</u>, as evidenced by the fact that ______

graph.caption: Battery Performance after 300 Charge Cycles

questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the underlined conclusion?

choices.A: the ceramic film produced a lower short-circuit rate than the oxide layer and was also associated with greater retained capacity.
choices.B: the polymer-brush and fluoropolymer coatings produced the two lowest short-circuit percentages, yet they were associated with the highest and lowest retained capacities, respectively.
choices.C: the oxide layer produced the greatest short-circuit percentage, whereas the polymer-brush coating produced the greatest retained capacity.
choices.D: the polymer-brush coating was associated with 94% retained capacity and only 3% short-circuited cells, outperforming the ceramic film on both of the measures.

questions.explanation:
B is correct. If more effective suppression of short circuits predictably produced greater retained capacity, the treatments with the lowest short-circuit rates should also tend to have the highest retained capacities. Instead, the two most effective coatings by short-circuit rate produce opposite extremes in capacity: the polymer brush has the highest retained capacity at 94%, while the nearly equally effective fluoropolymer film has the lowest at 56%. That contrast directly supports the conclusion that no predictable relationship exists.
A describes results consistent with a relationship in which better short-circuit suppression corresponds with greater capacity, so it does not support the claim of unpredictability. C compares two different extreme values but does not show why short-circuit effectiveness fails to predict capacity as clearly as B does. D also presents a result consistent with a positive relationship between the two measures rather than evidence against such a relationship.

questions.passage: In a study of how screen contrast affects proofreading efficiency, participants spent forty minutes on one day identifying typographical errors in passages displayed with relatively low contrast. The following day, the same participants performed an equivalent task using a substantially higher-contrast display. Researchers predicted that the higher contrast would allow participants to identify errors more rapidly. However, lingering visual fatigue from the first session may have impaired participants’ performance during the second session. Thus, _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: differences between the two sessions may have resulted primarily from participants becoming familiar with the proofreading task.
choices.B: researchers may have been unable to determine how many errors participants identified during the second session.
choices.C: the second session’s results may underestimate the extent to which higher contrast improves proofreading efficiency.
choices.D: participants likely preferred the higher-contrast display even if it did not improve their proofreading performance.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is C. Researchers expected higher contrast to improve performance, but the second session may have been depressed by fatigue carried over from the first session. If participants performed less well on the second day than they otherwise would have, the observed benefit of higher contrast would appear smaller than its true benefit. The experiment could therefore underestimate the effect of higher contrast.
A is incorrect because the passage identifies visual fatigue, not increased task familiarity, as the potential confounding factor. B is incorrect because nothing suggests that the researchers were unable to measure performance accurately. D is incorrect because the passage concerns proofreading efficiency, not participants’ subjective preferences.

questions.passage: Subglacial sediments contain diverse microorganisms, including the archaeon Nitrosopumilus glacialis and several species of heterotrophic bacteria, such as Polaromonas vacuolata. Researchers began with sediment samples whose microbial compositions were initially very similar, then subjected the samples to different oxygen concentrations and pressures. Both variables influenced microbial growth. However, when total archaeal growth increased, most of that increase was attributable specifically to N. glacialis, whereas changes in bacterial growth were distributed across numerous bacterial species.

table.caption: Growth Rates of Archaeal Communities in Three Subglacial Sediment Samples

questions.question: Taken together, the text and table best support which statement about the sediment samples at the conclusion of the experiment?

choices.A: The sample exposed to 16% oxygen and 2.5 atm necessarily contained a greater total proportion of archaea than of bacteria.
choices.B: The sample exposed to 8% oxygen and 1.0 atm contained a lower proportion of N. glacialis within its archaeal community than the sample exposed to 16% oxygen and 2.5 atm did.
choices.C: The sample exposed to 16% oxygen and 2.5 atm contained a greater proportion of N. glacialis than of P. vacuolata.
choices.D: The sample exposed to an oxygen concentration of 8% and a pressure of 1.0 atm contained a lower proportion of P. vacuolata than the sample exposed to 16% oxygen and 2.5 atm did.

questions.explanation:
The samples began with very similar microbial compositions. The table shows that archaeal growth was lowest under 8% oxygen and 1.0 atm and highest under 16% oxygen and 2.5 atm. The passage further states that increases in total archaeal growth were driven primarily by N. glacialis. It therefore follows that the condition producing much greater archaeal growth would also tend to produce a larger representation of N. glacialis within the archaeal community. Thus, the low-growth sample would contain a lower proportion of that archaeon than the high-growth sample, making B correct.
Choice A cannot be established because no data compare the total quantities of archaea and bacteria. Choice C also compares N. glacialis directly with a bacterial species, but neither the table nor the passage provides enough information to establish which species ultimately made up the larger proportion of the entire microbial community. Choice D is unsupported because the passage says bacterial growth changes were spread across many bacterial species; it does not single out P. vacuolata as varying systematically with the archaeal growth pattern.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from William Shakespeare’s play Measure for Measure, first performed around 1604. Duke Vincentio is reflecting on the consequences of having enforced Vienna’s laws too leniently.
DUKE:
For years I let the statutes sleep, preferring
Counsel to punishment when both were mine.
Habit has taught the insolent that restraint
Is but a threat rehearsed and never acted.
I know now what such lenity has purchased:
Not gratitude, but license to despise
The hand that would not govern. What I spared
Must now be ruled with firmer judgment.
questions.question: Which statement best describes how the Duke presents himself in the text?

choices.A: He admits that his reluctance to exercise authority has weakened respect for it and concludes that he must govern more forcefully.
choices.B: He argues that his measured treatment of offenders was fundamentally correct, even though others have mistaken restraint for weakness.
choices.C: He claims that he has judged wrongdoing impartially but recognizes that repeated punishment has nevertheless caused citizens to distrust him.
choices.D: He concedes that his administration has been ineffective, yet he attributes that failure primarily to the deliberate insolence of those subject to the law.

questions.explanation:
Choice A captures both parts of the Duke’s reasoning. He acknowledges that his own “lenity” and unwillingness to enforce the laws have taught people to disregard his authority, and he then states that what he previously spared “must now be ruled with firmer judgment.” He therefore sees his former tolerance as a cause of diminished respect and resolves to become more forceful.
Choice B contradicts the passage because the Duke does not defend his previous leniency; he identifies it as the source of the problem. Choice C reverses the situation: the Duke says he punished too little, not that excessive punishment caused distrust. Choice D contains part of the passage’s idea—the citizens have become insolent—but wrongly makes their behavior the primary cause. The Duke instead places responsibility on his own failure to enforce the law.

questions.passage: Hydrologists estimate snow-water equivalent (SWE), the amount of liquid water contained in a snowpack, using instruments such as snow pillows installed at monitoring stations. Because such stations are sparse in many high-elevation regions, researchers also estimate SWE remotely from satellite measurements of microwave radiation emitted and scattered by snow. The relationship between microwave signals and SWE varies with forest cover, snow-grain size, and liquid-water content, so the satellite measurement is not a direct substitute for an on-site reading. Nevertheless, studies have found that properly calibrated microwave observations often correspond closely with ground-based SWE measurements.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain why variation in forest cover prevents satellite measurements from providing meaningful estimates of mountain snowpack
choices.B: To compare two instruments that hydrologists commonly install at monitoring stations to determine which produces more reliable SWE measurements
choices.C: To describe a remotely obtained proxy for SWE that can partly address the limited geographic coverage of ground-based monitoring
choices.D: To identify systematic flaws in snow-pillow measurements that have led researchers to replace ground stations with satellite observations

questions.explanation:
Choice C accurately captures the passage as a whole. The text first establishes a limitation of the standard ground-based method: monitoring stations are sparse. It then introduces satellite microwave observations as an indirect way to estimate SWE across areas where ground measurements may be unavailable, while also acknowledging limitations in the relationship between the proxy and the quantity being measured.
Choice A exaggerates one complication into a complete failure; the text explicitly states that calibrated satellite observations often correspond well with ground measurements. Choice B is incorrect because the passage does not compare two ground instruments. Choice D misrepresents the motivation for the remote method: the problem described is insufficient geographic coverage, not systematic measurement error in snow pillows, and the text never says satellites have replaced ground stations.

- Because he cannot visually study a model while working, he learns the contours of many subjects through touch.
- He then relies on tactile and spatial memory as he shapes figures in clay.
- Rather than concealing every mark made during modeling, Naranjo sometimes allows fingerprints and hand-worked textures to remain visible in finished pieces.
- One sculpture depicts a dancer leaning forward with both arms extended.

questions.question: The student wants to describe Naranjo’s artistic process. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.D: Naranjo, a Santa Clara Pueblo sculptor who lost his sight as a young adult, has produced sculptures depicting both human figures and animals.

Choice B merely identifies subjects he has depicted. Choice D provides biographical information and describes the subjects of his work but does not explain how he creates the sculptures.

questions.passage: Automated analysis of enormous collections of whale vocalizations allows bioacousticians to detect migration-scale patterns that would be difficult to recognize by examining recordings individually, but statistical aggregation can _____ the distinctive phrasing of particular animals. Close spectrographic study of single call sequences, by contrast, can reveal subtle variations that population-level summaries leave invisible.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: ratify
choices.B: elide
choices.C: magnify
choices.D: prefigure

questions.explanation:
Choice B, “elide,” means to omit, suppress, or pass over something. The passage contrasts broad statistical aggregation with close examination of individual calls. Because aggregation can make individual variations disappear from view, “elide” precisely expresses the intended idea.
Choice A, “ratify,” means to formally approve or confirm, which does not fit the relationship between statistical analysis and individual vocal patterns. Choice C, “magnify,” means to make something more prominent or noticeable, the opposite of what the next sentence suggests. Choice D, “prefigure,” means to foreshadow or anticipate something that comes later; nothing in the passage concerns prediction or foreshadowing.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Helena Marlowe’s 1907 play The Crown’s Measure. Governor Vale is addressing councilors who have repeatedly ignored his directives.
VALE:
I called my silence patience; you called it leave.
Because my hand lay quiet on the seal,
You thought the seal itself had lost its force.
Enough. I have worn courtesy so long
That even insolence mistakes it for surrender.
From this hour I will speak in my own voice,
And those who prized the softness of restraint
May learn what weight restraint was holding back.
questions.question: Which statement best describes how Vale presents himself in the text?

choices.A: He argues that his earlier restraint has been mistaken for weakness and resolves to reveal a more forceful aspect of his character.
choices.B: He admits that his harsh treatment of the councilors caused their defiance and promises to govern with greater patience.
choices.C: He maintains that courtesy is his most authentic trait and insists that he will preserve it even if the councilors continue to disregard him.
choices.D: He claims that the councilors have obeyed him too readily and therefore urges them to challenge his authority more openly.

choiceExplanations.A: Vale says that his “silence” and “courtesy” have been interpreted as permission, surrender, or lack of force. He then declares that he will now “speak in my own voice” and reveal the “weight” that restraint had concealed. Thus, A accurately captures both parts of his self-presentation: he believes his earlier restraint damaged perceptions of his authority, and he now intends to act more forcefully.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice reverses the situation; Vale does not say he has been excessively harsh.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice contradicts his decision to stop relying on the softness of restraint.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice is unsupported because the councilors have been insufficiently deferential, not excessively obedient.

questions.explanation: Vale says that his “silence” and “courtesy” have been interpreted as permission, surrender, or lack of force. He then declares that he will now “speak in my own voice” and reveal the “weight” that restraint had concealed. Thus, A accurately captures both parts of his self-presentation: he believes his earlier restraint damaged perceptions of his authority, and he now intends to act more forcefully. B reverses the situation; Vale does not say he has been excessively harsh. C contradicts his decision to stop relying on the softness of restraint. D is unsupported because the councilors have been insufficiently deferential, not excessively obedient.

questions.passage: From the pallid bat to the greater mouse-eared bat, several distantly related species make long nightly trips between roosts and feeding grounds. choices.B: To describe a particular flight pattern that explains why certain species of bats use less energy during flight than all other nocturnal mammals
choices.C: To identify a behavioral similarity among several bat species that makes protecting them unusually difficult
choices.D: To present a finding about the movement behavior of certain species that could inform efforts to protect those species

choiceExplanations.C: This choice incorrectly characterizes the shared behavior as an obstacle to conservation; the text instead suggests that understanding the pattern could assist conservation.
choiceExplanations.D: The passage presents a research finding about where several bat species tend to fly during long-distance commuting and then explains a possible conservation application: the information could help determine where turbine restrictions would most effectively reduce collisions.

questions.passage: Printing workshops established in Iceland during the late nineteenth century tended to rely on comparatively modest equipment. questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choiceExplanations.D: The text explicitly narrows the possible artist to Valcárcel or Rueda while stating that available evidence does not establish which one painted the plate. Thus, scholars know that one of two illustrators was responsible but cannot identify the individual with certainty.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Bombardier beetles possess abdominal glands that store chemicals used in a defensive reaction.
When threatened, the beetles can combine the chemicals and eject a hot, irritating spray.
The spray can cause an attacking predator to release or retreat from the beetle.
The beetles do not normally use this chemical spray to capture prey.
questions.question: The student wants to explain how bombardier beetles use their chemical reaction for protection. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Bombardier beetles can eject a hot, irritating chemical spray that causes attacking predators to release them or retreat.
choices.B: Bombardier beetles store the chemicals involved in their defensive reaction in abdominal glands.
choices.C: Bombardier beetles combine chemicals immediately before producing their characteristic spray.
choices.D: Bombardier beetles generally do not rely on their chemical spray when capturing prey.

choiceExplanations.A: It directly explains both the defensive behavior and its protective effect: the beetle releases an irritating spray, and the spray can cause a predator to let go or withdraw.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not work because it explains where the chemicals are stored but not how the reaction protects the beetle. C describes part of the mechanism behind the spray but does not state how the spray affects a predator. D distinguishes defense from hunting but still does not explain the protective mechanism itself.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice describes part of the mechanism behind the spray but does not state how the spray affects a predator.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice distinguishes defense from hunting but still does not explain the protective mechanism itself.

questions.explanation: It directly explains both the defensive behavior and its protective effect: the beetle releases an irritating spray, and the spray can cause a predator to let go or withdraw.

questions.passage: H. G. Wells’s 1895 novel The Time Machine presents a discussion in which the Time Traveller argues that time should be understood as a dimension comparable in an important respect to the dimensions of space. _____
questions.question: Which quotation from The Time Machine most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “The whole surface of the earth seemed changed—melting and flowing under my eyes.”
choices.B: “I gripped the lever with both hands, and went off with a thud.”
choices.C: “The laboratory got hazy and went dark.”
choices.D: “There is no difference between Time and any of the three dimensions of Space except that our consciousness moves along it.”

choiceExplanations.A: This choice describes the appearance of Earth changing as the narrator moves through time; although related to time travel, it does not directly support the specific claim about the dimensional nature of time.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not work because it describes the operation of the time machine rather than the theoretical relationship between time and space. C describes a visual effect experienced during time travel but offers no conceptual explanation of time as a dimension. D describes the appearance of Earth changing as the narrator moves through time; although related to time travel, it does not directly support the specific claim about the dimensional nature of time.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice describes a visual effect experienced during time travel but offers no conceptual explanation of time as a dimension.
choiceExplanations.D: The claim concerns the Time Traveller’s argument that time is a dimension comparable to spatial dimensions.

questions.explanation: The claim concerns the Time Traveller’s argument that time is a dimension comparable to spatial dimensions. Choice A states this idea directly by comparing Time with “the three dimensions of Space” and identifying consciousness as the relevant difference.

choices.B: painters working on major commissions before then would often have reserved natural ultramarine for particularly important passages?
choices.C: would painters working on major commissions before then have reserved natural ultramarine for particularly important passages.
choices.D: painters working on major commissions before then would often have reserved natural ultramarine for particularly important passages.

choiceExplanations.A: This choice does not work because it uses inverted question word order (“would painters ... have reserved”) and ends with a question mark, even though the introductory phrase sets up a statement. B uses the correct declarative word order but incorrectly ends the sentence with a question mark. C uses interrogative word order but ends with a period; changing the punctuation does not make the inverted structure appropriate for the declarative sentence.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice uses the correct declarative word order but incorrectly ends the sentence with a question mark.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice uses interrogative word order but ends with a period; changing the punctuation does not make the inverted structure appropriate for the declarative sentence.
choiceExplanations.D: The introductory phrase “According to conservation historians,” is followed by a declarative statement. Therefore, the sentence requires normal subject-verb order: “painters ... would often have reserved...” Since it is a statement rather than a question, it must end with a period.
