questions.passage: In a 1911 paper interpreting the results of gold-foil experiments, physicist Ernest Rutherford proposed that nearly all of an atom’s positive charge was concentrated in a minute central region called the _____ interpretation fundamentally altered prevailing models of atomic structure.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: nucleus, Rutherford’s
choices.B: nucleus Rutherford’s
choices.C: nucleus and Rutherford’s
choices.D: nucleus. Rutherford’s

choiceExplanations.A: This choice creates a comma splice because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice provides no punctuation at all between the two independent clauses, producing a run-on sentence.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice uses “and,” but without the comma normally needed before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses; moreover, its construction awkwardly makes “Rutherford’s interpretation” appear to continue the object of “called.” Only C establishes a clear sentence boundary.
choiceExplanations.D: The text contains two independent clauses: “physicist Ernest Rutherford proposed that nearly all of an atom’s positive charge was concentrated in a minute central region called the nucleus” and “Rutherford’s interpretation fundamentally altered prevailing models of atomic structure.” A period correctly separates those two complete thoughts.

questions.explanation:
The text contains two independent clauses: “physicist Ernest Rutherford proposed that nearly all of an atom’s positive charge was concentrated in a minute central region called the nucleus” and “Rutherford’s interpretation fundamentally altered prevailing models of atomic structure.” A period correctly separates those two complete thoughts.
Choice A creates a comma splice because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma. Choice B provides no punctuation at all between the two independent clauses, producing a run-on sentence. Choice D uses “and,” but without the comma normally needed before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses; moreover, its construction awkwardly makes “Rutherford’s interpretation” appear to continue the object of “called.” Only C establishes a clear sentence boundary.

questions.passage: Although the Pratt truss was widely adopted for railroad bridges during the nineteenth century, it receives relatively little attention in popular histories of structural engineering, a literature often centered on a handful of monumental suspension-bridge _____ that narrow narrative, historian Celeste Navarro has documented how standardized truss designs transformed regional freight networks.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: projects, and reassessing
choices.B: projects, reassessing
choices.C: projects reassessing
choices.D: projects. Reassessing

choiceExplanations.A: This choice does not solve the problem: the conjunction “and” cannot appropriately attach the participial phrase “reassessing that narrow narrative” to the preceding noun phrase while also introducing the new subject “historian Celeste Navarro.”
choiceExplanations.B: This choice incorrectly joins the complete first sentence to a second independent clause with only a comma.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice supplies no boundary at all and also momentarily suggests that the “projects” themselves are “reassessing” something.
choiceExplanations.D: The first sentence forms a complete thought ending with “suspension-bridge projects.” The next sentence begins with the introductory participial phrase “Reassessing that narrow narrative,” which appropriately modifies the subject “historian Celeste Navarro.” A period is therefore needed before “Reassessing.”

questions.explanation: The first sentence forms a complete thought ending with “suspension-bridge projects.” The next sentence begins with the introductory participial phrase “Reassessing that narrow narrative,” which appropriately modifies the subject “historian Celeste Navarro.” A period is therefore needed before “Reassessing.”

questions.passage: Crystalline diamond transmits heat considerably more efficiently than ordinary window glass _____ phonon scattering, the process by which lattice vibrations are disrupted by defects or boundaries, helps determine how readily thermal energy moves through a solid.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: does. Phonon scattering,
choices.B: does. Phonon scattering—which is
choices.C: does. Phonon scattering is
choices.D: does, phonon scattering,

choiceExplanations.A: “Crystalline diamond transmits heat considerably more efficiently than ordinary window glass does” is a complete sentence. The next sentence has “phonon scattering” as its subject and “helps determine” as its main verb. The phrase “the process by which lattice vibrations are disrupted by defects or boundaries” is a nonessential appositive explaining what phonon scattering is, so it is correctly enclosed by commas.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice begins a parenthetical construction with a dash but never closes it before the main verb “helps.” Choice C creates competing main predicates: “Phonon scattering is the process...” and “helps determine....” Because “is” makes the intervening material part of the main clause rather than an appositive, the sentence cannot grammatically proceed to “helps determine.” Only D produces two complete, correctly structured sentences.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice begins a parenthetical construction with a dash but never closes it before the main verb “helps.” Choice C creates competing main predicates: “Phonon scattering is the process...” and “helps determine....” Because “is” makes the intervening material part of the main clause rather than an appositive, the sentence cannot grammatically proceed to “helps determine.” Only D produces two complete, correctly structured sentences.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice uses only a comma to join two independent clauses, creating a comma splice.

questions.explanation:
“Crystalline diamond transmits heat considerably more efficiently than ordinary window glass does” is a complete sentence. The next sentence has “phonon scattering” as its subject and “helps determine” as its main verb. The phrase “the process by which lattice vibrations are disrupted by defects or boundaries” is a nonessential appositive explaining what phonon scattering is, so it is correctly enclosed by commas.
Choice A uses only a comma to join two independent clauses, creating a comma splice. Choice B begins a parenthetical construction with a dash but never closes it before the main verb “helps.” Choice C creates competing main predicates: “Phonon scattering is the process...” and “helps determine....” Because “is” makes the intervening material part of the main clause rather than an appositive, the sentence cannot grammatically proceed to “helps determine.” Only D produces two complete, correctly structured sentences.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
John James Audubon’s The Birds of America was published in installments between 1827 and 1838.
The completed work contains 435 hand-colored plates depicting birds.
The plates were printed on sheets measuring approximately 39 by 26 inches.
This unusually large page size is known as “double-elephant folio.”
The large format allowed Audubon to portray many species at or near life size.
questions.question: The student wants to describe the physical format of The Birds of America. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Audubon chose oversize pages to portray many birds near life size.
choices.B: Nineteenth-century natural-history publications were commonly produced on double-elephant folio sheets large enough to accommodate life-size illustrations.
choices.C: Published in installments from 1827 through 1838, The Birds of America eventually included hundreds of hand-colored depictions of birds.
choices.D: The Birds of America contains 435 hand-colored plates printed on approximately 39-by-26-inch sheets in a format known as double-elephant folio.

choiceExplanations.A: This choice focuses primarily on why Audubon chose the format rather than describing the format itself.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice makes an unsupported generalization about nineteenth-century natural-history publications; the notes establish that The Birds of America used this format, not that such a format was common across the field.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice emphasizes publication history and the contents of the work but omits the defining physical information about page dimensions and double-elephant folio size.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice works because it directly describes the work’s physical format. It identifies both the number and nature of the plates and, crucially, the approximate dimensions and name of the large folio format.

questions.explanation:
This choice works because it directly describes the work’s physical format. It identifies both the number and nature of the plates and, crucially, the approximate dimensions and name of the large folio format.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
The Svalbard Global Seed Vault opened on the Norwegian island of Spitsbergen in 2008.
The vault stores backup copies of seed samples held by gene banks around the world.
The Nordic Genetic Resource Center, known as NordGen, is one of the organizations involved in the vault’s operation.
NordGen receives incoming seed deposits and maintains records identifying the deposited material.
The Crop Trust helps support the conservation system financially.
The vault was designed to protect crop diversity from losses caused by disasters, conflict, equipment failures, and other threats.
questions.question: The student wants to provide an example of a responsibility NordGen performs in connection with the Svalbard Global Seed Vault. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Because disasters and equipment failures can threaten gene-bank collections, backup seed samples are stored at Svalbard.
choices.B: Opened in 2008 on Spitsbergen, the Svalbard Global Seed Vault preserves backup samples from gene banks around the world.
choices.C: NordGen and the Crop Trust both contribute to an international system intended to reduce the risk that crop diversity will be permanently lost.
choices.D: NordGen receives seed deposits sent to the Svalbard Global Seed Vault and maintains records identifying the stored material.

choiceExplanations.A: This choice explains the purpose of storing backup seeds but says nothing about NordGen’s role.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice describes the Seed Vault itself rather than a responsibility performed by NordGen.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice mentions NordGen but gives only a broad statement about participation in the conservation system; it does not identify a particular responsibility that NordGen carries out.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice works because it provides a concrete example of a task specifically attributed to NordGen: receiving incoming deposits and maintaining information about them. It therefore directly fulfills the student’s goal of identifying one of NordGen’s responsibilities.

This choice works because it provides a concrete example of a task specifically attributed to NordGen: receiving incoming deposits and maintaining information about them. It therefore directly fulfills the student’s goal of identifying one of NordGen’s responsibilities.

questions.passage: A shift from centralized workshop production to more dispersed household manufacture in the Koru Valley between approximately 900 and 600 BCE can be inferred from ceramic remains in settlements dating to different periods. Vessels from layers dating to about 900 BCE are generally <u>highly standardized in diameter, stamped with one of only three workshop seals, and made from clay originating near the valley’s fortified administrative center</u>. Pottery from layers younger than about 650 BCE, however, <u>varies much more widely in size, bears dozens of distinct local marks, and incorporates clay from several separate tributary valleys</u>.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the two underlined portions in the text as a whole?

choices.A: They describe differing characteristics of earlier and later pottery that together support the claim that production became less centralized and more locally varied over time.
choices.B: They provide evidence from two periods that supports the claim that ceramic production remained concentrated near the Koru Valley’s administrative center.
choices.C: They distinguish pottery from separate geographical regions in order to suggest that different communities simultaneously adopted incompatible manufacturing traditions.
choices.D: They identify contrasting features of pottery assemblages that together suggest that the overall amount of ceramic production declined steadily over the course of the period discussed.

choiceExplanations.A: The first underlined portion describes uniformity and centralization: standardized sizes, only three workshop seals, and clay from near the administrative center. The second describes greater variation and geographic dispersion: wider differences in size, many local marks, and clay from multiple valleys. Taken together, those contrasts support the passage’s opening claim that production shifted from centralized workshops toward more dispersed local manufacture.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice contradicts the younger evidence, which points away from continued concentration near the administrative center.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice incorrectly treats the evidence primarily as a simultaneous geographical comparison; the passage explicitly contrasts assemblages from different periods to establish change over time.
choiceExplanations.D: Choice

questions.explanation: The first underlined portion describes uniformity and centralization: standardized sizes, only three workshop seals, and clay from near the administrative center. The second describes greater variation and geographic dispersion: wider differences in size, many local marks, and clay from multiple valleys. Taken together, those contrasts support the passage’s opening claim that production shifted from centralized workshops toward more dispersed local manufacture.

The Niagara Movement was a civil rights organization formed in 1905 by Black activists demanding full political and civil equality in the United States.

Twenty-nine activists attended an organizational meeting in July 1905 at Fort Erie, Ontario, near Niagara Falls.

choices.B: By 1909, several people associated with the Niagara Movement had helped establish the NAACP, extending the struggle for civil rights through a new organization.
choices.C: Political equality rarely develops without sustained disagreement, organization, and pressure from people dissatisfied with existing institutions.

questions.passage: The following text is from Walt Whitman’s 1855 poem Song of Myself. The speaker acknowledges that apparently incompatible qualities or beliefs can coexist within a single person, suggesting that such inconsistency does not diminish the complexity of the self. _____
questions.question: Which quotation from Song of Myself most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “I celebrate myself, and sing myself, / And what I assume you shall assume”
choices.B: “I too am not a bit tamed, I too am untranslatable, / I sound my barbaric yawp over the roofs of the world.”
choices.C: “I loafe and invite my soul, / I lean and loafe at my ease observing a spear of summer grass.”
choices.D: “Do I contradict myself? / Very well then I contradict myself, / (I am large, I contain multitudes.)”

choiceExplanations.A: This choice emphasizes identification between the speaker and others, not the coexistence of contradictory qualities within the speaker.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice emphasizes the speaker’s untamed and difficult-to-define nature, which could suggest individuality, but it does not directly address the acceptance of contradiction as B does.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice depicts contemplation and leisure but says nothing about inconsistency or complexity of identity.
choiceExplanations.D: The claim concerns the speaker’s acceptance of internal inconsistency as part of a complex identity. In B, the speaker explicitly acknowledges that he may “contradict” himself and immediately explains that contradiction by saying he “contain[s] multitudes.” The quotation therefore directly supports both parts of the claim: inconsistency exists, and that inconsistency reflects expansiveness rather than deficiency.

questions.explanation:
The claim concerns the speaker’s acceptance of internal inconsistency as part of a complex identity. In B, the speaker explicitly acknowledges that he may “contradict” himself and immediately explains that contradiction by saying he “contain[s] multitudes.” The quotation therefore directly supports both parts of the claim: inconsistency exists, and that inconsistency reflects expansiveness rather than deficiency.
A emphasizes identification between the speaker and others, not the coexistence of contradictory qualities within the speaker. C depicts contemplation and leisure but says nothing about inconsistency or complexity of identity. D emphasizes the speaker’s untamed and difficult-to-define nature, which could suggest individuality, but it does not directly address the acceptance of contradiction as B does.

questions.passage:

Beyond the clustered roofs, the harbor widened toward a chain of low islands whose dark spruce trees seemed almost level with the sea. At high tide, the water reached the weathered pilings beneath the wharves; when it withdrew, broad beds of rockweed shone between exposed stones. The afternoon wind carried salt through the open windows, while fishing boats, diminished by distance, moved slowly across the pale outer bay.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To establish the physical character and atmosphere of a coastal setting
choices.B: To introduce a disagreement between the narrator and the fishing community
choices.C: To explain an economic difficulty confronting the settlement’s residents
choices.D: To characterize the narrator through a decision the narrator is preparing to make

choiceExplanations.A: Nearly every detail concerns the surrounding environment: the harbor, islands, spruce trees, tides, wharves, rockweed, salt air, and distant fishing boats. Together, these details create a vivid impression of the coastal landscape and its atmosphere.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not work because no disagreement or conflict appears.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not work because the text does not discuss income, trade, scarcity, or any other economic problem.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice does not work because although the narrator observes the setting, the passage does not reveal a decision, plan, or significant personality trait. Its focus is overwhelmingly on place rather than plot or characterization.

questions.explanation: Nearly every detail concerns the surrounding environment: the harbor, islands, spruce trees, tides, wharves, rockweed, salt air, and distant fishing boats. Together, these details create a vivid impression of the coastal landscape and its atmosphere.

questions.passage: Engineers investigating lower-carbon paving materials tested whether finely crushed basalt could replace part of the mineral filler in a composite without substantially reducing its flexural strength. Four mixtures were prepared: a baseline mixture with no basalt substitution and mixtures containing 8%, 16%, or 32% basalt. Flexural strength was measured after 10 and 30 days of curing. Based on the results, the researchers recommended using basalt substitutions of approximately 8% when maintaining structural strength is a priority.
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses the data shown to support the researchers’ recommendation?

choices.A: The 8% basalt mixture never exceeded the flexural strength of the baseline mixture at either measurement point.
choices.B: The flexural strength of the 8% basalt mixture changed very little between day 10 and day 30, whereas the strengths of the 16% and 32% mixtures increased over the same interval.
choices.C: The 8% basalt mixture was stronger than the baseline mixture on day 10, but by day 30 its strength had declined while that of the baseline mixture had increased.
choices.D: The 8% basalt mixture equaled or exceeded the baseline mixture in flexural strength on both measurement days, whereas the 16% and 32% mixtures remained below the baseline on both days.

choiceExplanations.A: This choice is false because the 8% mixture exceeds the baseline on day 10.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice accurately notices that the 8% value changes little, but stability alone does not establish that its strength remains comparable to the baseline; C provides the more relevant comparison.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not work because the 8% mixture does not decline between the two measurements; it rises slightly.
choiceExplanations.D: On day 10, the 8% mixture has a flexural strength of about 44 MPa, compared with about 42 MPa for the baseline. On day 30, the 8% mixture is about 45 MPa, essentially equal to the baseline’s 45 MPa. By contrast, both the 16% and 32% mixtures remain substantially weaker than the baseline at both measurements. These data directly support recommending the smaller substitution level when strength must be preserved.

questions.explanation:
On day 10, the 8% mixture has a flexural strength of about 44 MPa, compared with about 42 MPa for the baseline. On day 30, the 8% mixture is about 45 MPa, essentially equal to the baseline’s 45 MPa. By contrast, both the 16% and 32% mixtures remain substantially weaker than the baseline at both measurements. These data directly support recommending the smaller substitution level when strength must be preserved.
A is false because the 8% mixture exceeds the baseline on day 10. B accurately notices that the 8% value changes little, but stability alone does not establish that its strength remains comparable to the baseline; C provides the more relevant comparison.

questions.passage: Producing exceptionally large scholarly reference books requires publishers to balance legibility, binding durability, and manufacturing cost. One recent botanical compendium contains approximately 460,800 words across 1,280 pages, while a comparative atlas of marine invertebrates contains about 604,800 words in a 960-page edition. This suggests that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the marine-invertebrate atlas contains more words per page than the botanical compendium does.
choices.B: the botanical compendium was probably less expensive to manufacture than the marine-invertebrate atlas.
choices.C: the botanical compendium likely contained fewer words before it was edited for publication.
choices.D: readers would require approximately the same amount of time to finish the two works.

choiceExplanations.A: The botanical compendium averages 460,8001,280=360 words per page. The marine-invertebrate atlas averages 604,800960=630 words per page. Therefore, the atlas contains substantially more words per page.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice is unsupported because page and word counts alone do not establish manufacturing costs; paper quality, illustrations, binding, print run, and other factors could matter.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice cannot be inferred because no information is given about earlier drafts.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice is also unsupported: reading time depends on far more than page count, and the works differ considerably in total word count.

questions.explanation:

questions.passage: In 2021, historian Nadia Farouk published Beyond the Last Meridian, a biography of surveyor and expedition leader Elias Venn. Yet Farouk organizes those episodes backward: the book opens with Venn’s final expedition and gradually retreats toward his adolescence. Reviewing the biography, critic Hana Okafor wrote that this arrangement “turns causation into an afterthought; the reader repeatedly encounters consequences before being allowed to understand their origins.”
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It contrasts two biographies of the same historical figure before explaining why one biography received stronger reviews.
choices.B: It introduces the subject of a biography, summarizes major events from that person’s life, and argues that the biography omits important causes of those events.

choices.D: It identifies a biography, notes several events that the biography covers, and then presents a critic’s negative assessment of one aspect of the biography’s organization.

choiceExplanations.A: Choice

choiceExplanations.C: This choice correctly recognizes that the organization is unconventional but incorrectly claims that the passage explains why Farouk chose it and then defends the decision. Neither occurs.
choiceExplanations.D: The passage first identifies Farouk’s biography of Elias Venn. It then lists several episodes from Venn’s life that the biography covers. questions.passage: In competitive orchid breeding, exhibition labels often include lineage diagrams, provenance notes, and hand-rendered sketches that reflect growers’ priorities and classification habits. ____ many breeders spend considerable time preparing these displays, treating them not merely as identification cards but as integral parts of how a specimen is presented.

choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: Finally,

choiceExplanations.A: This choice. Indeed, is correct. The second sentence reinforces the first sentence’s suggestion that exhibition labels are meaningful expressions of a breeder’s priorities. Saying that breeders devote substantial time to the displays and regard them as integral to presenting a specimen provides further evidence for that idea, so “Indeed” appropriately signals emphasis and confirmation.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not work because “Nevertheless” signals a contrast, but the second sentence supports rather than contradicts the first.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not work because “Consequently” would indicate that the time spent preparing labels is a result of the specific features listed in the first sentence; the relationship is primarily one of reinforcement, not cause and effect.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice does not work because “Finally” signals the last step in a sequence, and no sequence of steps has been established.

questions.explanation: This choice. Indeed, is correct. The second sentence reinforces the first sentence’s suggestion that exhibition labels are meaningful expressions of a breeder’s priorities. Saying that breeders devote substantial time to the displays and regard them as integral to presenting a specimen provides further evidence for that idea, so “Indeed” appropriately signals emphasis and confirmation.

questions.passage: During the 1970s, fluorescent yellow tennis balls increasingly displaced white ones in televised tournaments. choices.C: leading

choiceExplanations.A: This choice does not work because “having led” is a participial construction and cannot serve as the finite main verb here.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not work because “which led” would create another subordinate relative clause and leave the sentence without a main verb.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not work because “leading” is also a participle rather than the required finite verb.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice. led is correct. The subject of the sentence is “The sport’s widespread adoption of the brighter color.” Although the intervening relative clause beginning with “which” contains its own verb, the main clause still requires a finite verb. “Led” supplies that verb: “The sport’s widespread adoption . . . led to television producers favoring it.”

The subject of the sentence is “The sport’s widespread adoption of the brighter color.” Although the intervening relative clause beginning with “which” contains its own verb, the main clause still requires a finite verb. “Led” supplies that verb: “The sport’s widespread adoption . . . led to television producers favoring it.”

For years my notebooks had been crowded with calculations that seemed to terminate in other calculations: predicted currents, sediment estimates, revisions to earlier estimates. On the marsh, however, each measurement governed some tangible decision—where a channel would be reopened, how high a barrier would stand, whether young cordgrass would survive the next spring tide. After so much work that had existed chiefly on paper, my figures had acquired a practical end.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does the word “end” most nearly mean?

choices.B: consequence
choices.C: boundary
choices.D: conclusion

choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not work because end can mean a physical or temporal boundary, but nothing in the passage concerns the boundary of the calculations.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice does not work because end can also mean termination, but the calculations have not merely stopped; they have gained a practical purpose.

questions.explanation: This choice. objective is correct. The passage contrasts calculations that previously seemed abstract with calculations that now serve a concrete practical purpose. In the phrase “a practical end,” end therefore means an aim, purpose, or objective.

A historical exhibition never merely accumulates surviving objects. questions.passage: A 2022 paper by Priya Nandakumar and colleagues introduced nanoscale infrared mapping (NIM), a method that simultaneously images microscopic structures and identifies chemical bonds within them. Researchers led by Mateo Ruiz later combined NIM with expansion microscopy, in which a swellable polymer physically enlarges a prepared specimen. The resulting technique, expansion-assisted nanoscale infrared mapping (eNIM), preserves NIM’s chemical-identification capabilities while reducing the spatial-resolution limitation by increasing the physical separation between neighboring structures.

choiceExplanations.B: This choice incorrectly says the two techniques are merely compared as independent alternatives; the passage instead explains that they are combined.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice incorrectly claims the same researchers developed both the original and newer techniques.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice reverses the passage’s emphasis: the text does not present expansion microscopy as chemically inadequate or propose combining it with ordinary light microscopy.

questions.passage: Landscape architect Mireya Solano’s Tide Court allows seawater to enter a public plaza through concealed channels, periodically transforming dry stone terraces into shallow reflective pools. Engineer-artist Anton Bell’s Waterworks Pavilion, by contrast, places its valves, pipes, gauges, and filtration tanks in full view; visitors can watch water moving through the structure while standing inside it. choiceExplanations.B: This choice is unsupported because the passage says nothing about either creator celebrating or condemning artificiality.

D mischaracterizes Solano’s purpose; the text does not say she tries to imitate untouched nature.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice mischaracterizes Solano’s purpose; the text does not say she tries to imitate untouched nature.

questions.passage: Many premium agricultural products carry machine-readable seals whose microscopic patterns function as authenticity cues for automated customs scanners. Once calibrated, the scanners route packages displaying registered patterns through ordinary processing while diverting unrecognized ones for additional inspection. The researchers therefore concluded that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the uncertified packages likely exploit a deceptive strategy in which products lacking certification reduce scrutiny by imitating an authenticity cue associated with certified goods.
choices.B: certified and uncertified saffron producers likely participate in a cooperative signaling system in which both of the groups benefit from displaying nearly identical seals.
choices.C: microscopic authentication seals are probably used more widely on fraudulent agricultural products than previous customs investigations have suggested.
choices.D: automated authentication is probably ineffective because customs scanners can readily distinguish registered seals from visually similar imitations.

choiceExplanations.A: This choice most directly follows from the evidence. The uncertified packages contain substitute material yet display patterns closely resembling the registered patterns that scanners use as evidence of authenticity. That is a deceptive imitation strategy: an unverified product gains an advantage by resembling a verified one. A contradicts the proposed benefit of the imitation and is not supported by any evidence that scanners reliably distinguish the counterfeit patterns.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice incorrectly treats the relationship as cooperative; the uncertified sellers are exploiting the signal rather than jointly benefiting from a legitimate shared certification system.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice makes an unsupported claim about how widespread such seals are across fraudulent products generally; the investigation concerns only the shipments examined.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice contradicts the proposed benefit of the imitation and is not supported by any evidence that scanners reliably distinguish the counterfeit patterns.

questions.passage: In a 2024 survey of Bronze Age settlements in the eastern Mediterranean, archaeologist Neha Qureshi classified forty-six sites as fortified centers partly on the basis of perimeter walls at least 2.5 meters thick—for instance, Tell Aram, whose surviving wall averages 2.9 meters. _____ archaeologist Tomás Elian argues that a site should be classified as fortified only when evidence such as controlled gateways, guard chambers, or weapon storage indicates deliberate defensive planning.

choices.B: Questioning whether the surviving measurements at Tell Aram are accurate,

choices.D: Providing an additional illustration of the same classification system,

choiceExplanations.B: This choice is too narrow: Elian is not merely disputing the accuracy of Tell Aram’s measurement but challenging the broader method.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice accurately signals the contrast between the two classification approaches. Qureshi relies partly on a quantitative threshold, wall thickness, whereas Elian argues that classification should instead depend on functional archaeological evidence of defensive planning.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice is also incorrect because Elian’s proposal is not another example of Qureshi’s system; it counters that system.

questions.passage: Repeated applications of deicing salt can cause chloride ions to penetrate reinforced-concrete bridge decks, where sufficiently high chloride concentrations may accelerate corrosion of embedded steel. Engineers generally determine internal chloride levels by drilling cores from the concrete, a procedure that is costly and mildly destructive. In a 2024 study, civil engineer Kaori Nishimura and colleagues found that chloride concentrations could also be measured in storm runoff collected from bridge surfaces. Because runoff can be sampled easily, the researchers hypothesized that runoff chloride concentration might serve as a proxy for chloride accumulation within bridge decks, reducing the need for frequent core sampling.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the hypothesis presented in the text?

choices.A: Across bridges exposed to comparable quantities of deicing salt, chloride concentrations in runoff show no reliable relationship to chloride concentrations measured in concrete cores from the same bridges.
choices.B: Runoff samples contain measurable sodium as well as chloride, whereas concrete cores can also reveal compounds unrelated to deicing salt.
choices.C: Runoff chloride concentrations are consistently about four times higher than the corresponding concentrations measured in samples taken from concrete cores, but increases and decreases in the two measurements closely track one another over time.
choices.D: Runoff can be collected repeatedly from bridge surfaces without drilling into the deck or interrupting traffic for extended periods.

choiceExplanations.A: The proposed proxy is useful only if runoff chloride levels reliably correspond to chloride levels inside the concrete.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not show that chloride measurements themselves are uninformative.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice would actually support the proxy hypothesis because a consistent proportional difference could still allow runoff measurements to predict internal chloride levels.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice strengthens the practical case for the proxy by emphasizing that runoff sampling is easier and less disruptive than coring.

questions.explanation: The proposed proxy is useful only if runoff chloride levels reliably correspond to chloride levels inside the concrete. B directly undermines that necessary relationship: if the two measurements do not correlate even under comparable exposure conditions, runoff concentration would not reliably indicate internal accumulation. A does not show that chloride measurements themselves are uninformative. C would actually support the proxy hypothesis because a consistent proportional difference could still allow runoff measurements to predict internal chloride levels. D strengthens the practical case for the proxy by emphasizing that runoff sampling is easier and less disruptive than coring.

questions.passage: A 2024 study by epigrapher Ana Torres and colleagues examined hundreds of notched wooden accounting tablets recovered from medieval Baltic trading settlements. Torres’s team proposed that some paired symbols on the tablets exhibit a rudimentary form of compositionality: the symbols appear in recurring combinations whose meanings depend not merely on which symbols are present but also on the order in which they occur. The researchers based this claim on statistical patterns in the tablets as well as on the commercial contexts associated with individual inscriptions.

questions.passage: The geographic distribution of plants mentioned in centuries-old farming proverbs often ____ the historical ranges of the species themselves, perhaps because such sayings preserved practical information about where particular crops or wild plants could be found. choices.B: compensates for
choices.C: retreats from
choices.D: submits to

The passage says that traditional sayings may preserve information about where species occur, then identifies sayings about Icelandic oak forests as an exception because those sayings persisted after the relevant vegetation disappeared. This contrast indicates that, ordinarily, the locations mentioned in such sayings correspond to or coincide with the historical ranges of the plants.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not work because “compensates for” means offsets or makes up for something; a geographic distribution does not logically compensate for another distribution.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not work because “retreats from” would indicate that the two distributions move away from each other, contradicting the idea that the sayings preserve accurate location information.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice does not work because “submits to” describes yielding to authority or control and does not make logical sense for two geographic distributions.

questions.explanation: This choice. coincides with is correct. The passage says that traditional sayings may preserve information about where species occur, then identifies sayings about Icelandic oak forests as an exception because those sayings persisted after the relevant vegetation disappeared. This contrast indicates that, ordinarily, the locations mentioned in such sayings correspond to or coincide with the historical ranges of the plants.

questions.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the underlined claim in Text 1?

choiceExplanations.A: Text 2 directly challenges the idea that official recognition by itself necessarily boosts tourism. questions.passage: Medieval European bestiaries drew upon numerous earlier works describing animals, including Isidore of Seville’s seventh-century Etymologiae and the much older Greek Physiologus. questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choiceExplanations.B: The passage explicitly states that the earliest Latin versions of the Physiologus do not contain the barnacle-goose account, whereas Gerald of Wales and later bestiaries do. choiceExplanations.C: reverses the chronology: the earliest Latin Physiologus versions predate Gerald.
choiceExplanations.D: introduces an unsupported judgment about perceived scientific reliability; the passage establishes textual chronology, not medieval evaluations of accuracy.

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that the earliest Latin versions of the Physiologus do not contain the barnacle-goose account, whereas Gerald of Wales and later bestiaries do. questions.passage: Earlier ecological studies have found that animal populations occupying very small, isolated habitats often contain less genetic variation than populations distributed across broad, connected regions. questions.passage: In the 1890s, racing yachts in the Varenne Maritime League were classified according to sail area, hull length, and displacement. choiceExplanations.B: introduces crew size, a variable never discussed.

questions.passage: Two autonomous inspection robots share a manufacturing facility with forklifts that emit standardized warning tones while reversing. Model N usually travels through narrow aisles bordered by tall storage racks, which sharply restrict its field of view; Model W operates mainly across an open loading floor with few visual obstructions. Both robots can detect the forklifts’ warning tones. Engineers hypothesize that sensitivity to these auditory warnings is inversely related to how much of the surrounding workspace a robot can see while moving.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the engineers’ hypothesis?

choices.A: Model W changed course after most warning tones, whereas Model N usually continued moving at the same speed.
choices.B: Neither Model N nor Model W changed its behavior when warning tones were played without a forklift present.
choices.C: Model N consistently slowed or changed course when forklift warning tones sounded, whereas Model W showed little or no change in movement.
choices.D: Several additional robots that had been specifically designed to navigate through narrow aisles did not react to the standardized warning tones, although Model N occasionally did react to those sounds.

choiceExplanations.A: shows the opposite of the predicted pattern.
choiceExplanations.B: shows no difference between the two robots and therefore does not support an inverse relationship.
choiceExplanations.C: The hypothesis predicts an inverse relationship between visual field and responsiveness to sound. Model N has the more restricted view, so it should be more sensitive to auditory warnings; Model W has the broader view, so it should be less responsive.
choiceExplanations.D: provides mixed evidence and indicates that other visually restricted robots often failed to react, making it much weaker support than A.

questions.explanation: The hypothesis predicts an inverse relationship between visual field and responsiveness to sound. Model N has the more restricted view, so it should be more sensitive to auditory warnings; Model W has the broader view, so it should be less responsive.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Nikhil Rao’s 1904 nonfiction essay The Durable Record.
A public address belongs first to the hour in which it is delivered. Once the speaker has fallen silent, the message survives only insofar as those who heard it can remember or repeat it. A written record has another kind of existence: it may wait untouched through decades, be consulted by readers whom its author never knew, and transmit an account after both speaker and first audience have disappeared.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Public speeches are generally more persuasive than written records because listeners encounter them directly.
choices.B: Readers preserve written material more accurately when they have previously heard the same information spoken aloud.
choices.C: Speakers should prepare written copies of every address so that later readers can evaluate the speaker’s rhetorical skill.
choices.D: Written records can preserve information for substantially longer than messages transmitted only through speech.

choiceExplanations.D: The passage contrasts the fragility of spoken communication with the durability of writing.
choiceExplanations.A: reverses the passage’s emphasis and introduces persuasion, which is not discussed.
choiceExplanations.B: claims that hearing information first improves later reading accuracy, a relationship absent from the text.
choiceExplanations.C: turns the passage into advice about preserving rhetorical performances, whereas its broader point concerns the comparative permanence of written and spoken information.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts the fragility of spoken communication with the durability of writing.

questions.passage: The Meridian Cost Observatory compares prices for standardized collections of consumer goods across European economies. According to its 2025 index, a collection priced at 100 euros in Paris would cost approximately 71 euros in the EU member _____
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: state Estonia.
choices.B: state: Estonia.
choices.C: state, Estonia.
choices.D: state—Estonia.

choiceExplanations.A: “Estonia” identifies which EU member state the sentence means. Because the proper noun is essential to the meaning of the phrase “the EU member state Estonia,” no punctuation should separate “state” from “Estonia.”
choiceExplanations.B: incorrectly treats the country’s name as an explanation introduced by a colon.
choiceExplanations.C: wrongly sets “Estonia” off as nonessential information.
choiceExplanations.D: likewise separates the identifying name from the noun it specifies.

questions.explanation: “Estonia” identifies which EU member state the sentence means. Because the proper noun is essential to the meaning of the phrase “the EU member state Estonia,” no punctuation should separate “state” from “Estonia.”

questions.passage: Some virtual museum guides use synthetic voices designed to reproduce tiny features of human speech, including breaths, hesitations, and changes in pitch. Such details are intended to make interactions feel more natural, but designers have found that a voice that sounds almost human while remaining subtly unnatural can leave listeners more unsettled than _____.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: indifferent
choices.B: reassured
choices.C: vindicated
choices.D: astonished

choiceExplanations.C: “vindicated,” means shown to have been right or justified, which is unrelated to the emotional effect described.
choiceExplanations.A: “indifferent,” means unconcerned rather than comfortable.
choiceExplanations.B: The sentence contrasts two emotional effects. Designers intend humanlike speech to make interactions feel comfortable and natural, yet an imperfect imitation can instead make listeners uncomfortable. “Reassured”, meaning made calmer or more secure, supplies the precise contrasting state.
choiceExplanations.D: “astonished,” means greatly surprised and is not the natural opposite of “unsettled” in this context.

questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts two emotional effects. Designers intend humanlike speech to make interactions feel comfortable and natural, yet an imperfect imitation can instead make listeners uncomfortable. “Reassured”, meaning made calmer or more secure, supplies the precise contrasting state.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from E. Nesbit’s 1906 novel The Railway Children. Peter is trying to move through a railway cutting obscured by thick fog.
The fog had swallowed the lamps beyond the bend, but from somewhere ahead came the station porter’s whistle, faint and regular. Directing himself by the sound, Peter kept close to the wall and went cautiously toward it.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does the word “Directing” most nearly mean?

choices.A: Displaying
choices.B: Instructing
choices.C: Steering
choices.D: Withdrawing

choiceExplanations.A: means showing or presenting and does not fit the physical movement described.
choiceExplanations.B: refers to giving instructions to someone, but Peter is using the sound to navigate rather than teaching himself something.
choiceExplanations.C: Peter uses the sound of the whistle to determine which way to move through the fog. In this context, “directing himself” therefore means steering or guiding himself toward the sound.
choiceExplanations.D: means moving away or retreating, whereas Peter proceeds toward the whistle.

questions.explanation: Peter uses the sound of the whistle to determine which way to move through the fog. In this context, “directing himself” therefore means steering or guiding himself toward the sound.

questions.passage: The astronomer Henrietta Swan Leavitt’s study of Cepheid variable stars established a relationship between their pulsation periods and intrinsic brightness. Because that relationship eventually enabled astronomers to estimate distances far beyond the reach of direct parallax measurements, Leavitt’s work represented a consequential _____ observational astronomy.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: constraint on
choices.B: departure from
choices.C: dependence on
choices.D: advance in

choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because a departure from something means a divergence or abandonment, not an improvement within a field.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because a constraint on astronomy would limit what astronomers could do, whereas Leavitt’s work expanded their capabilities.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because the passage does not describe astronomy as becoming dependent on Leavitt’s research; it describes the research as an important contribution.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice. advance in is correct. The passage explains that Leavitt’s discovery gave astronomers a powerful new method for measuring enormous cosmic distances, so her work constituted significant progress, or an advance, in observational astronomy.

questions.explanation: B. advance in is correct. The passage explains that Leavitt’s discovery gave astronomers a powerful new method for measuring enormous cosmic distances, so her work constituted significant progress, or an advance, in observational astronomy.

questions.passage: Both choreographer Katherine Dunham and dancer Pearl Primus have been celebrated for _____ contributions to twentieth-century performance, particularly for incorporating extensive research on African and Caribbean dance traditions into their work.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: their
choices.B: its
choices.C: they’re
choices.D: it’s

choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because they’re is the contraction of they are, producing the ungrammatical phrase “they are contributions.” B is incorrect because its is singular and therefore cannot refer to two people.
choiceExplanations.A: This choice. their is correct. The antecedent consists of two people, Katherine Dunham and Pearl Primus, so a plural possessive pronoun is required: their contributions.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because it’s means it is or it has and is also singular.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not satisfy the evidence, wording, or grammatical requirement established by the question.

questions.explanation: C. their is correct. The antecedent consists of two people, Katherine Dunham and Pearl Primus, so a plural possessive pronoun is required: their contributions.

questions.passage: Although individual manuscripts in the Timbuktu collections may follow recognizable West African, North African, or Middle Eastern scribal conventions, some volumes incorporate features from several traditions at once. Such manuscripts therefore exhibit a distinctive _____ of calligraphic and decorative practices rather than reproducing any one tradition unchanged.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: repudiation
choices.B: synthesis
choices.C: simplification
choices.D: critique

choiceExplanations.B: This choice. synthesis is correct.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because repudiation means rejection, yet the manuscripts incorporate rather than reject the traditions.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because combining multiple traditions does not necessarily simplify them.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because a critique is an evaluation or analysis; the passage describes stylistic combination, not judgment.

questions.explanation: B. synthesis is correct.

questions.passage: The widespread adoption of electric lighting along several North Sea coastlines during the early twentieth century is thought to have _____ an abrupt decline in certain nocturnally migrating bird populations. Although habitat loss and changes in food availability also affected those populations, researchers have linked many fatal nighttime collisions directly to intense artificial illumination.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: prolonged
choices.B: followed
choices.C: precipitated
choices.D: counteracted

choiceExplanations.C: This choice. precipitated is correct. In this context, precipitated means caused or brought about suddenly. The second sentence strengthens the causal connection by explaining that artificial lighting was directly linked to many bird deaths.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because prolonged means extended in duration; the passage concerns what helped cause the decline, not what made an existing decline last longer.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because followed indicates only chronological sequence and would imply that electric lighting came after the decline.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because counteracted means reduced or opposed an effect, the opposite of what the passage indicates.

questions.explanation: C. precipitated is correct. In this context, precipitated means caused or brought about suddenly. The second sentence strengthens the causal connection by explaining that artificial lighting was directly linked to many bird deaths.

questions.passage: The essays of Virginia Woolf vary considerably in subject: some examine fiction and literary convention, whereas others consider streets, objects, or ordinary encounters. Yet across these differences, Woolf repeatedly challenges the assumption that perception is neutral or complete. _____, throughout her nonfiction she treats the observer’s point of view as something that actively shapes what can be known.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: At that time,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Indeed,

choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because Nevertheless signals a concession or contrast, whereas the two sentences are mutually reinforcing.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because Instead introduces an alternative, but the final sentence does not replace the preceding idea; it develops it.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because At that time expresses a temporal relationship that the passage does not establish.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice. Indeed, is correct. The final sentence reinforces and sharpens the preceding claim. Saying that an observer’s perspective actively shapes knowledge supports the assertion that Woolf questions the idea of neutral perception, so Indeed appropriately signals emphasis and confirmation.

questions.explanation: C. Indeed, is correct. The final sentence reinforces and sharpens the preceding claim. Saying that an observer’s perspective actively shapes knowledge supports the assertion that Woolf questions the idea of neutral perception, so Indeed appropriately signals emphasis and confirmation.

questions.passage: In a study by urban-planning researcher Sofia Lindström and colleagues, residents of Turku, Finland, and Rijeka, Croatia, were surveyed about their use of municipal libraries. Of 426 respondents in Turku, 62% reported visiting a public library at least monthly, compared with 44% of 781 respondents in Rijeka. Yet the proportion of Turku respondents living within a fifteen-minute walk of a library was substantially lower than the corresponding proportion in Rijeka. Thus, differences in geographic proximity alone cannot account for the difference in reported library use.
questions.question: The text makes which point about the difference between the percentages of Turku and Rijeka respondents who regularly use public libraries?

choices.A: It must involve some factor other than residents’ proximity to a library.
choices.B: It was probably produced by an error in the researchers’ survey procedure.
choices.C: It was calculated using demographic information gathered before the survey began.
choices.D: It was considerably greater than the researchers had predicted.

choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because the passage gives no indication that the survey results were inaccurate.
choiceExplanations.A: Turku had the higher reported rate of library use despite having a lower proportion of respondents living close to a library. Therefore, proximity by itself cannot explain the difference; at least one other factor must be involved.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because nothing states that older demographic information was used to calculate the percentages.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because the researchers’ expectations are never described, so no comparison with a predicted difference can be made.

questions.explanation: Turku had the higher reported rate of library use despite having a lower proportion of respondents living close to a library. Therefore, proximity by itself cannot explain the difference; at least one other factor must be involved.

questions.passage: At nearly 84 meters tall and more than 31 meters in circumference at its base, the giant sequoia known as the General Sherman Tree contains more trunk volume than any other known living single-stem tree. Its extraordinary scale gives the tree a particularly _____ presence among the surrounding forest.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: illusory
choices.B: commanding
choices.C: intricate
choices.D: idealized

choiceExplanations.B: This choice. commanding is correct. Something commanding is striking, impressive, or capable of attracting attention because of its scale or appearance. The passage emphasizes the tree’s enormous height, circumference, and volume, so “commanding presence” follows logically.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because illusory means deceptive or unreal, and the tree’s size is presented as factual.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because intricate describes complexity of detail rather than overwhelming size or prominence.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because idealized means represented as more perfect than reality; the passage simply gives measurements and comparisons.

questions.explanation: B. commanding is correct. Something commanding is striking, impressive, or capable of attracting attention because of its scale or appearance. The passage emphasizes the tree’s enormous height, circumference, and volume, so “commanding presence” follows logically.

questions.passage: Hypothesizing that low-frequency natural soundscapes reduce stress in captive harbor seals, behavioral ecologist Maren Voss and colleagues played recordings of distant surf and, on separate occasions, recordings of irregular mechanical clanking to the same animals. The seals’ heart rates decreased more during the surf recordings. Because a reduction in heart rate can accompany relaxation, the researchers interpreted the result as evidence of reduced stress. One critic, however, argues that lowered heart rate can also occur during intense orienting responses and that the surf recordings may simply have captured the seals’ attention. Voss and colleagues also measured pupil diameter, which generally increases when an animal’s attentional arousal rises.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the critic’s argument?

choices.A: The seals blinked at approximately the same rate during the surf recordings and the mechanical recordings.
choices.B: The seals had not previously been exposed to either set of recordings used in the experiment.
choices.C: The seals’ pupils were smaller during the surf recordings than during the mechanical recordings.
choices.D: Animal-care staff generally rated recordings of surf as more pleasant than recordings of machinery.

choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because the passage establishes no relationship between blinking and the disputed explanation, so equal blink rates would not directly address the critic’s claim.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because unfamiliarity with both recordings does not distinguish between the relaxation and attention explanations.
choiceExplanations.C: The critic proposes an alternative explanation: the lower heart rate may reflect heightened attention rather than relaxation. The passage states that increased attentional arousal is generally associated with larger pupils. If the seals instead had smaller pupils during the surf recordings, that result would undermine the claim that heightened attention explains their lower heart rates and would therefore strengthen the researchers’ relaxation interpretation.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because the preferences of human staff members provide no evidence about the seals’ physiological state.

questions.explanation: The critic proposes an alternative explanation: the lower heart rate may reflect heightened attention rather than relaxation. The passage states that increased attentional arousal is generally associated with larger pupils. If the seals instead had smaller pupils during the surf recordings, that result would undermine the claim that heightened attention explains their lower heart rates and would therefore strengthen the researchers’ relaxation interpretation.

questions.passage: Historian Amara Keene serves on a committee that recommends additions to the Provincial Register of Industrial Heritage, which already includes the 1908 Bellhaven Pumping Station and the 1916 Calder Foundry. Keene does not determine which properties receive protected status by herself, _____ final designations require approval from the committee’s eleven other voting members.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: however and all
choices.B: however, all
choices.C: however all
choices.D: however. All

choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because it provides no appropriate boundary between the two independent clauses.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “however and all” does not form a grammatical connection between the clauses.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because a comma after however would leave two independent clauses joined only by punctuation that cannot properly connect them in this structure.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice. however. All is correct. The word however functions at the end of the first independent clause: “Keene does not determine which properties receive protected status by herself, however.” A period then properly separates that complete sentence from the next independent sentence, “All final designations require approval....”

questions.explanation: C. however. All is correct. The word however functions at the end of the first independent clause: “Keene does not determine which properties receive protected status by herself, however.” A period then properly separates that complete sentence from the next independent sentence, “All final designations require approval....”

questions.passage: In hospital design, access to daylight, natural materials, and views of vegetation is sometimes incorporated into waiting areas to make unfamiliar clinical environments feel less severe. Such features can help _____ a sense of ease in patients and visitors, although excessive visual stimulation may have the opposite effect.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: foster
choices.B: constrain
choices.C: repudiate
choices.D: counterbalance

choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because repudiate means reject or disavow, and one cannot logically “repudiate a sense of ease” in this context.
choiceExplanations.A: This choice. foster is correct. To foster something is to encourage or promote its development. Because the design features are intended to make clinical spaces feel less severe, they can logically foster a sense of ease.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because constrain means limit or restrict, which contradicts the stated goal of increasing comfort.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because counterbalance means offset one thing with another; although the design features may counterbalance the severity of the environment, the sentence specifically requires a verb describing what they do to a sense of ease, which they create or encourage rather than offset.

questions.explanation: C. foster is correct. To foster something is to encourage or promote its development. Because the design features are intended to make clinical spaces feel less severe, they can logically foster a sense of ease.

questions.passage: A student is writing about early structures associated with astronomical observation and wants to indicate approximately how long ago each was constructed.
questions.question: According to the table, the Goseck Circle was built _____

choices.A: 1,900 to 2,100 years ago.
choices.B: 6,800 to 7,000 years ago.
choices.C: 5,400 to 5,600 years ago.
choices.D: 2,250 to 2,350 years ago.

choiceExplanations.C: gives the age of the Mnajdra South Temple.
choiceExplanations.A: gives the age listed for the Uaxactun E-Group.
choiceExplanations.B: the row for the Goseck Circle lists its approximate age as 6,800 to 7,000 years before present.
choiceExplanations.D: gives the age of the Chankillo Tower Complex. The question requires a direct match between the named structure and the age reported in its row.

questions.explanation: the row for the Goseck Circle lists its approximate age as 6,800 to 7,000 years before present.
