questions.passage: Honeybees and some vertebrates have demonstrated an ability to learn abstract relationships such as “same” and “different,” but fruit flies were long assumed to respond only to comparatively simple associations between individual stimuli and rewards. To test that assumption, behavioral neuroscientist Mireya Santos and her team trained fruit flies in a Y-shaped maze. Flies first encountered pairs of odors that were either identical or different; after training, they were presented with entirely new odors arranged according to the same relationships. The flies selected the arm corresponding to the previously rewarded relationship at rates well above chance, even though they had never encountered the new odors before.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Researchers have long known that honeybees can distinguish among unfamiliar odors in laboratory mazes.
choices.B: Contrary to a previous assumption about their cognitive limitations, fruit flies may be capable of learning an abstract relationship between stimuli.
choices.C: Fruit flies appear to respond with greater accuracy to newly encountered odors than honeybees do when the two groups are tested under comparable experimental conditions.
choices.D: The ability to detect differences among odors allows many insect species to locate food more efficiently.

choiceExplanations.C: introduces a comparison between fruit flies and honeybees that the study does not make.
choiceExplanations.A: concerns honeybees, which appear only as background context and are not the focus of the experiment.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice states the central conclusion supported by the experiment. Researchers had assumed that fruit flies could learn only simple associations, but the flies successfully applied a previously learned relationship to entirely new odors. That result suggests that they may be capable of a more abstract form of learning than researchers had expected.
choiceExplanations.D: discusses the ecological usefulness of odor discrimination, whereas the passage focuses specifically on whether fruit flies can generalize an abstract relationship to unfamiliar stimuli.

questions.explanation:
Choice C states the central conclusion supported by the experiment. Researchers had assumed that fruit flies could learn only simple associations, but the flies successfully applied a previously learned relationship to entirely new odors. That result suggests that they may be capable of a more abstract form of learning than researchers had expected.
Choice A concerns honeybees, which appear only as background context and are not the focus of the experiment. Choice B introduces a comparison between fruit flies and honeybees that the study does not make. Choice D discusses the ecological usefulness of odor discrimination, whereas the passage focuses specifically on whether fruit flies can generalize an abstract relationship to unfamiliar stimuli.

questions.passage: Although composers Noura Haddad and Elias Karam are both frequently grouped under the broad label of contemporary Levantine classical music, their compositional practices draw on markedly different traditions. Haddad builds many of her works around microtonal melodic systems derived from Arabic maqam. Karam, ____, structures much of his music around contrapuntal procedures associated with European chamber composition.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: therefore,
choices.B: in other words,
choices.C: however,
choices.D: to this end,

choiceExplanations.C: This choice. however, is correct. The passage first establishes that the two composers are placed under the same broad category but then emphasizes that their musical traditions differ. Haddad draws on maqam, whereas Karam relies on European contrapuntal procedures. “However” appropriately signals this contrast.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “therefore” indicates a cause-and-effect relationship; Karam’s use of counterpoint is not presented as a consequence of Haddad’s use of maqam.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because “in other words” introduces a restatement, but the sentence about Karam provides contrasting information rather than rephrasing the preceding sentence.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because “to this end” introduces an action taken to accomplish a previously stated goal, and no such goal has been established.

questions.explanation: C. however, is correct. The passage first establishes that the two composers are placed under the same broad category but then emphasizes that their musical traditions differ. Haddad draws on maqam, whereas Karam relies on European contrapuntal procedures. “However” appropriately signals this contrast.

questions.passage: Copper ore extracted from the Chuquicamata mine in northern Chile is first crushed near the excavation site, then transported by rail more than 200 kilometers to processing facilities near the Pacific coast. The refined material is subsequently carried to the port of Antofagasta. ____, in the port’s outer loading terminal, the copper is transferred onto cargo vessels bound for overseas markets.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: For instance,
choices.D: There,

choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because “Instead” indicates that one action replaces another, which is not the relationship between the sentences.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “Nevertheless” signals an unexpected contrast, but no contrast exists.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because “For instance” would introduce an example of a broader claim, whereas the sentence simply continues describing the ore’s route.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice. There, is correct. The immediately preceding sentence identifies the port of Antofagasta, and the next sentence describes what happens at that location. “There” precisely refers back to the port and creates a clear spatial progression.

questions.explanation: B. There, is correct. The immediately preceding sentence identifies the port of Antofagasta, and the next sentence describes what happens at that location. “There” precisely refers back to the port and creates a clear spatial progression.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Historian Mara Vance published the scholarly book Listening to Ice in 2016.
The book examines how scientists have interpreted sounds recorded in polar environments.
Chapter 5 analyzes acoustic descriptions found in nineteenth-century whaling logs.
Chapter 8 considers uncertainty in modern scientific measurements of polar sound.
In chapter 8, Vance writes, “Noise is not merely interference; it is evidence of the instrument, the environment, and the observer meeting.”
questions.question: The student wants to provide a quotation from chapter 8 while conveying the chapter’s relevant subject. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: While discussing uncertainty in modern measurements of polar sound, Vance writes, “Noise is not merely interference; it is evidence of the instrument, the environment, and the observer meeting.”
choices.B: In her 2016 book Listening to Ice, Mara Vance examines how researchers have interpreted sounds recorded in polar regions.
choices.C: After analyzing nineteenth-century whaling logs in chapter 5, Mara Vance later considers modern scientific measurements of polar sound.
choices.D: Mara Vance writes in Listening to Ice that nineteenth-century whaling logs contain descriptions of acoustic phenomena.

choiceExplanations.C: accurately refers to material from chapters 5 and 8 but does not include the requested quotation.
choiceExplanations.A: The student must both provide a quotation from chapter 8 and communicate the chapter’s relevant subject.
choiceExplanations.B: summarizes the book’s overall subject but neither specifies chapter 8’s focus nor provides the quotation.
choiceExplanations.D: discusses the topic of chapter 5 rather than chapter 8 and does not use the quotation.

questions.explanation: The student must both provide a quotation from chapter 8 and communicate the chapter’s relevant subject.

questions.passage: Although many ____ investigations of nocturnal pollination are conducted under controlled laboratory illumination, ecologists Priya Raman and Felix Ordoñez recently took a less typical approach: they reproduced the irregular pulses of moonlight created when fast-moving clouds cross the night sky.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: provisional
choices.B: conventional
choices.C: sporadic
choices.D: eccentric

choiceExplanations.B: This choice. conventional is correct. The sentence contrasts the researchers’ “less typical approach” with the kind of investigations ordinarily conducted under controlled lighting. “Conventional” means customary or standard, so it establishes exactly the contrast the sentence requires.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “provisional” means temporary or subject to revision; the passage says nothing about whether the studies are temporary.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because “sporadic” means intermittent or irregular, which describes frequency rather than methodological normality.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because “eccentric” means unconventional or unusual, which would undermine the contrast: if the earlier studies were already eccentric, the researchers’ less typical approach would not meaningfully differ from them.

questions.explanation: B. conventional is correct. The sentence contrasts the researchers’ “less typical approach” with the kind of investigations ordinarily conducted under controlled lighting. “Conventional” means customary or standard, so it establishes exactly the contrast the sentence requires.

questions.passage: An early generation of underwater archaeological drones could photograph shipwrecks in considerable detail but could not preserve fragile sediment cores for later laboratory analysis. ____ when engineers developed the Pelagos II survey drone in 2023, they incorporated a sealed rotary coring system designed to retrieve and store undisturbed samples.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Previously,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: Likewise,

choiceExplanations.C: This choice. Consequently, is correct. The inability of earlier drones to preserve sediment cores created a limitation that engineers addressed in the later design. The addition of a sealed coring system is therefore presented as a result of the earlier shortcoming, making “Consequently” the appropriate transition.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “Specifically” introduces a more precise example or elaboration, not a consequence.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because “Previously” indicates an earlier point in time, whereas the sentence concerns the later 2023 design.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because “Likewise” signals similarity, but the later drone differs from the earlier ones by solving their limitation.

questions.explanation: C. Consequently, is correct. The inability of earlier drones to preserve sediment cores created a limitation that engineers addressed in the later design. The addition of a sealed coring system is therefore presented as a result of the earlier shortcoming, making “Consequently” the appropriate transition.

questions.passage: The earliest surviving photographs are sometimes discussed as though they were produced by the daguerreotype process introduced in 1839. Nicéphore Niépce’s famous image made more than a decade earlier did not use that process; ____, Niépce coated a pewter plate with light-sensitive bitumen and exposed it for many hours.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: consequently,
choices.B: eventually,
choices.C: similarly,
choices.D: rather,

choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because “eventually” indicates something occurring after a delay or sequence of events, not an alternative method.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “consequently” signals a result; the use of bitumen is not a consequence of the statement that Niépce did not employ daguerreotype.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because “similarly” indicates similarity, even though the sentence emphasizes a difference between processes.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice. rather, is correct. The sentence first states what Niépce did not use and then explains what he used instead. “Rather” is the appropriate transition for correcting or replacing one possibility with another.

questions.explanation: B. rather, is correct. The sentence first states what Niépce did not use and then explains what he used instead. “Rather” is the appropriate transition for correcting or replacing one possibility with another.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Magnesium is an essential mineral involved in normal nerve and muscle function.
Almonds contain magnesium.
Apples contain magnesium.
There are approximately 270 milligrams (mg) of magnesium in 100 grams (g) of almonds.
There are approximately 5 mg of magnesium in 100 g of apples.
Humans must obtain magnesium through dietary sources.
questions.question: The student wants to make and support the claim that almonds are a better source of magnesium than apples. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Almonds provide about 270 mg of magnesium per 100 g, compared with about 5 mg for apples.
choices.B: Humans must obtain magnesium from foods, and both almonds and apples contain the mineral.
choices.C: Magnesium, which is involved in normal nerve and muscle function, occurs in approximately 270 mg quantities in some foods.
choices.D: Almonds contain magnesium, an essential mineral, whereas apples are also among the foods from which people can obtain magnesium.

choiceExplanations.B: establishes that both foods contain magnesium but provides no evidence that one is a better source.
choiceExplanations.A: The student needs both to make the comparison and to support it with evidence.
choiceExplanations.C: gives the amount found in almonds only, so the reader cannot directly compare almonds with apples.
choiceExplanations.D: again establishes that both foods contain magnesium without supplying the numerical evidence necessary to support the comparative claim.

questions.explanation: The student needs both to make the comparison and to support it with evidence.

questions.passage: At the Zafra coastal wetland, average salinity is 14 parts per thousand in May; it ____ to 19 parts per thousand in June and then falls to 15 parts per thousand in July.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: has risen
choices.B: rises
choices.C: rose
choices.D: rising

choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because “rising” is a participle and cannot function as the finite verb after the explicit subject “it.” C is incorrect because “rose” is past tense and conflicts with the present-tense verbs elsewhere in the sentence.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “has risen” uses the present perfect, which does not match the simple-present description of the recurring pattern.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice. rises is correct. The sentence describes a recurring or general pattern using the present tense: salinity “is” 14 parts per thousand in May and later “falls” to 15 in July. The present-tense verb “rises” correctly maintains that tense and supplies the finite verb required after the subject “it.”
choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not satisfy the evidence, wording, or grammatical requirement established by the question.

questions.explanation: D. rises is correct. The sentence describes a recurring or general pattern using the present tense: salinity “is” 14 parts per thousand in May and later “falls” to 15 in July. The present-tense verb “rises” correctly maintains that tense and supplies the finite verb required after the subject “it.”

questions.passage: A continuous-flow grain dryer moves harvested grain steadily through a heated chamber, allowing processing to continue with relatively little interruption. A batch dryer instead dries a fixed quantity at a time; once one batch is finished, it must be removed before another can be loaded. Although batch dryers do not operate continuously in the same way that continuous-flow systems do, a facility using batch dryers can process more grain annually than some facilities using continuous-flow systems. For example, the ____.
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?

choices.A: Red Willow Grain dries more grain annually than Pine Belt Storage does, even though Red Willow uses continuous-flow dryers
choices.B: Pine Belt Storage, a batch facility, operates more dryer units than any other facility in the table
choices.C: High Plains Cooperative, a batch facility, dries more grain annually than either continuous-flow facility shown in the table
choices.D: continuous-flow facility with the greatest annual output dries more grain than the batch facility with the greatest annual output

choiceExplanations.A: is factually true according to the table, but it demonstrates the opposite comparison: a continuous-flow facility outperforming a batch facility. It therefore does not support the stated claim.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because High Plains Cooperative, not Pine Belt Storage, has the greatest number of dryer units.
choiceExplanations.C: The claim is that a batch facility can process more grain annually than some continuous-flow facilities. High Plains Cooperative uses batch drying and processes 162,400 metric tons per year, exceeding both continuous-flow facilities: Red Willow Grain at 48,300 and Delta AgriDry at 9,700.
choiceExplanations.D: is false because the highest-output continuous-flow facility, Red Willow Grain at 48,300 metric tons, processes far less grain annually than the highest-output batch facility, High Plains Cooperative at 162,400 metric tons.

questions.explanation: The claim is that a batch facility can process more grain annually than some continuous-flow facilities. High Plains Cooperative uses batch drying and processes 162,400 metric tons per year, exceeding both continuous-flow facilities: Red Willow Grain at 48,300 and Delta AgriDry at 9,700.

table.caption: Selected Grain-Drying Facilities, 2025

questions.passage: Few first-time conservators ____ that a sheet of nineteenth-century paper can become more brittle after an apparently successful washing treatment. Yet if the cellulose fibers have already undergone substantial oxidation, prolonged exposure to alkaline solutions can accelerate deterioration rather than reverse it.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: dispute
choices.B: disregard
choices.C: require
choices.D: anticipate

choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because “disregard” means ignore; although a conservator might disregard a risk, the second sentence specifically emphasizes the unexpected nature of the result.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “dispute” means argue against a claim; the passage concerns whether conservators expect an outcome, not whether they challenge it.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because “require” means need or demand and does not make sense with the clause that follows.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice. anticipate is correct. The passage states that inexperienced conservators may not expect a seemingly beneficial treatment to worsen fragile paper. “Anticipate” means expect or foresee, which precisely fits that idea.

questions.explanation: B. anticipate is correct. The passage states that inexperienced conservators may not expect a seemingly beneficial treatment to worsen fragile paper. “Anticipate” means expect or foresee, which precisely fits that idea.

questions.passage: Published enrollment figures for the same university can differ substantially depending on which campuses are included. Institutions commonly report one figure for a principal campus and another for an entire university system, including satellite campuses in other locations. Citing the data in the table, an education journalist argues that the national enrollment estimates most likely include at least some students outside the institutions’ principal campuses.
questions.question: Which choice best describes data in the table that support the journalist’s claim?

choices.A: Universidad del Valle Norte’s national estimate of 41,800 students is substantially greater than its main-campus enrollment of 23,460.
choices.B: The main campus of Lakehurst State University occupies a substantially larger area of land than the main campus of Université de Montferrand does.
choices.C: Université de Montferrand reports a larger main-campus enrollment than Marston University does.
choices.D: Every university’s systemwide enrollment exceeds 25,000 students.

choiceExplanations.B: compares campus areas, which has no direct bearing on whether enrollment estimates include students at satellite campuses.
choiceExplanations.A: If the national estimate for Universidad del Valle Norte is 41,800 while only 23,460 students attend the main campus, the much larger national figure is consistent with the journalist’s claim that the estimate includes students attending locations beyond that campus.
choiceExplanations.C: compares the main-campus enrollments of two different universities rather than comparing two measures for the same institution.
choiceExplanations.D: concerns the size of the systems overall; it does not show that the national estimates extend beyond individual principal campuses.

questions.explanation: If the national estimate for Universidad del Valle Norte is 41,800 while only 23,460 students attend the main campus, the much larger national figure is consistent with the journalist’s claim that the estimate includes students attending locations beyond that campus.

table.caption: Enrollment and Campus Data for Four University Systems, 2022

questions.passage: A fifteenth-century astronomical manuscript preserved in Samarkand contains hand-drawn planetary tables whose calculations have long since been superseded. The manuscript is sometimes described as compelling despite its antiquity; arguably, however, it is especially ____ because of that antiquity. Marginal corrections and worn page edges make the distance between its original users and present-day readers unusually palpable.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: meticulous
choices.B: poignant
choices.C: ingenious
choices.D: pristine

choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because “ingenious” means cleverly inventive, but the passage does not argue that age makes the manuscript more inventive.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “meticulous” describes something carried out with great care and precision; the sentence concerns emotional impact, not workmanship.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice. poignant is correct. The final sentence emphasizes the emotional force produced by encountering physical traces of people who handled the manuscript centuries ago. “Poignant” means deeply affecting or emotionally evocative, which fits the idea that the manuscript is compelling precisely because of its age.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because “pristine” means exceptionally well preserved or unspoiled, directly conflicting with the references to worn edges and corrections.

questions.explanation: C. poignant is correct. The final sentence emphasizes the emotional force produced by encountering physical traces of people who handled the manuscript centuries ago. “Poignant” means deeply affecting or emotionally evocative, which fits the idea that the manuscript is compelling precisely because of its age.

questions.passage: A conservation consortium tracked the number of active wetland-restoration projects in three European river basins. Between 2018 and 2022, the number increased in one basin, while elsewhere it either remained unchanged or declined. For example, ____.
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?

choices.A: the Tagus gained two projects between 2018 and 2022, while the Lower Vistula lost three
choices.B: the Upper Morava had more projects in 2022 than the Tagus did in 2018
choices.C: the Lower Vistula had more projects in 2022 than in 2018, whereas the Tagus had the same number in both years
choices.D: the Lower Vistula and Upper Morava both had ten projects in 2022

choiceExplanations.A: reverses both trends: the Tagus remained unchanged, while the Lower Vistula increased.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because the Upper Morava had only 3 projects in 2022, fewer than the Tagus’s 7 in 2018.
choiceExplanations.C: The Lower Vistula rises from 6 projects in 2018 to 10 in 2022, while the Tagus remains at 7 projects in both years. That evidence directly illustrates the statement that one basin experienced an increase while another remained unchanged.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because only the Lower Vistula had 10 projects in 2022; the Upper Morava had 3.

questions.explanation: The Lower Vistula rises from 6 projects in 2018 to 10 in 2022, while the Tagus remains at 7 projects in both years. That evidence directly illustrates the statement that one basin experienced an increase while another remained unchanged.

graph.caption: Wetland-Restoration Projects Active in Three River Basins, 2018–2022

questions.passage: After examining the correspondence of physicist Chien-Shiung Wu, the researcher located archival files concerning two other scientists who worked at Columbia ____ chemist Gertrude Scharff Goldhaber and physicist Tsung-Dao Lee.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: University,
choices.B: University
choices.C: University;
choices.D: University:

choiceExplanations.D: This choice. University: is correct. The clause before the blank—“the researcher located archival files concerning two other scientists who worked at Columbia University”—is grammatically complete. What follows names the two scientists referred to in that clause.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because a comma alone is not appropriate for introducing the list after a complete independent clause in this construction.
choiceExplanations.B: provides no punctuation to signal that the two names specify the preceding phrase.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because a semicolon normally separates independent clauses; “chemist Gertrude Scharff Goldhaber and physicist Tsung-Dao Lee” is not an independent clause.

questions.explanation: D. University: is correct. The clause before the blank—“the researcher located archival files concerning two other scientists who worked at Columbia University”—is grammatically complete. What follows names the two scientists referred to in that clause.

questions.passage: Leena Patel and colleagues found that prescribed burning—deliberately setting controlled, low-intensity fires—was associated with greater seedling density in bur oak. But studies involving other tree species have sometimes found the opposite association. For example, ____.
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the assertion?

choices.A: Henrik Dahl and colleagues recorded 218 eastern-hemlock seedlings per hectare with burning but 463 without burning.
choices.B: Owen Mercer and colleagues reported a pattern in blue oak similar to the one Patel and colleagues reported in bur oak.
choices.C: María Quispe and colleagues found 114 more longleaf-pine seedlings per hectare with burning than without it.
choices.D: Seedling density with burning ranged from 218 per hectare in eastern hemlock to 755 per hectare in bur oak.

choiceExplanations.C: describes another positive association between burning and seedling density, not an opposite one.
choiceExplanations.A: The passage needs an example of the opposite of Patel’s result. Patel’s study found more seedlings with burning than without it. Dahl’s study found only 218 seedlings per hectare with burning compared with 463 without burning, so burning was associated with substantially lower seedling density.
choiceExplanations.B: explicitly says that Mercer found a pattern similar to Patel’s.
choiceExplanations.D: accurately states a range of densities, but it does not compare burned and unburned conditions within a species, so it does not demonstrate the opposite association.

questions.explanation: The passage needs an example of the opposite of Patel’s result. Patel’s study found more seedlings with burning than without it. Dahl’s study found only 218 seedlings per hectare with burning compared with 463 without burning, so burning was associated with substantially lower seedling density.

table.caption: Effects of Prescribed Burning on Seedling Density

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Friendship agreements between botanical gardens are formal partnerships intended to encourage horticultural and cultural exchange.
Such agreements became increasingly common among public gardens during the late twentieth century.
Numerous botanical gardens in Canada maintain partnerships with gardens overseas.
Montréal’s Jardin botanique and the Botanical Garden of Curitiba, Brazil, established a formal friendship agreement in 1991.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the duration of the relationship between the two botanical gardens. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Public botanical gardens increasingly established international friendship agreements during the late twentieth century.
choices.B: Montréal’s Jardin botanique and the Botanical Garden of Curitiba have maintained a formal partnership since 1991.
choices.C: The Botanical Garden of Curitiba, located in Brazil, has a formal friendship agreement with Montréal’s Jardin botanique.
choices.D: Like numerous Canadian botanical gardens, Montréal’s Jardin botanique participates in an international horticultural partnership.

choiceExplanations.B: The goal is to emphasize how long the relationship has existed. The phrase “have maintained a formal partnership since 1991” directly communicates its duration by identifying the starting year and showing that the relationship has continued.
choiceExplanations.A: provides historical context about such partnerships generally but says nothing about the duration of this specific relationship.
choiceExplanations.C: identifies the partnership and locations but omits when it began.
choiceExplanations.D: likewise establishes that the partnership exists without indicating its length.

questions.explanation: The goal is to emphasize how long the relationship has existed. The phrase “have maintained a formal partnership since 1991” directly communicates its duration by identifying the starting year and showing that the relationship has continued.

questions.passage: Stretching for more than 160 kilometers across the tidal flats of South Korea’s southwest coast, the Saemangeum seawall ____ among the world’s longest human-made coastal barriers.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: having ranked
choices.B: ranking
choices.C: is ranked
choices.D: to rank

choiceExplanations.C: This choice. is ranked is correct. The introductory participial phrase “Stretching for more than 160 kilometers...” modifies the subject “the Saemangeum seawall.” The main clause still requires a finite verb, which “is ranked” supplies.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because “having ranked” is a participial form and cannot serve as the finite verb of the main clause.
choiceExplanations.B: has the same problem: “ranking” would leave the sentence without a finite verb.
choiceExplanations.D: “to rank,” is an infinitive and likewise cannot complete the main clause.

questions.explanation: C. is ranked is correct. The introductory participial phrase “Stretching for more than 160 kilometers...” modifies the subject “the Saemangeum seawall.” The main clause still requires a finite verb, which “is ranked” supplies.

questions.passage: Bioluminescence is often associated with ocean animals such as lanternfish and comb jellies. Yet the ability to produce visible light is not confined to marine organisms. Several terrestrial fungi, including species of Mycena, emit a greenish glow from their fruiting bodies or mycelia, and certain beetles produce light through specialized abdominal organs.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain why bioluminescence evolved independently in fungi and insects
choices.B: To contrast the chemical mechanisms that produce light in marine and terrestrial organisms
choices.C: To argue that bioluminescence occurs predominantly in terrestrial rather than marine environments
choices.D: To discuss the occurrence of bioluminescence in organisms beyond those with which the trait is most commonly associated

choiceExplanations.D: The passage begins with organisms commonly associated with bioluminescence and then broadens the reader’s understanding by explaining that terrestrial fungi and insects can also produce light. Its main purpose is therefore to show that the trait occurs in a wider range of organisms than people may initially assume.
choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because the passage does not discuss evolutionary origins or independent evolution.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because no biochemical mechanisms are compared.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because the passage does not claim that terrestrial bioluminescence is more common than marine bioluminescence; it simply establishes that the phenomenon is not limited to marine organisms.

questions.explanation: The passage begins with organisms commonly associated with bioluminescence and then broadens the reader’s understanding by explaining that terrestrial fungi and insects can also produce light. Its main purpose is therefore to show that the trait occurs in a wider range of organisms than people may initially assume.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Photographer Mireya Solano is known for large-format photographs of abandoned industrial interiors.
Her photograph After the Last Shift (46 × 68 in) depicts a former textile mill shortly before sunrise.
A rusted loom occupies the extreme lower-left portion of the image.
A broken clerestory window appears near the upper-right edge of the frame.
Pale morning light enters through the window and crosses the otherwise shadowed machinery.
Solano frequently uses strong diagonal compositions to direct viewers’ attention across an image.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the locations of the two prominent objects in After the Last Shift. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: *After the Last Shift* places a rusted loom at the lower left and a broken clerestory window near the upper right.
choices.B: Measuring 46 by 68 inches, After the Last Shift is a large-format photograph of an abandoned textile mill shortly before sunrise.
choices.C: Solano uses light entering through a broken clerestory window to create a strong diagonal across the machinery in After the Last Shift.
choices.D: Like many of Solano’s photographs, After the Last Shift depicts an industrial interior whose abandoned machinery remains visually prominent.

questions.explanation: it directly identifies where both objects are positioned: the loom is at the extreme lower left, and the window is near the upper-right edge. Those are precisely the notes relevant to the student’s goal.

choiceExplanations.A: it directly identifies where both objects are positioned: the loom is at the extreme lower left, and the window is near the upper-right edge. Those are precisely the notes relevant to the student’s goal.
choiceExplanations.B: provides the photograph’s dimensions, subject, and time of day but says nothing about where the two objects appear.
choiceExplanations.C: identifies the window and discusses the direction of the light, but it does not state the locations of both the window and the loom.
choiceExplanations.D: describes the photograph more generally and mentions industrial machinery, but it does not specify the objects’ positions within the frame.

questions.passage: For decades, seismologists classified certain faults as either active or inactive largely according to whether those faults had produced detectable movement during a specified span of geological time. Researchers Leena Varma and Nicolás Estevez have argued, however, that such labels can become unstable as measurement technology improves. Instruments capable of detecting millimeter-scale deformation sometimes reveal motion along faults formerly regarded as inactive, while longer observation records can show that supposedly active faults remain quiet for extended periods. These observations suggest that ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: faults currently classified as active should automatically be considered more dangerous than any fault classified as inactive.
choices.B: faults previously labeled inactive generally begin moving because monitoring equipment has become more sensitive.
choices.C: improved instruments will eventually eliminate the need to distinguish among different categories of faults.
choices.D: geological agencies may periodically need to reconsider how particular faults are classified as new measurements become available.

questions.explanation: The passage explains that improved measurements can reveal evidence inconsistent with earlier classifications. If supposedly inactive faults show measurable movement and supposedly active ones can remain quiet for long periods, then existing classifications may need to be reevaluated as evidence changes.

choiceExplanations.B: mistakes detection for causation.
choiceExplanations.A: goes beyond the passage, which discusses classification rather than comparative danger.
choiceExplanations.C: is too extreme: better measurements may complicate or refine categories, but nothing suggests that categories will become unnecessary.
choiceExplanations.D: The passage explains that improved measurements can reveal evidence inconsistent with earlier classifications. questions.explanation: The first sentence defines corbeling in general terms. questions.passage:
Text 1
For much of the twentieth century, archaeologists maintained that glass production in the Late Bronze Age Aegean was concentrated at palatial centers. Furnaces, crucibles, and colored-glass fragments had been documented most often at large administrative sites, leading researchers to argue that elites exercised substantial control over the manufacture of glass objects.
Text 2
Recent fieldwork has complicated that account. Lena Kouris and colleagues identified evidence of small-scale glassworking at several nonpalatial coastal settlements, including vitrified crucible fragments and production waste. The researchers contend that the older interpretation may partly reflect an archaeological sampling bias: excavations in the region historically concentrated on monumental palace complexes, while smaller settlements received comparatively little investigation.

choices.D: They would contend that access to raw materials, rather than elite administration, explains why glassworking occurred primarily at palatial sites.

If archaeologists disproportionately excavated monumental palace complexes and investigated smaller settlements less often, evidence from palatial sites would naturally be overrepresented. Kouris and colleagues would therefore regard the view in Text 1 as influenced by the kinds of sites researchers historically selected. Choice A introduces a distinction between the types of objects made at different sites that Text 2 never establishes. Choice C invents a chronological shift; the coastal evidence is presented as evidence that complicates the traditional account of the same broad period, not as evidence from a later era. Choice D substitutes access to raw materials for the excavation-bias explanation actually emphasized in Text 2.

questions.passage: Linguist Neha Raman and colleagues have examined cases in which unrelated languages independently acquire similar grammatical structures after sustained contact with the same regional lingua franca. Other researchers, including Mateo Serra and his team, have documented grammatical similarities that arise through separate internal changes without such a shared external source. Yet the relative frequency of these two routes to structural convergence remains poorly established. choices.B: Before Nwosu and Chen’s study, linguists generally assumed that unrelated languages could develop similar grammatical structures only through contact.
choices.C: Nwosu and Chen examined two mechanisms that can produce grammatical convergence in order to address uncertainty about their relative prevalence.
choices.D: Both Raman’s team and Nwosu and Chen compared externally driven convergence directly with convergence produced through independent internal change.

questions.explanation: Choice C accurately captures the full passage. Two different routes to grammatical convergence are introduced, the text identifies a gap in knowledge concerning how common each route is, and Nwosu and Chen’s study is presented as an attempt to address that gap by examining both mechanisms. Choice A incorrectly says the researchers proved that one mechanism predominates and used the earlier teams’ datasets; neither claim appears in the text. Choice B exaggerates the state of prior scholarship: the passage says researchers had already studied both mechanisms. Choice D mischaracterizes Raman’s research, which examined one route rather than explicitly comparing both routes.

questions.passage: Researchers often explain household adoption of rooftop rainwater-harvesting systems using a capital-access model, which predicts that wealthier households are more likely to adopt such systems because they can more readily absorb installation costs. questions.passage: Songs at the Threshold is a 1903 collection of poetry by Adelaide Mercer. In one poem, the speaker criticizes reformers who publicly lament injustices in distant places while failing to confront suffering within their own communities, saying _____

questions.passage: Beginning in 2006, several European cities substantially reduced fares on municipal bus and tram systems in an effort to increase public-transit use. Choice D also reverses the evidence; the longer-term analysis is precisely what casts doubt on the persistence of the initial gains.

Together, those results support the conclusion that fare reductions may boost ridership initially but that the gains may not persist.

questions.passage: The genetic identity of a barley population cultivated in eastern Anatolia roughly seven thousand years ago has not been directly established, but researchers suspect that it belonged to the West Eurasian domesticated-barley complex. Surviving landraces in that complex fall into two major genetic branches, the Zagros branch and the Aegean branch. Several domesticated-barley alleles are also present in genetically distinct wild barley populations from eastern Anatolia; researchers believe that those alleles entered the wild populations through ancient cross-pollination during the period when the vanished cultivated population dominated local agriculture. choices.B: the Aegean branch did not emerge until after cultivation of the vanished barley population had ended.
choices.C: the vanished barley population was more likely affiliated with the Zagros branch than with the Aegean branch.
choices.D: the vanished barley population contributed genetic material equally to the Zagros branch, the Aegean branch, and local wild barley.

questions.explanation: Choice C is the most logical inference. The wild barley populations acquired domesticated alleles during a period when the vanished cultivated population was widespread nearby. Because those introgressed alleles specifically match the Zagros branch, the vanished cultivated population was more likely genetically affiliated with that branch than with the Aegean branch. Choice A goes much further than the evidence supports: nothing indicates that the vanished population was ancestral to both major branches. Choice B makes an unsupported chronological claim about when the Aegean branch originated. Choice D contradicts the evidence because the introgressed alleles identified in the wild populations trace specifically to the Zagros branch, not equally to both domesticated branches.

choiceExplanations.B: Choice B makes an unsupported chronological claim about when the Aegean branch originated.

questions.passage: As sediment accumulates behind aging hydroelectric dams, reservoirs can lose storage capacity and eventually become uneconomical to operate. choices.B: It contrasts the obvious financial interest that workers have in dam operations with the less immediately evident financial interest of the municipal utilities discussed earlier in the text.
choices.C: It explains that utilities have concealed the financial consequences of sedimentation and describes how that concealment has harmed dam workers.
choices.D: It provides general background about reservoir sedimentation that applies equally to both utilities and workers introduced elsewhere in the text.

Choice C invents concealment by utilities; the passage merely says risks should be disclosed. questions.passage: Astronomer Mireya Solberg and colleagues used century-old photographic plates preserved in observatory archives to reconstruct the past brightness of a variable star. questions.passage: Adaptive route-choice theory predicts that drivers alter their behavior according to changing traffic conditions, but the benefit of real-time information may differ across groups. B describes the result of the earlier commuter study rather than Chen’s study. D confuses the proposed explanation—delivery drivers’ greater reliance on navigation software—with an observed change in that reliance as alerts increased.

choiceExplanations.B: B describes the result of the earlier commuter study rather than Chen’s study.

questions.passage: In 2004, the government of Lydavia abolished licensing rules that had sharply limited the number of private mobile-phone carriers permitted to operate in the country. questions.passage: The Aramoor Observatory maintains an extensive collection of historical astronomical instruments, but visitors hoping to _____ their understanding of early observational practice can also follow the observatory’s outdoor meridian trail, where reconstructed sighting posts demonstrate how astronomers aligned instruments before precision clocks became common.

choices.A: curtail

choices.C: augment
choices.D: provoke

questions.explanation: The outdoor trail provides an additional way for visitors to deepen what they learn from the observatory’s collection, so “augment,” meaning increase or add to, is the most precise choice. questions.passage: Researchers developed a computational model intended to predict how much listeners would enjoy short musical excerpts on a 10-point scale. Thus, A is correct. B contradicts the stated assumption that P6’s reported averages were equal. C reverses the relationship shown by the prediction differences. D would require the two prediction surpluses to be equal, but the graph shows that they are not.

questions.passage: Electricity generated by wind and solar installations can now be transmitted across long distances with considerably greater efficiency than in previous decades. Lithium-ion batteries perform well over shorter intervals but become costly when scaled for multiday storage. Alternative systems, including flow batteries and compressed-air storage, are being developed, but each currently faces substantial limitations involving cost, geography, efficiency, or maintenance. Accordingly, energy researchers suggest that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: even if demand for renewable electricity declines sharply, difficulties associated with multiday energy storage will necessarily become more severe.
choices.B: overcoming the limitations of long-duration energy storage will likely require further advances in storage technologies and methods.
choices.C: transmission efficiency is the principal factor determining public support for renewable energy, so utilities should focus primarily on transmission infrastructure.
choices.D: grid operators should invest more heavily in established long-distance transmission systems than in storage technologies that remain under development.

questions.explanation: The passage identifies long-duration storage as an unresolved bottleneck and explains that both established batteries and newer alternatives have important limitations. B logically follows: additional technological advances will likely be required to overcome those limitations. A introduces a decline in consumer demand that the passage never discusses and asserts an unsupported consequence. C shifts to public support and incorrectly identifies transmission as the main problem even though the passage says transmission has improved. D also conflicts with the passage’s reasoning: the unresolved difficulty is storage, so emphasizing already improved transmission does not address the identified bottleneck.

choiceExplanations.A: A introduces a decline in consumer demand that the passage never discusses and asserts an unsupported consequence.
choiceExplanations.B: The passage identifies long-duration storage as an unresolved bottleneck and explains that both established batteries and newer alternatives have important limitations.
choiceExplanations.C: C shifts to public support and incorrectly identifies transmission as the main problem even though the passage says transmission has improved.
choiceExplanations.D: D also conflicts with the passage’s reasoning: the unresolved difficulty is storage, so emphasizing already improved transmission does not address the identified bottleneck.

questions.passage: An irregular tremor in the shuttle of a century-old mechanical loom puzzled conservators at the Veyra Textile Laboratory. A is incorrect because motion is central to the model; the passage does not describe a method that dispenses with motion evidence.
B is incorrect because the tremor is precisely the evidence prompting the chamber hypothesis.

choiceExplanations.C: C is correct because it connects the observed tremor with the team’s tentative explanation while retaining the distinction between a proposed cause and a confirmed discovery.

questions.passage: Among canal engineers in the early twentieth-century Netherlands, keeping a pocket maintenance ledger was routine. questions.passage:

No one trained to judge such things could have called the collection distinguished. The curator objected to its uncertain labels and its lack of a proper catalog; the clockmaker, turning a tarnished dial, pronounced the workmanship a distressing jumble of incompatible traditions. To the apprentices, who until that week had measured an afternoon by the length of a fence-post’s shadow, these shortcomings scarcely existed. Here were brass birds that sang without breathing, tiny hammers that announced an hour, and wheels apparently capable of remembering time. choices.C: Despite the experts’ criticisms, the apprentices find the collection profoundly captivating.

questions.passage: The pace and timing of speech help organize everyday interactions, signaling deference, familiarity, and the expectation that another speaker will take a turn. Linguistic historians are increasingly interested in recovering these features from early sound recordings to investigate political oratory, classroom conduct, and regional conventions. You took the room I gave for room to trample;
That lesson ends. The man beneath this [habit]

Has cost the name of mastery its weight.
The lofty will acknowledge only strength;

The pale kiln arches hold a patient gleam.
No draught disturbs that uninsistent bloom,
No sound pursues the workshop’s quiet dream.

Upon my hurrying years without regret:
A guarded ember, generous and small,

choiceExplanations.A: A is incorrect because the intervening publication phrase still leads to Kest as the subject, producing the same misplaced description.

questions.passage: Edda Nerl and Taren Soot’s assessment of nominal network fault tolerance and its evolution across design generations ______ nine architectural features that strengthen such tolerance, including independent backup channels and fixed clock references. The Selen relay blueprint contains eight of these features.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: are isolating
choices.B: have isolated
choices.C: isolates
choices.D: isolate

questions.explanation:
C is correct because the singular subject’s head is “assessment.”
A is incorrect because “are” is plural.
D is incorrect because the bare present form does not agree with the singular head.
B is incorrect because “have” is plural. Two authors and multiple design generations do not make their one assessment plural.

choiceExplanations.C: C is correct because the singular subject’s head is “assessment.”

choiceExplanations.D: D is incorrect because the bare present form does not agree with the singular head.

questions.passage: The Merren campus in Ravelle was once headquarters of the Astrel Photonics Division, one of several nominally autonomous units in the Raynor Research Consortium. Like ______ peer regional units, the Astrel Division was organized by spectral range: most specialists studied infrared emission.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: its
choices.B: it’s
choices.C: they’re
choices.D: their

questions.explanation:
A is correct because the singular division has peer units, requiring possessive “its.”
C is incorrect because “they’re” means “they are.”
D is incorrect because “their” is plural; the owned peers are plural, but the owner is one division.
B is incorrect because “it’s” is a contraction rather than a possessive.

questions.passage: Corroborated by ultrasonic inspections of 3,460 riveted joints in decommissioned suspension bridges, ______
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the principal sources of fatigue in the suspension cables were moisture and repeated loading, according to a 2018 investigation.
choices.B: the suspension cables’ fatigue was attributed, in a 2018 investigation, primarily to moisture and repeated loading.
choices.C: conclusions drawn in a 2018 investigation indicated that moisture and repeated loading were the principal sources of fatigue in the suspension cables.
choices.D: moisture and repeated loading were, a 2018 investigation established, the principal sources of fatigue in the suspension cables.

questions.explanation: The introductory phrase describes something whose validity the inspections corroborated. Choice C places “conclusions” immediately after that phrase, correctly identifying the conclusions as the supported claims; the rest of the sentence states what those conclusions indicated. Choice A instead makes “the principal sources” the subject, so the inspections appear to corroborate the physical sources themselves. Choice D similarly attaches the modifier to “moisture and repeated loading,” rather than to a finding about their effects. Choice B attaches it to the cables’ fatigue, a physical condition rather than an investigative conclusion. References to an investigation later in those choices cannot repair the initial attachment.

questions.passage: Among the 83 variable stars represented in Chilean spectroscopist Inés Valcárcel’s atlas The Arclight Register is Vesper-31, a pulsating giant whose spectrum has been recorded on 926 separate nights. ______ characterized the survey archive (a repository of 1.7 million calibrated exposures) as “the southern sky’s patient witness,” preserves its historical continuity through comparative plates of Vesper-31 and neighboring stars.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Valcárcel, has
choices.B: Valcárcel has
choices.C: Valcárcel,
choices.D: Valcárcel, having

questions.explanation: The sentence’s main subject is “Valcárcel,” and its main verb is “preserves.” Choice D introduces “having characterized,” a participial phrase enclosed by the comma after the name and the comma following the quotation. That phrase supplies background without competing with the main predicate. Choice B makes “has characterized” a finite predicate but leaves “preserves” improperly connected after a comma. Choice C makes “characterized” finite as well, with a comma incorrectly separating it from its subject and no conjunction connecting the two predicates. Choice A creates both that subject–verb separation and the unconnected finite predicates. The atlas and repository details do not alter the sentence’s underlying structure.

questions.passage: Once a designated mooring (“East Pilaster” and “Beacon Nine” are two examples) has remained unoccupied for the interval specified in the harbor charter, ______ eligible for reassignment under the dormant-berth provision. Under that provision, the authority may issue a new permit without renewing the previous holder’s claim.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: these become
choices.B: this becomes
choices.C: they become
choices.D: it becomes

questions.explanation: Choice D uses the singular pronoun “it” to refer directly to the singular antecedent “a designated mooring,” and “becomes” agrees with that pronoun. The two quoted examples are parenthetical illustrations; they do not replace the sentence’s singular referent. Choices A and C use plural pronouns and plural verbs, incorrectly treating the examples as the subject under discussion. Choice B uses “this” without a clarifying noun, leaving it to point vaguely to the preceding circumstance of prolonged vacancy rather than clearly to the mooring itself. That circumstance is not the berth that becomes eligible for reassignment. “It” provides the precise antecedent the sentence requires.

questions.passage: Introduced at the Orlén textile works in 1983, the Kestrel-6 loom became a mainstay of regional manufacturing. Its exceptional operating range (from fine cambric and silk gauze to heavy sailcloth and industrial belting) made the machine useful to workshops serving markedly different markets, ______ it the sobriquet “the weavers’ common engine.”
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: secured
choices.B: securing
choices.C: had secured
choices.D: secure

questions.explanation: Choice B supplies the nonfinite participle “securing,” which introduces a supplementary phrase describing the result of the machine’s usefulness across markets. The sentence already has its finite main verb, “made,” so the material after the comma must fit as an attached modifier. Choice C introduces the finite predicate “had secured” without a new subject or a conjunction. Choice A creates the same structural problem with the finite past-tense form “secured.” Choice D supplies “secure,” which cannot introduce the required supplementary phrase; it would also fail to agree with the singular main subject if treated as a present-tense predicate. The participial form connects the consequence naturally to the completed clause.

questions.passage: Municipal archives assign accession numbers for two distinct administrative purposes: to locate an object and to document its chain of custody. The problem of which features separate those functions across cataloging systems, together with the subsidiary question of why some institutions combined them, ______ archivist Marit Kolsrud’s 2019 study “Locators and Ledgers: ‘Neutral’ Numbers in Institutional Memory.”
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: have anchored
choices.B: anchor
choices.C: anchoring
choices.D: anchors

questions.explanation: The main subject is the singular noun “problem.” The clauses about “features” and “institutions” describe that problem, while the phrase beginning “together with” adds a related question without creating a compound subject. Choice D therefore supplies the required singular finite verb, “anchors.” Choice A uses the plural auxiliary “have,” which does not agree with “problem.” Choice B uses the plural present-tense form “anchor” and fails for the same reason. Choice C supplies a participle without an auxiliary, leaving the sentence’s main clause without a finite verb. The several plural nouns inside the modifiers do not control the agreement.

questions.passage: A transfer to the Rivessa hydraulic laboratory in 1964 redirected engineer Oren Salcedo’s career. At that facility, Salcedo commissioned the Vellin spillway regulator (an apparatus admired for coupling an older float mechanism with a newly developed pressure sensor) and ______ enduring collaborations with specialists in sediment transport.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: established
choices.B: to establish
choices.C: establishing
choices.D: having established

questions.explanation: The conjunction “and” joins two predicates with the same subject, “Salcedo”: he “commissioned” the regulator and “established” collaborations. Choice A supplies the finite past-tense verb parallel to “commissioned,” accurately placing both actions in the completed period described. Choice D supplies a perfect participial phrase, and choice C supplies a present participle; neither can serve as the coordinated finite predicate in this construction. Choice B introduces an infinitive without a structure that licenses it after “commissioned ... and.” The parenthetical description of the regulator intervenes between the predicates but does not change their shared subject or their required parallel grammatical form.

questions.passage: For an archival digitization program, the thickest codices might seem the obvious recipients of scarce scanning funds. Yet a volume whose binding is stable and whose contents are seldom consulted may receive little investment. Allocation follows a different calculation: a manuscript’s condition report and its record of consultation, rather than its page count, ______ its priority for scanning.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: controls
choices.B: has controlled
choices.C: controlling
choices.D: control

questions.explanation: The verb’s subject consists of two noun phrases joined by “and”: “a manuscript’s condition report” and “its record of consultation.” That compound subject requires the plural present-tense verb “control,” supplied by choice D. The intervening phrase “rather than its page count” identifies an excluded consideration and does not replace the compound subject with a singular one. Choice B uses the singular auxiliary “has”; choice A uses the singular present-tense form “controls.” Both therefore disagree with the subject. Choice C supplies the participle “controlling” without an auxiliary, leaving the clause after the colon without its required finite verb.

questions.passage: In a 2016 monograph, structural engineer Lucía Ibarra traces how maintenance practices changed across the suspension bridges of the Merava basin. Ibarra’s synthesis ______ 1,240 inspection records compiled from 1968 through 2003 establishes both the continued reliance on mechanical cable clamps and an increasing preference for bonded reinforcements, particularly carbon-fiber wraps and epoxy sleeves.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: compared
choices.B: had compared
choices.C: compares
choices.D: comparing

questions.explanation: The sentence’s subject is “Ibarra’s synthesis,” and its finite main verb is “establishes.” Choice D supplies “comparing,” introducing an integrated participial phrase that identifies the records considered by the synthesis. Because this phrase restricts and describes the subject, it can appear directly between the subject and main verb without an additional conjunction. Choices B, B, and C instead supply finite verb forms: “had compared,” “compares,” and “compared.” Each would create a second predicate immediately before “establishes,” with neither a conjunction nor a subordinate construction to connect the predicates. Differences in tense cannot repair that structural error.

questions.passage: While evaluating the drainage simulations developed by hydrologist Amira Bendel, ______ have overlooked her models’ equally substantial treatment of subsurface processes, including seasonal salt migration through buried clay lenses.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the attention of several reviewers has centered on Bendel’s treatment of surface runoff; they
choices.B: several reviewers have emphasized Bendel’s treatment of surface runoff but
choices.C: there are several reviewers who have emphasized Bendel’s treatment of surface runoff, but they
choices.D: Bendel’s treatment of surface runoff has attracted several reviewers, who

questions.explanation: The introductory phrase describes people performing the evaluation, so its understood subject must be the main subject that immediately follows. Choice B places “several reviewers” there, then coordinates their two actions: they “have emphasized” one feature but “have overlooked” another. Choice D attaches the evaluating phrase to “Bendel’s treatment,” which cannot perform an evaluation; the later “who” does not correct that attachment. Choice A similarly makes the reviewers’ “attention” the opening clause’s subject rather than the reviewers themselves. Choice C begins with the introductory “there” construction and leaves the evaluating phrase without the required directly adjoining subject. Mentioning reviewers later is insufficient.

questions.passage: Error-correcting codes, sometimes described as a storage system’s “mathematical insurance,” embed redundant bit patterns in recorded data; Reed–Solomon, BCH, and low-density parity-check codes are among the principal families. Reconstructing damaged bit sequences in long-lived tape archives, ______
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: a recent evaluation has estimated that these codes reduce unrecoverable file losses by 43 percent annually.
choices.B: a recent evaluation’s estimate is that these codes reduce unrecoverable file losses by 43 percent annually.
choices.C: an estimated 43 percent annual reduction in unrecoverable file losses is attributable to these codes, according to a recent evaluation.
choices.D: these codes reduce unrecoverable file losses by an estimated 43 percent annually, according to a recent evaluation.

questions.explanation: The opening participial phrase describes the codes that reconstruct damaged sequences. Choice D makes “these codes” the subject immediately following the phrase, so the modifier has a logical and explicit attachment. Choice C attaches the reconstructing action to a numerical “reduction,” which is an outcome rather than the mechanism that restores bits. Choice A makes “a recent evaluation” the apparent reconstructing agent; the evaluation measures the codes’ effect but does not itself serve as the code. Choice B attaches the action to an “estimate,” which likewise cannot reconstruct data. The statistic is grammatically compatible with all four endings; correct modifier placement distinguishes A.

questions.passage: The technical innovations of Saira Qureshi, whose 2007 monograph Networks Under Load transformed municipal pipe-flow analysis, ______ confined to hydraulic modeling; she had earlier developed corrosion-resistant alloys, making molybdenum (a metal she called “a reserve against fatigue” because it withstands repeated thermal cycling) central to her approach to materials design.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: aren’t
choices.B: wasn’t
choices.C: hasn’t been
choices.D: isn’t

questions.explanation: The main subject is the plural noun “innovations,” so choice A correctly supplies the plural verb “aren’t.” The relative clause about Qureshi’s singular “monograph,” along with the intervening technical phrase, describes the researcher and her work but does not control the main verb. Choice B uses singular “wasn’t”; choice C uses the singular auxiliary in “hasn’t been”; choice D uses singular “isn’t.” All three disagree with “innovations,” regardless of their differences in tense and aspect. The clause after the semicolon explains the breadth of the innovations and does not change the agreement required in the opening clause.

questions.passage: Instrument maker Reva Noren lost the ability to direct the Haldvik optical works in 1926 after developing a severe nerve disorder. The factory board consequently placed its senior designer, Petter Solheim, whose patent holdings gave him considerable authority within the firm, in charge of production. Having recovered three years later, ______ displacing an embittered Solheim from the design office and initiating a sequence of patent challenges remembered as the Calibration Dispute.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: it was Noren who resumed management of the works,
choices.B: the management of the works by Noren resumed,
choices.C: Noren resumed management of the works,
choices.D: Noren’s management of the works resumed,

questions.explanation: “Having recovered three years later” describes the person who recovered from the nerve disorder. Choice C places “Noren” immediately after that modifier and makes her the main clause’s subject. The subsequent participial phrases explain the consequences of her resuming management. Choices D and B instead make “management” the subject, illogically attributing recovery from an illness to an administrative activity. The possessive “Noren’s” in A does not make Noren the subject. Choice A begins with the anticipatory pronoun “it,” so the introductory modifier lacks the necessary direct attachment to Noren; naming her in the later cleft construction does not fix that problem.

questions.passage: During the late 1980s, systems architect Mireille Kervan became an influential advocate for maintaining accessible public records. Her exhaustive compatibility audit of tapes from the Veyrac Repository, a municipal archive in Brittany whose holdings included 1,360 magnetic reels (many containing the only surviving versions of regional census files), ______ decisive in the council’s decision to maintain the facility.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: was
choices.B: are
choices.C: were
choices.D: have been

questions.explanation: The subject of the main clause is the singular noun “audit.” Everything from “of tapes” through the parenthetical description identifies the audit’s material and setting; the plural nouns inside those modifiers do not change the head noun’s number. Choice A supplies “was,” a singular finite verb appropriate to the historical account. Choice D uses plural “have been,” choice C uses plural “were,” and choice B uses plural “are.” Each fails to agree with “audit.” The repository’s numerous reels may explain the audit’s significance, but the sentence attributes decisiveness to one audit rather than to the reels individually.

questions.passage: While restoring the upper gallery of the Marent observatory in 2017, a team led by mechanical conservator Joris Van Effen documented a previously uncatalogued hinge design. The design, which the team designated Vellan-4, resembles other articulated hinges in having staggered interlocking teeth that ______ it to tolerate repeated loading without losing alignment.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: allow
choices.B: allows
choices.C: allowing
choices.D: has allowed

questions.explanation: The relative clause beginning with “that” refers to the plural antecedent “staggered interlocking teeth.” Choice A supplies the plural finite verb “allow,” completing that clause and agreeing with its understood plural subject. Choice D supplies singular “has allowed,” and choice B supplies singular “allows”; neither agrees with the teeth. The singular nouns “design” and “Vellan-4” belong to the surrounding main clause, not to the relative clause’s subject. Choice C supplies the nonfinite participle “allowing” without an auxiliary, so the relative clause would lack a finite verb. The plural components, rather than the design as a whole, perform the action described after “that.”

questions.passage: Orbis-29 is an orbital reconstruction recalculated each spring at the Ardel tracking station in the Carpathian foothills. Derived from measurements collected while the station’s radar array operated under its first director, ______ had initially shared a stable transfer corridor with active spacecraft but was later stranded in a debris belt while executing an unauthorized course correction.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the defunct relay satellite whose path is reconstructed by Orbis-29, Arven-3,
choices.B: there was a defunct relay satellite, Arven-3, that in the Orbis-29 reconstruction
choices.C: Arven-3, the defunct relay satellite in the Orbis-29 reconstruction,
choices.D: Orbis-29 reconstructs the path of Arven-3, a defunct relay satellite that

questions.explanation: The introductory phrase describes the reconstruction, which is derived from tracking measurements. Choice D places “Orbis-29” immediately after the phrase and makes it the main clause’s subject. It then introduces a relative clause about Arven-3 that continues correctly with “had initially shared” and “was later stranded.” Choices A and C instead make the satellite the subject directly following the modifier, incorrectly suggesting that the physical spacecraft was derived from measurements. Choice B starts with an introductory “there” construction and likewise fails to attach the modifier directly to the reconstruction. Later references to Orbis-29 cannot repair that opening mismatch.

questions.passage: “Fractures That Speak,” an entry in geologist Romina Calvi’s 1923 Notebook of the Folded Coast, catalogs a basalt seam polished by tides, a quartz vein bent around a cavity, and a slate slab split into delicate fans. Calvi, a surveyor attached to the Valnera marine station, observed deformation with such acuity that the notebook’s diagnoses of stress in the western Ligurian cliffs ______ researchers more than a century later.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: engage
choices.B: engages
choices.C: has engaged
choices.D: is engaging

questions.explanation: The subject of the verb in the clause introduced by “that” is the plural noun “diagnoses.” Choice A supplies the plural present-tense verb “engage,” correctly describing those diagnoses’ continuing effect. The singular possessive noun “notebook’s” modifies “diagnoses,” while the phrase about stress and cliffs identifies their subject matter; neither replaces the plural head noun. Choice C uses singular “has,” choice D uses singular “is,” and choice B uses singular “engages.” All three therefore disagree with “diagnoses.” The earlier subject “Calvi” governs “observed,” not the verb required within the separate subordinate clause.

questions.passage: The Vardal Seed-Viability Survey, one of 237 annual assessments monitoring the condition of grain reserves at coastal storage facilities, ______ the reliability of regional planting programs by identifying seed lots whose germination rates decline during prolonged exposure to humid air.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: strengthens
choices.B: strengthen
choices.C: have strengthened
choices.D: are strengthening

questions.explanation: The singular proper noun “The Vardal Seed-Viability Survey” is the sentence’s subject. Choice A supplies the singular present-tense verb “strengthens,” which agrees with that subject. The intervening appositive identifies the survey as one assessment among many, so “assessments,” “reserves,” and “facilities” do not determine the main verb’s number. Choice D uses the plural auxiliary “are,” choice C uses plural “have,” and choice B supplies the plural present-tense form “strengthen.” Each incorrectly treats one of the nearby plural nouns as controlling the main predicate. The relative clause about declining germination rates belongs to “seed lots” and does not affect the earlier agreement.

questions.passage: The segmental load index (SLI), a calibrated measure of how unevenly force is borne by the fibers within a composite panel, ranges from 25 to 2,500 points. Compared with that of a panel whose load is sharply localized (that is, a panel in which very few fibers bear nearly all the force), ______
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: a panel in which the load is more evenly distributed will have an appreciably lower SLI score.
choices.B: when a panel’s load is more evenly distributed, it will have an appreciably lower SLI score.
choices.C: a panel with a more evenly distributed load will have an SLI score that is appreciably lower.
choices.D: the SLI score of a panel with a more evenly distributed load will be appreciably lower.

questions.explanation: In “compared with that of,” the pronoun “that” stands for an SLI score. The noun following the introductory modifier must therefore identify another score.
