Choice D does so: it compares the score for an evenly loaded panel with the score for a sharply localized one. Choices A and C make a panel the main subject, producing a comparison between a physical panel and a numerical score. Choice B inserts a conditional clause and then uses “it,” which leaves the comparison attached to a panel or its load rather than to a clearly identified score. Mentioning a lower score later does not establish the required parallel comparison at the modifier’s attachment point.

questions.passage: Elena Marwick’s 1941 autobiographical narrative *Beneath the Footlights* recounts her work repairing theatrical lighting. Marwick heightens suspense by foregrounding an involuntary bodily reaction to an approaching disturbance, writing _____.
questions.question: Which quotation from *Beneath the Footlights* most effectively supports this claim?

choices.A: “After carefully inspecting the switchboard, the electrician instructed our manager to keep the remaining members of the crew at the theater. Meanwhile, he would take three of his assistants to the harbor warehouse, where the replacement lamps had been stored.”
choices.B: “Something scraped along the unlit catwalk. My fingers stiffened around the wrench; crouching beneath the rail, I felt each breath catch. The scraping stopped directly overhead. Would my teeth betray me, knocking together in that awful silence?”
choices.C: “When the orchestra finally began, delight passed from row to row. Even the ushers, ordinarily so solemn, hummed along; from behind the curtain I could hear the audience laughing.”
choices.D: “A fortnight before the opening, our electrician returned from Trieste. The manager sent two apprentices to meet him, and presently a message arrived: every technician was to assemble in the rehearsal room.”

questions.explanation: B makes the narrator’s physical response the source of suspense: stiffened fingers, interrupted breathing, and chattering teeth convey fear while the unexplained sound approaches and stops overhead. C conveys communal pleasure rather than apprehension. D relates preparations for a meeting; its chronological sequence does not emphasize a frightened bodily reaction. A reports practical instructions and a destination, supplying neither an immediate threat nor the narrator’s physiological response.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Bellariva Manuscript Repository occupies a converted observatory in Trieste.
• Its collection is among the region’s most extensive holdings of handwritten documents.
• Humidity is higher in the repository’s western vault than in its eastern vault.
• The eastern vault contains nautical logbooks known as the Vescari Registers.
• The eastern vault also contains illuminated chant manuscripts known as the Orsena Antiphonals.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the Vescari Registers and the Orsena Antiphonals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The Orsena Antiphonals are a group of illuminated manuscripts containing chants that belong to the collections held by a cultural repository located in Trieste.
choices.B: Housed in a converted Trieste observatory, the Bellariva Manuscript Repository maintains an unusually extensive collection of handwritten documents.
choices.C: Among the handwritten documents in the Bellariva Manuscript Repository are nautical logbooks called the Vescari Registers.
choices.D: Although their subject matter differs, the Vescari Registers and the Orsena Antiphonals are both kept in the repository’s less humid eastern vault.

questions.explanation: D explicitly identifies a shared attribute of both collections: their location in the eastern vault. Calling that vault less humid is also supported by the east–west comparison. B describes the institution without comparing the collections. A gives information only about the antiphonals. C gives information only about the registers. Those statements are consistent with the notes, but none accomplishes the requested comparison.

questions.passage: After receiving the Mirel Prize for Conservation and the Halden Medal, cartographic historian Soraya Pell devised a multispectral process that allows archivists _____ erased annotations beneath successive layers of varnish, even when the surviving marks are narrower than one twentieth of a millimeter.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: examining
choices.B: who examine
choices.C: to examine
choices.D: will examine

questions.explanation: C completes the construction “allows archivists to examine”: allows takes an object, archivists, followed here by an infinitive expressing the permitted action. B supplies a relative clause modifying archivists and leaves the intended allows construction incomplete. A substitutes an -ing form for the required infinitive. D introduces a finite verb without a grammatical connection to allows; “allows archivists will examine” cannot form the intended clause.

questions.passage:
Items acquired by the Vardena Technical Archive, by document length, 2011–2014 (in thousands)
The Vardena Technical Archive held slightly more than 1.4 million documents in 2022. To trace the history of its holdings, a researcher needs the number of acquired documents containing 13–18 pages in 2014. In thousands, that number was _____.
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
questions.explanation: A is the entry at the intersection of Survey dossiers (13–18 pages) and 2014, the first numerical column. B uses the correct document class but takes the 2013 figure. C does not appear in the table and cannot be established from the stated information. D takes the 2014 entry for Field primers, which have 6–9 pages rather than 13–18. The archive’s later total is background information, not the requested historical count.

questions.passage: A 2019 investigation of the portable Eastmere organ revealed an unexpected mechanism. During abrupt changes in air pressure, the instrument’s _____ the hinged components that regulate airflow—shifted into a staggered arrangement, stabilizing the pitch before listeners could detect a fluctuation.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: valves;
choices.B: valves
choices.C: valves—
choices.D: valves,

questions.explanation: C supplies the opening dash needed to match the dash after airflow. The words between them explain what the valves are, while the main clause remains “the instrument’s valves shifted.” D opens that explanation with a comma but closes it with a dash, creating mismatched delimiters. B leaves the explanatory noun phrase unmarked. A uses a semicolon before a phrase that is not an independent clause.

questions.passage: The annual Orren Translation Prize uses a plurality rule. Rather than requiring support from more than half the judging panel, the rule awards the prize to whichever submission receives the largest number of votes. _____ when several entries divide the panel’s preferences, the winning translation may have been selected by fewer than half the judges.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Accordingly,
choices.B: Likewise,
choices.C: Furthermore,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

questions.explanation: A introduces a consequence of the stated rule: the largest share can be less than half when votes are divided among several entries. D incorrectly signals a result that conflicts with the rule. B would introduce a comparable situation rather than this rule’s implication. C signals an additional point but does not express the causal relationship that makes the final sentence a deduction from the preceding explanation.

questions.passage: The Fenrill Archive, whose holdings chiefly concerned glassmaking, was one of several centrally managed _____ by permitting these institutions to maintain independent catalogs, curator Alina Serrat probably accelerated the shared catalog’s eventual dissolution.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: archives assembled around regional specialties,
choices.B: archives. Assembled, around regional specialties,
choices.C: archives; assembled around regional specialties
choices.D: archives assembled around regional specialties;

questions.explanation: D attaches the restrictive modifier assembled around regional specialties to archives, then uses a semicolon between two independent clauses. The second clause’s subject and verb are curator Alina Serrat and accelerated; its opening by phrase does not make it dependent. C places the semicolon before a participial modifier and strands that modifier in an ill-formed clause. B similarly creates a fragment beginning Assembled. A joins the independent clauses with only a comma.

questions.passage: Astronomer Leander Voss is principally remembered for the 1928 Meridian Observatory affair, in which fabricated measurement logs implicated assistants Celia Renk and Tomas Ardell as well as Voss himself. <u>Yet this reputation compresses a more complicated career: Voss also devised a reliable method of calibrating photographic plates, and his proposed network of remote observation stations anticipated the system that astronomer Inez Halberg implemented three decades later.</u>
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It weighs the respective scientific contributions made by two different astronomers in an attempt to determine which astronomer made the more consequential contribution.
choices.B: It introduces evidence that a familiar assessment of a scientist leaves out significant aspects of that scientist’s career.
choices.C: It explains the scholarly practices that cause a scientist’s contributions to be overlooked.
choices.D: It substantiates the account of misconduct involving a scientist and the scientist’s collaborators.

questions.explanation: B captures the sentence’s corrective function: after identifying Voss with misconduct, the text gives contributions that complicate that association. C incorrectly supplies an explanation for historians’ behavior; no such behavior is analyzed. D mistakes the positive achievements for evidence of the scandal. A overreads the mention of Halberg, whose work establishes that Voss’s proposal anticipated a later system rather than introducing a comparison of the two astronomers’ overall importance.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Reinforcement lattices are internal frameworks made up of connected struts.
• Struts distribute mechanical loads through a structure.
• The Kelven bridge and the Aster span both use reinforcement lattices.
• Each standard lattice module in the Kelven bridge contains eighty-eight struts.
• Each standard lattice module in the Aster span contains forty-eight struts.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two bridges. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Struts within the Kelven bridge’s reinforcement lattice help carry mechanical loads through the structure.
choices.B: The Aster span incorporates lattice modules, each containing forty-eight struts that distribute mechanical loads.
choices.C: Both the Kelven bridge and the Aster span distribute structural loads through the use of internal frameworks that consist of connected struts.
choices.D: Although both bridges use reinforcement lattices, a standard Kelven module has eighty-eight struts, whereas an Aster module has forty-eight.

questions.explanation: D directly contrasts the bridges using the corresponding module counts, eighty-eight and forty-eight. B describes only the Aster span, leaving the reader without the Kelven figure needed for comparison. C emphasizes a shared structural feature rather than a difference. A explains a function of one bridge’s struts but offers no contrasting information about the other.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Cipherpath is a 1998 authentication design by cryptographer Nadira Velten.
• It records an access phrase as a sequence of electrical pulses.
• Arcmesh is a 2016 authentication design by systems engineer Pavel Orsen.
• It records a nonlinguistic geometric pattern as a sequence of electrical pulses.
• Pulse-based encoding became common in industrial signaling in the 1940s and declined there in the 1980s.
• Security researchers began adopting pulse-based encoding in the 1990s and continue to investigate it.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two authentication designs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Velten and Orsen use pulse-based encoding in distinct ways, illustrating the medium’s versatility for authentication.
choices.B: Used to encode phrases, geometric patterns, and industrial signals, electrical pulses have supported numerous applications.
choices.C: Both designs postdate pulse-based encoding’s principal period of use in industrial signaling, although Cipherpath appeared earlier.
choices.D: Cipherpath records a phrase as electrical pulses, while Arcmesh records a geometric pattern using pulses.

questions.explanation: D specifies the relevant contrast: linguistic information in Cipherpath and a nonlinguistic pattern in Arcmesh. C chiefly establishes a shared historical relationship to industrial signaling; its incidental chronology does not foreground how the designs differ. B surveys applications rather than focusing the comparison on the two designs. A asserts that the uses differ but does not identify the difference documented in the notes.

questions.passage: Dense shelving generally preserves fragile recordings more effectively when each item has a rigid support. A padded sleeve, _____ can keep a wax cylinder from bending under the weight of neighboring cylinders, whereas an unsupported paper envelope offers little resistance to that pressure.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: for example,
choices.B: moreover,
choices.C: meanwhile,
choices.D: however,

questions.explanation: A presents the sleeve’s performance as a concrete illustration of the preceding general statement about support. D would imply that the sleeve contradicts that statement, although it supports it. B would introduce another general consideration instead of labeling the specific instance. C suggests simultaneous developments or a separate comparison, neither of which explains why the sleeve is introduced at this point.

questions.passage: To trace how recipes migrated across maritime trade routes, acclaimed _____ Nerea Solven compares shipping ledgers, household inventories, and annotated cookbooks.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: culinary historian and 2014 Rassel Research Award recipient
choices.B: culinary historian and 2014 Rassel Research Award recipient—
choices.C: culinary historian and 2014 Rassel Research Award recipient,
choices.D: culinary historian, and 2014 Rassel Research Award recipient

questions.explanation: A keeps the coordinated professional descriptions directly connected to the name they identify. No comma or dash belongs between recipient and Nerea Solven in this construction. C and B incorrectly separate the descriptions from the name. D places an unnecessary comma between culinary historian and the coordinated phrase 2014 Rassel Research Award recipient; neither description is an independent clause.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Some early copperplate charts contain narrow blank bands between otherwise densely engraved coastal regions.
• Print historian Marta Deren proposes the plate-abrasion theory to account for the bands.
• According to Deren, repeated contact between adjacent engraving tools wore away fine lines at the boundaries.
• Cartographic scholar Olek Varn proposes the boundary-reservation theory.
• According to Varn, engravers noticing densely crowded neighboring regions deliberately stopped short of those regions.
questions.question: The student wants to compare the causes of the blank bands proposed in the two theories. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Varn’s boundary-reservation theory differs from the plate-abrasion theory proposed by Deren.
choices.B: Repeated contact between engraving tools could erase lines, according to Deren, producing bands between densely engraved regions.
choices.C: Both Deren and Varn offer accounts of the narrow blank bands found on certain early copperplate charts.
choices.D: Deren blames tool abrasion for the blank bands; Varn argues that engravers deliberately left them.

questions.explanation: D compares the proposed mechanisms, distinguishing accidental removal of lines from deliberate avoidance of adjacent engraving. C identifies the theories’ common explanatory target without comparing causes. A states that the theories differ but leaves that difference unspecified. B explains Deren’s mechanism alone and therefore does not provide the requested comparison with Varn’s.

questions.passage: The introduction of open auditions in 1932 radically altered the Virelle Chamber Company’s recruitment. Some historians contend that the policy fundamentally _____ the organization: for the first time, performers without personal ties to its directors could compete for every vacancy.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: inundated
choices.B: circumvented
choices.C: reconfigured
choices.D: impeded

questions.explanation: C means changed the arrangement or structure of something, fitting a policy that altered who could enter the company. B means went around or avoided the organization, which does not describe the policy’s internal effect. A means overwhelmed it with an excessive quantity, but no such excess is established. D means obstructed it, conflicting with the described expansion of recruitment opportunities.

questions.passage: Although repairs to precision instruments were routinely demonstrated in eighteenth-century workshops, few makers described those procedures in print before Lucan Vey began publishing illustrated manuals. _____ his books contain the earliest documented descriptions of more than 1,400 workshop operations, including “wheel indexing” in his 1726 guide *The Dividing Bench*; a contemporary accordingly called him “the craft’s first systematic chronicler.”
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Even so,
choices.B: In addition,
choices.C: On the other hand,
choices.D: In fact,

questions.explanation: D introduces specific evidence reinforcing the claim that Vey pioneered printed descriptions of workshop procedures. A and C would signal a qualification or contrast, although the evidence supports the claim. B marks simple addition; the numerous earliest documented descriptions have the more precise role of substantiating and emphasizing Vey’s pioneering contribution.

questions.passage: The 2018 climate atlas *Currents at the Margin* established atmospheric researcher Ilara Sen as a leading interpreter of coastal weather. <u>By incorporating measurements from small island stations, including those on Sen’s home island of Meredi, the atlas also brought frequently overlooked communities into regional climate analysis.</u> Sen was not alone in widening that coverage: oceanographer Davi Orell’s respected 2015 report *Tides Beyond the Grid* examined weather records from the remote Selven archipelago.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?

choices.A: It questions an assumption that Sen’s atlas chiefly recounts her own experiences.
choices.B: It predicts that mainland researchers will soon adopt Sen’s approach to climate analysis.
choices.C: It raises a question about the atlas’s popularity among readers uninterested in weather.
choices.D: It explains the importance of the atlas’s inclusion of island measurements.

questions.explanation: D identifies the sentence’s stated significance: the measurements give overlooked communities a place in regional analysis. B turns a description of an existing contribution into an unsupported prediction. A invents a biographical assumption and a challenge to it. C introduces a question about readership that the sentence neither asks nor attempts to answer.

questions.passage: The Lethora Conservatory classifies seventeen-interval tuning as “experimental,” reserving “established” for systems already widespread in performance. Musicologists Anika Verran and Celso Marr caution, however, that these categories describe present conditions. New instrument designs can make formerly impractical tunings usable; changes in performance practice can also bring an unfamiliar system into ordinary use. Applied to Lethora’s classification, their observations suggest that _____.
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: even without changes in instruments or performance practice, seventeen-interval tuning will inevitably become widespread.
choices.B: distinguishing established from experimental systems remains helpful for other tunings but has no practical value at present for seventeen-interval tuning.
choices.C: seventeen-interval tuning was formerly common at Lethora but disappeared when competing systems were introduced.
choices.D: Lethora’s classification of seventeen-interval tuning may be justified under current conditions yet cease to fit conditions in the future.

questions.explanation: D follows from the categories’ dependence on current usage and the possibility that usage will change. C invents a prior history not supplied by the passage. A replaces possible changes with an inevitable outcome independent of those changes. B asserts that the distinction is already inappropriate for this tuning, whereas the text only shows why a presently appropriate classification could later become inappropriate.

questions.passage: Researchers at the Darsen Map Center consult millions of digitized chart pages each year. _____ the center’s technicians regularly service its thirty-six document scanners, aiming to keep the production of those widely used images consistent and reliable.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: Conversely,
choices.D: As an alternative,

questions.explanation: A connects extensive use of the images with the maintenance undertaken to ensure their reliable production. C suggests opposition, although the maintenance responds to that use. B presents an example of the preceding claim, but servicing scanners is not an instance of researchers consulting pages. D would introduce a substitute course of action; maintenance is described as support for, rather than an alternative to, the digitization service.

questions.passage: How should the catalog code “Avelti” be pronounced? Under archivist Eren Varda’s 2011 transcription scheme, the letter pair -ti represents an -sh sound; consequently, the code’s name _____ rendered as “Avelsh” in reading guides.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: is routinely
choices.B: have been routinely
choices.C: are routinely
choices.D: are being routinely

questions.explanation: A supplies a singular verb agreeing with the singular subject name. The possessive code’s modifies name and does not change its number. B uses the plural auxiliary have; the singular form would be has. C and D both use plural are. The presence of guides later in the sentence cannot determine the verb’s number because guides is not the subject.

questions.passage: As archival historian Renata Neris explains, growing demand for shipbuilding plans attributed to particular coastal schools, such as the Velsari drafting tradition of Sestrena, created pressure to substantiate those attributions. _____ the Maritime Records Council introduced the CRP seal, certifying that a plan’s provenance and drafting methods conformed to the named school’s documented practices.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Despite this,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: As a result,
choices.D: For the same reason,

questions.explanation: C presents the certification seal as a response to the need for substantiated claims. B signals opposition rather than the stated problem–response relationship. A suggests the seal was introduced despite the demand, reversing the relationship. D implies another action prompted by a previously identified reason; the passage instead moves from a newly described need to its direct consequence.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Maia Dorell’s 2014 novel *The Porcelain Room*. Selin and her cousins are visiting a conservator’s workshop in Ravena.
At the end of the passageway, daylight caught in the cabinet doors and scattered pale rectangles across the floor. Selin had known the workshop since childhood, yet this specific cabinet never failed to arrest her. She beckoned the others closer. “Look here,” she whispered; behind the glass stood the cracked blue bowl her aunt had restored.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does “specific” most nearly mean?

choices.A: Merely imagined
choices.B: Individually identified
choices.C: Especially animated
choices.D: Accurately measured

questions.explanation: B fits the reference to one particular cabinet among the workshop’s furnishings. Specific identifies which cabinet Selin notices; it does not describe that cabinet’s dimensions. D therefore supplies the wrong sense of precision. C concerns liveliness rather than identification. A conflicts with the cabinet’s physical presence and the visible bowl behind its doors.

questions.passage: Gravity-fed grain mills draw kernels through rotating sieves before milling them into flour. Each day, such mills can process up to 24 percent of their hopper’s total holding capacity. The Varena mill, with capacity for 8,500 kilograms, is substantial by local standards but modest within this category. The much larger Rendell mill holds 520,000 kilograms and can process as much as 124,800 kilograms in a day.
questions.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be concluded about the two mills’ daily grain processing?

choices.A: Rendell can process a greater quantity of grain in a day than Varena can.
choices.B: Rendell’s grain consumption has reduced the amount of grain available to Varena.
choices.C: Varena is less likely than Rendell to process grain using rotating sieves.
choices.D: Both of the mills can process as much as 124,800 kilograms in a day.

questions.explanation: A follows from the common 24-percent capacity limit: Varena’s maximum is 2,040 kilograms, while Rendell’s is 124,800 kilograms. D applies Rendell’s maximum to Varena despite their different capacities. C invents a difference in operating method; both belong to the category described. B invents competition for a limited supply, which the text never discusses.

questions.passage: Archivists authenticated the earliest Velsera shipping ledger in 1863, the year in which the document first came to scholarly attention. _____ the authenticity of the Ordan register remained unresolved for seventy-six years after its initial discovery.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In much the same way,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: By comparison,
choices.D: Therefore,

questions.explanation: C contrasts immediate authentication with a seventy-six-year delay. D suggests that the first document’s authentication caused the second document’s delay, which is unsupported. B incorrectly makes the second timeline an example of the first. A signals similarity despite the sharply different elapsed times.

questions.passage: Many present-day island cartographers deliberately build charts around inherited navigational conventions. Kira Nessel, for example, organizes bearings using the landmark sequences preserved in Selvari pilots’ manuals. An earlier generation of island cartographers, including Tomas Edrin, generally adopted international geodetic conventions, which mainland survey offices also used, instead of those locally inherited systems. Consequently, identifying an Edrin-era chart as island cartography typically _____.
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: depends on knowing who made the chart rather than recognizing distinctive local conventions in its design.
choices.B: gives the chartmaker’s life greater weight than the chart’s technical quality.
choices.C: implies that the social and cultural community to which the chartmaker belonged had no influence whatsoever on the resulting chart.
choices.D: conceals the island origins of conventions now treated as international standards.

questions.explanation: A follows because the earlier charts’ design conventions were shared with mainland offices; those conventions alone would not establish the makers’ island identity. B confuses classification with an evaluation of technical merit. D asserts that international conventions originated on the islands, which the text does not claim. C overstates the point: using shared conventions does not demonstrate that community identity had no influence.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• *Channels Under Pressure* is a book by hydraulic engineer Veda Orsin.
• The book examines several strategies for managing river flow.
• Chapter 6, “Retentive Design,” defines an approach that stores excess water upstream.
• Chapter 7, “Distributive Design,” defines an approach that diverts excess water into secondary channels.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the order in which the topics appear. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Orsin defines upstream water storage in the chapter “Retentive Design.”
choices.B: Orsin provides definitions for both the diversion of water into secondary channels and the upstream storage of excess water.
choices.C: Orsin examines multiple river-management strategies in *Channels Under Pressure*.
choices.D: Before defining diversion into secondary channels, Orsin explains an approach that retains excess water upstream.

questions.explanation: D accurately makes the Chapter 6 topic precede the Chapter 7 topic, even though it mentions the later topic first in its sentence. C summarizes the book’s scope without giving an order. A identifies only one chapter. B names both approaches but gives no temporal or organizational relationship between them; the order of their mention cannot substitute for an explicit statement of chapter sequence.

questions.passage: The nineteenth-century Valeir specimen collection helped establish the classification of several prehistoric birds. Paleontologists nevertheless distinguish between *Peloravis*, represented by specimens from Oligocene deposits dating to roughly 34–23 million years ago, and *Orithena*, supposedly found in older Eocene deposits but disputed as an actual genus. *Orithena* appears in the *Valeir Catalog*, compiled between 1806 and 1812; that entry rests on collectors’ transmitted accounts rather than the physical specimens supporting the catalog’s later *Peloravis* entry.
questions.question: According to the text, how do paleontologists’ views of the two genera differ?

choices.A: They accept *Peloravis* as an actual genus but differ over whether *Orithena* existed.
choices.B: They consider the catalog’s evidence for *Orithena* stronger than its evidence for *Peloravis*.
choices.C: They find transmitted accounts of *Peloravis* more persuasive than equivalent accounts of *Orithena*.
choices.D: They agree that *Orithena* first appeared substantially later than *Peloravis*.

questions.explanation: A states the explicit contrast between an accepted, specimen-supported genus and one whose actuality is disputed. B reverses the evidentiary relationship. D contradicts the stated ordering of the deposits and invents agreement about the disputed genus. C incorrectly treats the evidence for both genera as transmitted accounts; *Peloravis* is supported by physical specimens.

questions.passage: Using polarized-light tomography, conservators mapped the alignment of microscopic mineral needles in vessel KR-62, a fired-clay jar from the Neral workshop district. Such needles occur throughout the walls of these vessels. The map unexpectedly showed no consistent orientation; based on other jars from neighboring workshop districts, the team had anticipated a predominantly aligned arrangement.
questions.question: According to the text, what surprised the researchers about the mapping of KR-62?

choices.A: It showed that the needles lacked a consistent alignment.
choices.B: It revealed fewer mineral needles than the researchers had expected.
choices.C: It reproduced the alignment typically observed in neighboring districts’ jars.
choices.D: It demonstrated that earlier maps of the jar were inaccurate.

questions.explanation: A states the observed mismatch with the researchers’ expectation of a predominantly aligned arrangement. C describes the expected result rather than the unexpected result. D asserts a problem with earlier maps, which are never mentioned. B substitutes a finding about quantity for the actual finding about orientation.

questions.passage: The Fenera pottery district uses highly standardized pressing frames and relatively uniform clay mixtures, yet its 2019 vessel-cracking rate was 7.8 percent. Dovar, which has less standardized frames and more variable clay mixtures, recorded only 1.2 percent. Comparisons of this kind prompted speculation that standardized frames prevent adjustments needed to avoid cracks. To test the hypothesis, materials scientist Elda Meren’s team examined frame standardization, clay variability, and cracking in 164 districts. Their analysis found that greater frame standardization, when paired with low clay variability, reduced cracking, suggesting that _____.
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: Fenera and Dovar probably differed more in frame standardization than the published records indicate.
choices.B: treating Fenera’s and Dovar’s cracking rates as proof of an inherent disadvantage of standardized frames would be unwarranted.
choices.C: the observed disparity in cracking rates between Fenera and Dovar is attributable to differences in clay variability rather than differences in frame standardization.
choices.D: measures of cracking systematically exaggerate failure rates in districts using standardized frames.

questions.explanation: B correctly limits the inference from two examples: the broader analysis shows standardized frames can reduce cracking under the specified clay conditions. D invents measurement bias. C identifies a definite cause of the two districts’ disparity, which the study does not establish. A invents inaccurate records of standardization. The evidence undermines the proposed general disadvantage without explaining every local difference.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Mira Sevran’s 1946 play *The Parcel Room*. Rellan and Iska meet on a railway platform.
RELLAN: I’m not waiting for a passenger train. The morning freight brings the replacement clocks, and I’ve promised to have the station’s old mechanisms exchanged before supper.
ISKA: Exchanged before supper? The freight will be late. Whenever I undertake anything, the timetable comes apart just when I need it; I’ll be standing here until the lamps are lit.
RELLAN: And if it arrived this instant, I suspect you’d bring an hourglass with the neck stopped up, Iska, so that time itself could furnish you a grievance.
questions.question: Based on the text, what does Rellan most likely believe about Iska?

choices.A: Iska can assist with replacing the station’s clocks.
choices.B: Iska will discover a reason for dissatisfaction regardless of what happens.
choices.C: Iska is primarily worried that Rellan has planned the work inadequately.
choices.D: Iska’s judgments about train delays are usually inaccurate.

questions.explanation: B captures Rellan’s exaggerated suggestion that Iska would manufacture a grievance even if the freight arrived immediately. D is narrower: Rellan criticizes Iska’s habitual complaining, not specifically the accuracy of forecasts. A offers a practical role never discussed. C attributes a concern about Rellan’s preparations that Iska does not express; Iska complains about what happens to Iska personally.

questions.passage: The Meren Railway Guild has an official anthem, crest, and flag, as well as an official metal: Darsen bronze. The alloy suits this designation partly because the guild’s regional foundries produce it in abundance. _____ it has considerable practical importance to the railway network, supplying bearings and fittings for many kinds of equipment.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: On the contrary,
choices.B: At that point,
choices.C: Moreover,
choices.D: Alternatively,

questions.explanation: C adds a second reason the alloy suits its designation: practical importance supplements local abundance. D presents a substitute explanation rather than an additional compatible reason. B introduces a time relationship that is absent. A implies that practical importance contradicts the alloy’s abundance, although the two claims can both support the designation.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2012, a team led by materials researcher Edra Voss measured the average thicknesses of several archival films.
• Kelvara film belongs to the cellulose-acetate category.
• Kelvara film had an average thickness of 0.26 millimeter.
• Ordelan film belongs to the polyester category.
• Ordelan film had an average thickness of 0.33 millimeter.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two films’ thicknesses. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A 2012 investigation compared several archival films, among them Kelvara and Ordelan.
choices.B: In the 2012 study, Kelvara averaged 0.26 millimeter in thickness, whereas Ordelan was thicker, averaging 0.33 millimeter.
choices.C: The cellulose-acetate film Kelvara and the polyester film Ordelan were included in a study of average thickness.
choices.D: Edra Voss’s team measured average film thicknesses, including 0.26 millimeter for Kelvara and 0.33 millimeter for Ordelan.

questions.explanation: B explicitly compares the measurements and correctly identifies Ordelan as thicker. D supplies both figures but emphasizes the research activity, leaving the comparison implicit. A names the films without their thicknesses. C distinguishes material categories, which does not fulfill the requested emphasis on thickness.

questions.passage: A 2017 report by the Merelon Instrument Consortium reviewed the availability of precision optics benches at several laboratories, including Bellariva, Torvess, and Emsford. It found an overall increase in availability between 1984 and 2014. For example, none of the three laboratories had more than seven benches in 1984, but _____.
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example across all three laboratories?

choices.A: neither Bellariva nor Emsford recorded a decline in any interval, although Torvess declined after 1994.
choices.B: by 2014, Bellariva, Torvess, and Emsford each had ten benches.
choices.C: Emsford’s net increase over the period exceeded Bellariva’s and Torvess’s respective net increases.
choices.D: Torvess went from seven benches in 1984 to ten in 2014.

questions.explanation: B supplies the later values for all three laboratories: each increased from no more than seven to ten. C correctly compares net gains but does not supply the later counts needed to complete the example across the three laboratories. D documents only Torvess’s change. A is false because Emsford fell from eleven benches in 1994 to seven in 2004; only Bellariva avoided a decline throughout the plotted intervals.

graph.caption: Precision optics benches at three laboratories, 1984–2014

questions.passage: Elise Rassel’s 2010 instructional city model *Teren* is often described as a replica. The description has some justification: many of its streets correspond to those in Rassel’s home district. It does not follow, however, that every represented building or intersection has an actual counterpart. Much of the layout was deliberately devised for training exercises. Viewers who overlook that qualification and search for ever more real-world equivalents therefore risk _____.
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: suggesting, incorrectly, that the model attracted a larger total number of visitors than it did in fact attract.
choices.B: exaggerating Rassel’s reliance on models created by earlier designers.
choices.C: understating how much Rassel’s design borrowed from actual places.
choices.D: proposing connections between the model and existing sites that the available evidence cannot support.

questions.explanation: D follows from treating deliberately devised features as if all must correspond to actual sites. C points in the opposite direction: those viewers overextend, rather than understate, real-world correspondence. A introduces visitor numbers, which are irrelevant to the qualification. B shifts to earlier designers, whose influence is not discussed.

questions.passage: Lateral firmware propagation occurs when devices exchange software modules outside the usual manufacturer-to-customer update sequence. It is common in distributed sensor networks, including the Velorin and Tessara monitoring systems. The exchanges can spread unauthorized code across otherwise isolated devices; identifying ways to block such propagation could therefore help contain network intrusions.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Lateral firmware propagation occurs more frequently than researchers initially believed.
choices.B: The public’s usual understanding of firmware propagation misrepresents its operation.
choices.C: Research into lateral firmware propagation could lead to practically useful methods of limiting intrusions.
choices.D: Recent findings concerning the process of firmware exchange undermine conclusions reached by researchers in earlier investigations.

questions.explanation: C covers both the described process and the practical value of studying how to prevent it. A invents a comparison with earlier frequency estimates. D invents a conflict between new and old research. B invents a public misconception. The passage presents a mechanism and a possible application, not revisions to previous beliefs.

questions.passage: Although the precision regulators designed by Arven Pell and Soria Kelm are used well beyond their region, they remain _____ the Neravic instrument-making tradition: both designers work within methods that extend back to the first water-driven timing mechanisms of the Vessara workshops.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: undermined by
choices.B: anticipated by
choices.C: inseparable from
choices.D: incompatible with

questions.explanation: C means closely connected in a way that cannot meaningfully be separated, fitting the regulators’ continuing relationship to an inherited technical tradition. B indicates prior prediction rather than an enduring connection. A suggests that the tradition weakens the regulators, contrary to the account of their basis in its methods. D directly contradicts that methodological continuity.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Hira Nessen’s 1943 short story “The Planet Room.”
The last school group had departed, leaving the model heavens to their own slow revolution. Above the demonstration desk, a brass globe, propped on four iron braces as broad as a carpenter’s hand, caught the remaining light. Installed twenty-nine years earlier by a clockmaker long since buried, it now seemed less an instrument than a quiet moon suspended over an empty classroom.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does “propped” most nearly mean?

choices.A: Held in position
choices.B: Regarded with affection
choices.C: Improved in design
choices.D: Protected from criticism

questions.explanation: A fits the physical relationship between the globe and its iron braces, which hold it in place. D supplies an abstract sense of defending something, not a structural function. C claims an improvement that the braces are not said to provide. B confuses the passage’s reflective tone with the literal meaning of the verb describing the globe’s support.

questions.passage: History instructor Maelen Varr wanted her seminars to require examination of evidence rather than the memorization of summary judgments. _____ she began replacing textbook recaps with workshops in which students interpreted shipping dispatches and annotated customs ledgers before drawing their own conclusions.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Even so,
choices.B: In reality,
choices.C: With that aim,
choices.D: To conclude,

questions.explanation: C links Varr’s instructional change to the goal stated immediately before it. D signals a summary or final conclusion, but the sentence introduces an action. A suggests the action runs counter to the goal, although it serves the goal. B signals a correction of an appearance or misconception; the first sentence is not presented as mistaken.

questions.passage: In the port of Vesmeri, the pilot-owned Navigators’ House uses the local fleet’s inherited seamanship practices to design training for that fleet’s crews. The cooperative school maintained by the Ordel pilots’ association takes a comparable approach. These institutions differ from commercially operated nautical schools, which usually organize courses around tourist expectations and standardized recreational sailing procedures.
questions.question: The text best supports which conclusion about the Ordel school?

choices.A: Its courses are probably designed primarily to benefit members of the local pilots’ community.
choices.B: Its courses are probably intended to reconcile the needs of commercial recreation with the inherited traditions of local pilots.
choices.C: Its courses probably combine the customary knowledge of several unrelated fleets.
choices.D: The size of its building probably restricts its ability to teach local practices.

questions.explanation: A follows from the school’s comparable approach to Navigators’ House, whose training serves the local fleet’s crews. C adds multiple fleets not mentioned in the text. D adds a physical limitation without evidence. B incorrectly treats the contrasted commercial approach as something the cooperative school seeks to combine with its own.

questions.passage: Needle and Aster are the workshop labels for two distinctive printing molds recovered from the old Renval press. After arriving at the conservation studio on September 16, 1997, conservator Celia Marden spent nearly nine months _____ the pigments still embedded in their engraved surfaces.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: are cataloging
choices.B: was cataloging
choices.C: cataloged
choices.D: cataloging

questions.explanation: D completes the construction spent nine months cataloging, in which the -ing form identifies the activity occupying that time. B and A introduce finite verb phrases that cannot attach to spent in this construction; A also uses plural are with a singular subject. C substitutes a simple past verb where the activity requires an -ing form.

questions.passage: The Vestara Book Exchange, commonly called the Night Parcel network, coordinates deliveries among independent presses. In many districts, such cooperative arrangements, in which participating presses align their dispatch schedules, _____ extensive supply chains capable of moving small print runs between distant towns.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: establish
choices.B: having established
choices.C: establishing
choices.D: to establish

questions.explanation: A provides the finite plural verb needed for the subject arrangements. The intervening clause explains those arrangements but does not provide their main predicate. C and B are participial forms, leaving the main clause without a finite verb. D is an infinitive and has the same defect. The singular Exchange in the earlier sentence is not this clause’s subject.

questions.passage: Large scientific institutions are not the only organizations that preserve systematic records. Volunteer associations also find recordkeeping useful. <u>The Neral Neighborhood Choir keeps dated notebooks of rehearsal observations to guide later performances.</u> Amateur theater groups, sometimes dismissed as informal enterprises, likewise compile detailed lighting diaries; the entries help crews reproduce effects that previously worked.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?

choices.A: It establishes that choirs are more methodical than amateur theater groups.
choices.B: It supplies a specific instance of recordkeeping by a volunteer association.
choices.C: It explains the many purposes for which scientific institutions preserve records.
choices.D: It argues that choirs preserve more records than other volunteer groups.

questions.explanation: B identifies the choir sentence as an example supporting the preceding claim about volunteer associations. D invents a comparison of record quantities. C mistakes an example outside scientific institutions for an explanation of those institutions’ practices. A invents a ranking between the choir and theater groups; the text gives parallel examples without measuring their relative methodicalness.

questions.passage: Meretine board consists of bonded layers of plant fiber. In 2020, researchers added a mineral catalyst to Dorlene, a similar composite, shortening its curing time by twenty-nine minutes. _____ Dorlene formerly required four hours and forty-seven minutes to cure; with the catalyst, it required four hours and eighteen minutes.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nonetheless,
choices.B: Conversely,
choices.C: More specifically,
choices.D: Besides,

questions.explanation: C introduces the precise before-and-after times that spell out the twenty-nine-minute reduction. D labels the figures as separate additional information rather than an elaboration of the reduction. A and B signal opposition, although the figures confirm the preceding claim. Subtracting 4:18 from 4:47 yields the stated twenty-nine minutes.

questions.passage: Market awnings in the port of Ravena follow a distinctive local design tradition. Their folding frames incorporate mechanisms inherited from regional sailmakers. Glassworkers also contributed to the tradition: the curvature of several reinforcing seams can be _____ to procedures used in the glass workshops of nearby Sorell.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: tendered
choices.B: proclaimed
choices.C: relinquished
choices.D: attributed

questions.explanation: D identifies the glassworkers’ procedures as the source of the seam design, fitting the statement that glassworkers contributed to the tradition. C means surrendered or given up, which does not express design origins. B means publicly announced, not derived from a source. A means offered formally; that action likewise does not identify the origin of the awnings’ structural feature.

questions.passage: Industrial historians once proposed that the arrival of rotary presses caused handwritten production ledgers to disappear rapidly from the Orven mills. Newly dated workshop records show, however, that the presses were installed decades before the ledgers ceased to be kept. This evidence is requiring historians to _____ their original hypothesis.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: decipher
choices.B: inaugurate
choices.C: modify
choices.D: recollect

questions.explanation: C means change or adjust, which the inconsistent chronology requires. D means recall the hypothesis, not revise it in response to contrary evidence. B means begin or introduce it, although the hypothesis already existed. A means work out its meaning; the problem concerns its accuracy rather than its intelligibility.

questions.passage: Materials scientist Eren Dask’s team analyzed response measurements and crystalline structures from 18,600 ceramic panels representing 140 formulations. Some similarities in response between formulations corresponded to similarities in crystalline structure, suggesting a structural basis for the response differences. The correspondence occurred for flexing and resonance but was strongest for fracture under abrupt temperature changes. A separate experiment found similar temperature-induced fracture behavior in formulations K-17 and R-44, suggesting that _____.
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the crystalline structures of K-17 and R-44 will become progressively less alike as time passes.
choices.B: the formulations’ similar fracture behavior may arise from a feature their crystalline structures share.
choices.C: K-17 and R-44 fracture more readily than most other formulations.
choices.D: K-17 panels individually fracture more frequently than R-44 panels do.

questions.explanation: B cautiously applies the observed structure–response association to the two formulations’ shared behavior. D contradicts the emphasis on similarity and supplies an unsupported ranking. C compares them with other formulations without evidence. A predicts future structural divergence, which neither study addresses. The evidence suggests a possible shared structural basis; it does not establish exact rates or future changes.

questions.passage: Recycled music manuscripts concealed inside old bookbindings have been identified throughout the Sorelan libraries. For discoveries made after 1975, including the 1982 Nera folio, portable imaging equipment, ultrasonic inspection, and digital contrast enhancement have enabled conservators to locate fragments before opening the bindings. Earlier finds, including the Vallin fragments uncovered around 1913, lacked those aids and were consequently much more likely to _____.
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: have occurred when a binding was opened and concealed material was exposed unintentionally.
choices.B: have been identified while the bindings remained undisturbed.
choices.C: contain unusually fine musical ornamentation.
choices.D: include rare notation from the thirteenth century.

questions.explanation: A follows from the absence of tools for finding fragments before bindings were opened: accidental exposure was comparatively more likely. B describes precisely the advance associated with later discoveries. C and D make claims about the fragments’ contents, whereas the text distinguishes the circumstances of discovery.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Most goods sold in Belsora’s harbor markets are imported, and most freight carriers there are externally owned.
• A 2018 study investigated the role of externally owned carriers in distributing locally produced and imported goods.
• Researchers cataloged items listed on those carriers’ delivery manifests.
• Merelan linen was one of twenty-one locally produced goods cataloged.
• Velthorn hinges were one of thirty-seven imported goods cataloged.
• The team concluded that externally owned carriers play an important role in distributing both groups of goods.
questions.question: The student wants to present findings from the study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Many goods sold in Belsora’s harbor markets, including Velthorn hinges, are imported.
choices.B: The researchers’ 2018 investigation listed both Merelan linen and Velthorn hinges on externally owned carriers’ delivery manifests.
choices.C: In 2018, researchers examined a collection of delivery manifests to investigate the role played by externally owned carriers in Belsora’s distribution system.
choices.D: Merelan linen was included in a 2018 study of freight distribution in Belsora.

questions.explanation: B states a specific observed result involving one local good and one imported good. C describes the purpose and method rather than what the examination found. A gives general background about the markets. D identifies an item included in the study but does not report the relevant finding about its presence on delivery manifests.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Selira Tessari (1875–1957) was a cartographic designer.
• Tessari lived and worked in Tivoli for many years.
• Tessari’s atlas *Harbors by Moonlight* appeared in 1907.
• Tessari’s atlas *The Inland Bearings* appeared in 1914.
questions.question: The student wants to indicate the order in which the two atlases appeared. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Cartographic designer Selira Tessari spent many years living and working in Tivoli.
choices.B: Tessari’s work as a cartographic designer included *Harbors by Moonlight*.
choices.C: Tessari, born in 1875, created the atlas *Harbors by Moonlight*.
choices.D: *The Inland Bearings* followed Tessari’s earlier *Harbors by Moonlight*: the atlases appeared in 1914 and 1907, respectively.

questions.explanation: D explicitly states that *The Inland Bearings* came after *Harbors by Moonlight* and assigns the dates correctly through respectively. A gives a place of residence rather than publication order. C gives a birth date and one title. B identifies a work but provides neither the second title nor a sequence.

questions.passage: Serenne’s surviving 1909 newsreels are brittle and easily scratched. Usually stored separately in isolated upland warehouses, they have rarely been examined systematically. Their preservation history is difficult to reconstruct because the repositories are so _____ major research libraries.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: far removed from
choices.B: accountable for
choices.C: saturated with
choices.D: attracted to

questions.explanation: A expresses the geographic separation that makes systematic examination difficult. C means filled with and conflicts with the described isolated repositories. D indicates attraction rather than remoteness. B means responsible for, supplying an administrative relationship rather than the location-based explanation the passage gives.

questions.passage: *Windward Measure* is a steel-and-limestone observation tower designed by engineer Yara Deren. It commemorates pioneering cartographer Celso Varr. The tower _____ on the Korell ridge, a short distance from the station where Varr prepared his first wind charts.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: are rising
choices.B: were rising
choices.C: rises
choices.D: have been rising

questions.explanation: C agrees with the singular subject tower and expresses the tower’s present location. B, D, and A use plural auxiliaries: were, have, and are. Neither the nearby station nor the earlier mention of charts changes the number of the sentence’s actual subject.

questions.passage: Illustrated navigation logs circulated in Ravess from approximately 1500 to 1790. Surviving bundles span that era, including the Ardel bundle of entries dating to about 1570, recovered in 1825, and the later Sorna bundle of entries dating to about 1690, recovered in 2007. Between roughly 1620 and 1660, Ravess navigators first developed color-coded wind roses. That innovation helps explain why evidence of such wind roses occurs in _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: bundles recovered before 2007 but not in those recovered later.
choices.B: both bundles, although the Sorna examples are more technically refined.
choices.C: the Ardel bundle, although no complete wind rose survives there.
choices.D: the Sorna bundle but not in the Ardel bundle.

questions.explanation: D aligns the evidence with the innovation’s date: Sorna’s approximately 1690 entries postdate the development, whereas Ardel’s approximately 1570 entries predate it. B and C incorrectly place evidence in the earlier bundle. A confuses the dates of modern recovery with the dates when the entries were made; recovery chronology does not explain whether navigators had developed the technique.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Meroven panels are construction sheets containing silicon dioxide, a stiffening ingredient.
• Every 100 grams of Meroven panel contains 18 grams of silicon dioxide.
• Some workshops manufacture silicon dioxide themselves, but the Ordel plant cannot.
• The Ordel plant obtains silicon dioxide from supplied materials, including mineral products.
• Silicon dioxide is also called silica.
questions.question: The student wants to provide an example of a construction material containing silica. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Some workshops can manufacture silica, unlike the Ordel plant.
choices.B: The Ordel plant sources silicon dioxide from supplied materials rather than manufacturing it.
choices.C: Silicon dioxide is an ingredient used for stiffening that the Ordel plant must obtain from external suppliers.
choices.D: Meroven panels are a construction material containing silica, the substance also known as silicon dioxide.

questions.explanation: D identifies the construction material and connects silica with the silicon dioxide the notes say it contains. B and A contrast sources or production capabilities but name no example of a construction material. C explains procurement and function without identifying the required example.

questions.passage: The Adern control unit, with 54 watt-hours of reserve battery capacity, and the Veltis unit, with 12 watt-hours, operate in the same depot as the Rensel monitor, which sounds an alert when it detects an approaching interruption in the power supply. Engineer Mira Taren’s team reasoned that lower reserve capacity makes units more vulnerable to interruptions. They therefore hypothesized an inverse relationship between reserve capacity and sensitivity to warning alerts from neighboring equipment.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the team’s hypothesis?

choices.A: Veltis units entered protective mode both when the Rensel alert was played and when random control noise was played.
choices.B: Several units with less reserve capacity than Adern responded to the alert, but none with less reserve capacity than Veltis responded.
choices.C: Veltis units entered protective mode when the Rensel alert was played, whereas Adern units did not.
choices.D: Only units with greater reserve capacity than Adern entered protective mode when the alert was played.

questions.explanation: C shows the lower-capacity unit responding to the warning when the higher-capacity unit does not, directly supporting greater sensitivity at lower capacity. A fails to distinguish a warning response from a general noise response. D reverses the predicted relationship. B excludes the lowest-capacity units from responding, also working against the inverse relationship the hypothesis predicts.

questions.passage: Although the Velsara Engineering Board attempted to _____ Edda Taren’s maintenance bulletin, restricting its circulation to a few supervisors, unauthorized printouts continued to pass privately between workshop crews.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: procure
choices.B: appraise
choices.C: curtail
choices.D: reproduce

questions.explanation: C means reduce or restrict, fitting the board’s effort to limit the bulletin’s circulation despite continuing private distribution. D means reproduce and would work against that effort. A means obtain, not restrict distribution. B means evaluate; evaluation alone does not express the attempted limitation described by the sentence.

questions.passage: Reconstructing a torn player-piano roll is an _____ undertaking: weeks, and sometimes months, of close inspection and physically tiring work at the restoration bench may be needed to recover the pattern of its perforations.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: expeditious
choices.B: arduous
choices.C: inexpensive
choices.D: ordinary

questions.explanation: B means demanding sustained effort, matching the prolonged, physically tiring work. A means quick or efficiently accomplished and conflicts with the described duration. C concerns cost, which the passage does not establish. D concerns how usual the task is, not its difficulty; the explanatory clause gives evidence of effort rather than frequency.

questions.passage: Meteorological analyst Anira Venn produces annotated weather atlases. She generally _____ them from station logs and satellite observations.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: to be compiling
choices.B: compiling
choices.C: compiles
choices.D: to compile

questions.explanation: C supplies the finite verb that the independent clause with subject She requires. D and A are infinitives, so neither completes that clause. B is an -ing form without an auxiliary such as is. Generally describes a habitual activity, which the simple present compiles expresses naturally.

questions.passage: Maritime historians Veda Marren and Olek Senn contributed their expertise to the *Coastal Exchange Atlas*, a digital resource that, _____ shipping manifests and port diagrams, charts the development of particular trade routes, including the Velsari circuit and the Naroven passage.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: combining
choices.B: combines
choices.C: has combined
choices.D: is combining

questions.explanation: A creates a participial phrase, set off by commas, explaining how the resource charts the routes. The relative clause already has its finite verb, charts. B, D, and C add another finite verb phrase without a coordinating conjunction, producing an ungrammatical sequence of predicates inside that clause.

questions.passage:
Text 1
Efforts to sort recipes automatically into culinary traditions have yielded unreliable results. More fundamentally, labels for culinary traditions may be too disputed and reductive to be useful. In their analysis of the Varela recipe collection, food historians Anira Pell and Tomas Neri argue that affinities among recipes are better understood through dimensions other than inherited cuisine labels.
Text 2
Orven fermented-rye broths share ingredient proportions and flavor profiles with Selari smoked-buckwheat soups. Classification software often struggles with similarities of this kind. Rena Solven’s team addressed the problem by converting chemical flavor profiles into images and comparing the images’ features computationally. The method could improve culinary classification, providing substantial benefits to users.
questions.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to Text 2’s claim about the potential benefits of Solven’s research?

choices.A: By emphasizing that further technical research will probably improve automatic classification considerably
choices.B: By arguing that some culinary traditions are easier for software to distinguish than others
choices.C: By maintaining that cuisine labels may not be the most useful framework for understanding recipes
choices.D: By noting that diners do not necessarily enjoy every dish assigned to a cuisine they prefer

questions.explanation: C applies Text 1’s central objection: improving classification accuracy does not establish that the categories themselves are useful. A accepts a technical advance without addressing that objection. B focuses on relative ease of recognition rather than category usefulness. D introduces diners’ preferences, which neither text discusses. Text 1 questions the framework even if Solven’s method improves its operation.

questions.passage: Hydrologist Mara Nellen has _____ mapping subterranean waterways across markedly different geological settings. Her widely admired surveys of the Ardel limestone system and the basalt passages beneath Lake Verena exemplify that established expertise.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: earned a name for
choices.B: accepted a requirement for
choices.C: posed a question about
choices.D: raised an objection to

questions.explanation: A means become known for an activity, fitting the admired surveys that exemplify Nellen’s expertise. D suggests a complaint about mapping, not accomplishment in it. B suggests an obligation, which does not explain the established reputation. C suggests uncertainty or inquiry about mapping rather than the demonstrated skill emphasized by the examples.

questions.passage: Municipal consultation panels such as the Velsora Forum, established in 2007, and the Darven Assembly, established in 2013, borrow familiar procedures to make participants feel secure. Features such as orderly speaking turns can _____ that confidence. Yet a panel that imitates a courtroom too closely may enter an “authority trap”: its procedures unintentionally unsettle participants who mistake voluntary consultation for compulsory adjudication.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: constrain
choices.B: attenuate
choices.C: repudiate
choices.D: bolster

questions.explanation: D means strengthen or support, matching the procedures’ intended contribution to confidence. B means weaken, contrary to the positive role assigned to those features. C means reject or disavow, which does not describe increasing confidence. A means limit or restrict. The later caution distinguishes excessive imitation from the ordinary features’ supportive effect; it does not make the earlier effect negative.

questions.passage: Drafting teams and instrument-calibration teams are major tenants in converted industrial studios, including the Sorelan complex in Ravess. To investigate their choices of workspace, researcher Ilara Venn’s team examined site locations and daytime brightness during the busiest production quarter. Drafting teams preferred brighter studios; calibration teams did not show that preference. The team concluded that renovations increasing daytime brightness during that quarter would be less likely to _____.
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: decrease the appeal of studios to both team types than to increase their appeal to both.
choices.B: attract calibration teams than to attract drafting teams.
choices.C: improve the longevity of drafting teams’ equipment than to attract more drafting teams.
choices.D: attract tenants from outside the industrial-studio sector than to attract either of the two team types.

questions.explanation: B directly applies the differing preferences: added brightness supplies an attraction for drafting teams that the calibration teams did not demonstrate. C introduces equipment longevity, which was not studied. D generalizes to other tenants without data. A treats both groups as sharing a positive response, contrary to the distinction that supports the researchers’ conclusion.

questions.passage:
Days per year with a detectable calibration tone at three receivers
Receivers operating at gains near or above 30 decibels, such as the Felerin unit at Havren Laboratory, often detect faint calibration tones during observation campaigns. Detection duration depends on several factors, including background noise, antenna geometry, and signal power. Electrical engineer Sarina Pell nevertheless claims that a receiver with higher gain will typically detect a calibration tone on more days per year.
questions.question: Which choice best describes data from the table that support Pell’s claim?

choices.A: Talren detected the tone on 101 days in 1987 and 128 days in 2012.
choices.B: Velsin detected the tone on 218 days in 1987 and 179 days in 2012.
choices.C: Velsin’s measured gain exceeded that of Orvena, but Velsin generally detected the tone on a smaller number of days during each year.
choices.D: Velsin’s gain exceeded Orvena’s, and Velsin detected the tone on more days in five of the six years shown.

questions.explanation: D relates the claimed predictor, gain, to the outcome, detection days: 42.6 exceeds 28.4, and Velsin’s count exceeds Orvena’s except in 2007 (163 versus 165). That five-of-six pattern supports the qualified word typically without asserting an exceptionless rule. C reverses the observed comparison. B and A compare years within one receiver; neither establishes a relationship between different gains and detection duration.

questions.passage: The Velsar Festival is now associated almost exclusively with orchestral performances, but music was originally _____ its principal purpose: demonstrating new scientific instruments to prospective buyers. Only after the concerts attracted unexpectedly large audiences did organizers make them the festival’s centerpiece.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: subsidiary to
choices.B: essential to
choices.C: removed by
choices.D: replicated within

questions.explanation: A means secondary to or less important than, fitting the contrast between music’s original supporting role and its later central role. D describes duplication rather than relative importance. C implies removal, although concerts remained part of the event. B asserts necessity rather than the hierarchy established by principal purpose and the later shift to centerpiece.

questions.passage: Survey projects can be classified according to who supplies their records. The Velnic Census, which accepts observations from the public, is classified as _____ other projects, including the Privan Inventory, are classified as closed because only authorized staff may submit observations.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: participatory for instance,
choices.B: participatory; for instance,
choices.C: participatory, for instance,
choices.D: participatory, for instance;

questions.explanation: B places a semicolon between independent clauses and sets off the introductory phrase for instance with a comma. D puts the semicolon after the introductory phrase instead of between the clauses. A provides no proper boundary after the first clause. C joins independent clauses using commas alone. The second clause illustrates the broader classification system, not the participatory category specifically.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Rhea Taren’s 1937 short story “The Ledger Kitchen.”
Most suppers served in vanished households (apart from those whose recipes still circulate among neighbors) survive as little more than entries in a ledger. They do not return to us as evenings actually lived. What a menu and an inventory disclose may be exact: the dishes, their quantities, the vessels in which they were served. Yet such knowledge resembles a potter’s measurements of a bowl; every dimension is recoverable, while the warmth of the bowl in someone’s hands remains beyond the figures.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Precise measurements of pottery are more useful than descriptions of how pottery feels.
choices.B: Accounts of meals preserved in neighborhood traditions should be recorded as fact even when their details cannot be verified.
choices.C: Formal records generally preserve factual details about past meals rather than recreating the experience of those meals.
choices.D: Writers should document forgotten household meals as thoroughly as famous ceremonial meals.

questions.explanation: C captures the distinction developed throughout the passage between recoverable facts and a vividly lived experience. D converts a description of records’ limitations into an unsupported recommendation about which meals to document. B invents a recommendation about factual verification. A mistakes the pottery analogy for the passage’s subject and adds a judgment about usefulness that the passage does not make.

questions.passage: *The Quiet Sounding* is a 1972 novel by Ansel Verren set at a coastal research station in the late 1950s. Rena Varden and Mikel Orr have recently begun directing a survey together. While staying with Rena’s relatives in the port of Sovren, they prepare for a season of routine measurements. Rena is perplexed by Mikel’s reluctance to participate:
questions.question: Which quotation from *The Quiet Sounding* most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “The harbor survey committee conducted its midsummer briefing each year in the Vardens’ long upstairs room.”
choices.B: “[Rena] stood for dependable company, an orderly future, and the reassuring weight of a task that could not simply be abandoned.”
choices.C: “[Mikel] felt again the unaccountable exhilaration of setting out from school on an unsupervised afternoon, with no destination settled.”
choices.D: “Rena could discover no reason for [Mikel’s] resistance to a schedule that appeared to her both manageable and agreeable.”
