questions.question: Which quotation from a history of statistics would most effectively support the student's claim?

choices.A: “No other publication presents Dain's analytical capabilities and theoretical commitments as distinctly as *Recursive Estimation* does.”
choices.B: “Debate about *Recursive Estimation* has persisted among statisticians since the work was first published, and specialists continue to offer sharply divergent interpretations of what its arguments and findings imply.”
choices.C: “Dain drew on the work of contemporary statisticians while anticipating later developments, as *Recursive Estimation* amply demonstrates.”
choices.D: “The methods in Dain's publications preceding *Recursive Estimation* constitute an earlier research approach that she did not subsequently resume.”

questions.explanation: D establishes a before-and-after division in Dain's research and specifies that the earlier approach was permanently abandoned, directly supporting a decisive change. A identifies a particularly representative work without showing a shift. B establishes disagreement among readers, not development in Dain's research. C describes influences and foresight but supplies no comparison between her earlier and later approaches.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The annual Aster First Aid Drill takes place throughout Veloria each September.
• It commemorates the establishment of Veloria's national emergency service.
• Participants practice treating simulated injuries in large public training sessions.
• In Mavren, more than 1,400 participants assemble in Avlin Square for the city's largest session.
• In Sarvek, more than 1,400 participants assemble at the retired Hesk Freight Station for the city's largest session.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in how people in Mavren and Sarvek participate in the drill. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Mavren's largest training session takes place in a public square, whereas Sarvek's takes place at a former freight station.
choices.B: In both Mavren and Sarvek, more than 1,400 people gather for the city's largest session to practice treating simulated injuries.
choices.C: Participants in Mavren and Sarvek observe the Aster First Aid Drill, although their arrangements are not identical.
choices.D: Each September, Velorians commemorate the establishment of their national emergency service through the Aster First Aid Drill.

questions.explanation: B identifies a specific shared practice in the two named cities: large gatherings in which participants rehearse first aid. C acknowledges participation but shifts attention to unspecified differences. D describes the nationwide occasion without identifying a similarity between the two cities' activities. A accurately contrasts their venues, which serves a comparison of differences rather than the requested similarity.

questions.passage: It is well established that the reference archive at Ardent Deep Laboratory, with its extensively annotated records of gamma pulses and charged-particle tracks, _____ a comprehensive catalog of background events.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: to have maintained
choices.B: maintaining
choices.C: to maintain
choices.D: maintains

questions.explanation: D supplies the finite verb needed for the clause introduced by “that”: the singular subject “archive” takes “maintains.” The intervening phrase beginning “with” does not change that subject or provide a predicate. A and C are infinitive forms, and B is a participle; none can independently serve as the verb of this clause.

questions.passage: Intrusion research, including Sera Danen and colleagues' 2018 assessment, has demonstrated that unfiltered network traffic can compromise institutional computing systems. Regional councils therefore require threat reviews before authorizing new campus networks. One review recommended substantially more safeguards for databases than for file archives. Although few recommendations specifically addressed archives, the reviewers considered the proposed safeguards sufficient for both kinds of system because _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: safeguards directed at databases are also likely to reduce most of the threats faced by file archives.
choices.B: attacks on databases have been documented less extensively than attacks on file archives.
choices.C: safeguards designed for databases can occasionally create additional vulnerabilities in file archives.
choices.D: the consequences of an attack can differ considerably from one database to another.

questions.explanation: A explains why a plan concentrated on databases could still adequately protect file archives: its safeguards have benefits that extend to those archives. B concerns the amount of research, not the safeguards' effectiveness. C supplies a reason to doubt adequate protection. D describes variation among databases without connecting database safeguards to protection of file archives.

questions.passage: The Anvar Planetarium usually presents its star tours through live commentary and spontaneous exchanges with visitors; recorded narration is used only occasionally. Students surveyed visitors about a proposal to replace a larger share of these tours with prerecorded programs. Most respondents opposed the change, and the students argue that much of this opposition reflects a fear that the planetarium would lose its distinctive character.
questions.question: Which quotation from a survey respondent would best illustrate the students' claim?

choices.A: “The administrators scarcely consulted regular visitors before announcing the proposal. Our views deserve more consideration.”
choices.B: “Long prerecorded programs often tire me out. I would rather visit places where I can take a break from a continuous stream of amplified sound.”
choices.C: “The live tours employ several local guides. Replacing those tours could leave the guides struggling to earn a living.”
choices.D: “The unscripted conversation makes Anvar unlike any other planetarium I have visited. I would hate for its tours to become indistinguishable from everyone else's.”

questions.explanation: D directly connects opposition to the loss of a feature that makes Anvar distinctive: its unscripted conversation. B opposes the change because of fatigue from amplified narration. A objects to the decision-making process. C emphasizes guides' livelihoods. Those concerns could explain opposition, but none specifically illustrates a fear that the institution will lose its unique character.

questions.passage: Instructional verse can preserve administrative knowledge: harbor tally chants explain levy calculations, while guild recitations encode rules for reconciling accounts. Archive keeper Nadra Ilven assisted historian Miro Saren's research by contributing verses that describe a sequence of cross-checks used in balancing cargo ledgers, a procedure documented as early as 1375. Analysis of surviving account books revealed that both accounting accuracy and processing capacity increased as the procedure became more widespread, even while transaction volume rose. This finding lends support to the idea that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the procedure preserved in the verses effectively sustained reliable accounting under increasing workloads.
choices.B: present-day clerks have made only minor departures from the procedure described in the verses.
choices.C: the procedure was initially adopted from the administrative practices of neighboring ports.
choices.D: clerks maintained accurate ledgers by periodically diverting transactions to unrelated accounting systems.

questions.explanation: A connects the observed gains in accuracy and capacity, despite heavier workloads, to the practical effectiveness of the procedure described in the verses. D proposes diversion to other systems, for which no evidence is given. C concerns the procedure's origin, which the ledger analysis does not establish. B compares historical and contemporary practice, but the passage provides no evidence about present-day clerks.

questions.passage: Some materials engineers obtain useful properties by bringing structurally different components together. Nadia Senkar, for instance, incorporated a basalt-fiber mesh into a flexible thermoplastic matrix in her Teravex panels. In a comparable approach, Ren Vorrel _____ a carbon lattice with cellulose resin in the load-bearing composite called Arcalen.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: confused
choices.B: combined
choices.C: compared
choices.D: replaced

questions.explanation: B describes joining the lattice and resin within one composite, matching both the general statement and Senkar's example. C indicates examining similarities or differences without necessarily creating a material. A indicates mistaking one component for another. D indicates substituting the resin for the lattice, whereas the passage's parallel examples concern using distinct components together.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2019, acoustic engineers Nerel Orez and Bastien Valen tested how a tiled lining affected reverberation in a courtyard.
• The lining consisted of glazed ceramic plates and their supporting mortar.
• The test site was a sheltered courtyard in La Quiaca, Argentina.
• The site had a high-altitude semiarid climate.
• Under those environmental conditions, the lining reduced the duration of reverberation.
questions.question: The student wants to specify the climate at the test site. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Orez and Valen investigated reverberation in Argentina under a particular set of climatic conditions.
choices.B: Orez and Valen conducted their courtyard study in a high-altitude semiarid climate.
choices.C: Orez and Valen tested glazed ceramic plates and supporting mortar in an Argentine courtyard.
choices.D: In their 2019 study, Orez and Valen found that a tiled lining reduced reverberation.

questions.explanation: B explicitly identifies the climatic conditions as high-altitude and semiarid, fulfilling the stated goal. C identifies the material and country. D reports the result and date. A refers to climatic conditions without specifying what those conditions were; a general reference to climate is insufficient for the requested purpose.

questions.passage: *A Signal in Winter: Three Acts beside the Atlantic* is a 1936 play by Adela Senet, originally written in Portuguese. Chief engineer Rui Melgar and his wife Lidia arrive at a coastal transmission station, which Garan supervises with assistance from Iria, Melgar's daughter from an earlier marriage. Senet depicts Lidia attempting to lessen the hostility between Garan and Melgar, as is evident when _____
questions.question: Which quotation from a translation of *A Signal in Winter* most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: Lidia says to herself, “If only I could drift beyond the reach of these voices, leave these weary faces behind, and remember none of them!”
choices.B: Lidia says to Garan, “You mock my husband, then turn such pitying eyes on me. I can almost hear you thinking, ‘What a fate, to have married someone so much older!’ Your sympathy is perfectly plain to me.”
choices.C: Lidia says to Garan, “An educated man like you, [Garan], must see that a station is ruined less by storms and broken wires than by rancor, suspicion, and this endless muttering. Make your peace [with Chief Engineer Melgar]; you cannot answer every difficulty with resentment.”
choices.D: Lidia says to Iria, “October has come already! How are we to endure all those silent months here [at the station]?”

questions.explanation: C explicitly urges Garan to make peace with Melgar and challenges the resentment sustaining their conflict, directly illustrating Lidia's effort to reduce hostility. A expresses a wish to escape the company of others. D expresses concern about the coming months. B describes mockery and pity but does not urge reconciliation or otherwise try to settle the conflict.

questions.passage: The Ventra Library's accession manual, issued in 1891, specifies only two of the eight record-verification safeguards identified by archivists Delia Moren and Jakub Havel. Such safeguards became more prevalent after 1977, as illustrated by the Rasen Library's revised manual, issued in 2016 and _____ seven of the safeguards.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: had contained
choices.B: contained
choices.C: contains
choices.D: containing

questions.explanation: D supplies a participial modifier that parallels “issued in 2016”: both describe the revised manual within the phrase introduced by “as illustrated by.” C and A introduce finite verbs where the sentence requires a modifier, disrupting the existing structure. B cannot function as the intended modifier because “contained seven” would improperly treat the manual as something contained rather than something that contains safeguards.

questions.passage: If you walked through Nerin Hall, you would encounter a pinwheel plan: the passages circulate outward from a central atrium. Each gallery therefore occupies a different orientation around that common space. _____ at the Kaldre Annex, the galleries follow a linear plan, forming a succession of rooms along one straight axis.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: To illustrate,
choices.B: At another site,
choices.C: More precisely,
choices.D: Put differently,

questions.explanation: B shifts the discussion from one building to a different location where another layout occurs. C and D would introduce a clarification or restatement of Nerin Hall's plan, but the annex has a different plan. A would introduce an example of the previously described pinwheel arrangement; the linear arrangement is not such an example.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Nika Rosen is an Austrian engineer known for waterworks and full-scale filtration prototypes.
• Rosen first gained widespread recognition in 1997 for the Teresio Waterworks, which includes two 61-meter concrete channels.
• Rosen completed *Aerovault* in 2008.
• *Aerovault* uses porous ceramic membranes and occupies an entire testing chamber.
• Rosen completed *Lineweave* in 2021.
• *Lineweave* uses woven steel mesh and occupies an entire testing chamber.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between *Aerovault* and *Lineweave*. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: After gaining recognition for the Teresio Waterworks, Rosen completed another substantial project, *Aerovault*.
choices.B: The substantial scale of the Teresio Waterworks is also apparent in *Aerovault*, which fills a testing chamber.
choices.C: Porous ceramic membranes form the filtering material in *Aerovault*, whereas *Lineweave* employs woven steel mesh.
choices.D: Rosen's reputation rests on waterworks and filtration prototypes, including *Aerovault* and *Lineweave*.

questions.explanation: C directly contrasts a corresponding feature of the two requested prototypes: their filtering materials. D groups them within Rosen's body of work without distinguishing them. B emphasizes a similarity between *Aerovault* and the earlier waterworks, not a difference between the two requested prototypes. A describes a sequence involving only one of those prototypes.

questions.passage: Collectors sometimes judge an instrument less accurate when its case bears the crest of an unfashionable workshop. For a strictly mechanical assessment, however, the crest is _____: it has no direct bearing on whether the escapement maintains uniform time.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: immaterial
choices.B: implicit
choices.C: indistinct
choices.D: unassailable

questions.explanation: A means irrelevant to the matter being assessed, matching the explanation that the crest does not affect timekeeping. D means impossible to challenge and says nothing about relevance. B means implied rather than explicitly stated; the crest is a visible feature, and the passage concerns its bearing on accuracy. C means unclear or poorly defined, which does not express the stated lack of a mechanical connection.

questions.passage: Archive dating can help historians establish whether the closure of handloom workshops near Rellin in 1846 _____ the introduction of mechanized looms to that district. If the workshops had closed before mechanized production could have displaced their output, the closures would instead point to another cause, such as interrupted wool deliveries following the Meren Pass landslide.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: compensated for
choices.B: clashed with
choices.C: developed into
choices.D: coincided with

questions.explanation: D means occurred at approximately the same time as, matching the proposed comparison between the timing of workshop closures and the arrival of mechanized looms. C describes transformation from one thing into another. A describes offsetting a loss or disadvantage. B describes conflict, not temporal correspondence. The contrasting possibility that the closures came earlier confirms that timing is the relevant relationship.

questions.passage: Mara Iken and Dario Senn were among the 240 engineers represented at the 1907 Gleiren Materials Forum in Zurich, an event that introduced experimental resins to a broad professional audience. Several processes demonstrated there, though now standard (especially a self-repairing formulation developed by Leona Vesk), _____ regarded as implausible at the time.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: was
choices.B: were
choices.C: has been
choices.D: is

questions.explanation: B agrees with the plural subject “Several processes” and establishes the past tense required by “at the time.” The singular formulation mentioned in parentheses is an example, not the subject of the clause. A, C, and D are singular verb forms and cannot agree with “processes”; C and D also fail to express the same simple past construction.

questions.passage: An archival plotter can reproduce finely shaded maps at a rate of 82 sheets per hour; a rotary press, producing simpler monochrome maps, can reach 335 sheets per hour. The _____ between those rates is unsurprising, since the movements needed to place tiny drops of several inks constrain throughput more than the continuous rotation used in monochrome printing does.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: rivalry
choices.B: divergence
choices.C: interplay
choices.D: parity

questions.explanation: B denotes a difference or separation, fitting the markedly unequal production rates and the explanation for that difference. A would describe competition between agents, not the numerical gap between rates. D means equality and contradicts the figures. C suggests interaction between the rates, whereas the passage describes separate mechanisms that yield different outputs.

questions.passage: The unequal advantages of compression across device classes can be summarized as _____ compact delta blocks for long-range radar transmitters; dictionary-coded packets for routine control units; and uncompressed messages for the emergency beacons in the Arven series.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: follows,
choices.B: follows;
choices.C: follows:
choices.D: follows

questions.explanation: C completes the independent introductory clause and uses a colon to introduce the three-part explanatory list. B incorrectly places a semicolon before a noun phrase rather than an independent clause. A does not provide the conventional punctuation required after the list-introducing expression “as follows.” D omits the boundary that separates that expression from the items it introduces.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Maren Ordel's 2011 novel *The Salt Meridian*. Miren, a cartographer, hosts visiting navigators in the instrument room of her family's house, and Lerida is her sister. A chart circle is an informal gathering devoted to discussing maps and navigation.
At last the visitors reached for their coats. Uncle Orsan had appeared at the doorway three times since dusk, each time looking past Miren toward the occupied chairs. Before the chart circles began, that room had belonged to his barometers and measuring benches. Now it became, every evening, what Lerida grandly called Miren's academy; the inkpots and unrolled sheets were still scattered about whenever Orsan arrived to arrange his instruments for the next morning's readings.
questions.question: Based on the text, what most likely motivates Orsan's behavior during Miren's chart circle?

choices.A: He wants the gathering to end so he can prepare the room for his own work.
choices.B: He finds the visitors' conversation tedious and hopes to persuade them to leave.
choices.C: He needs Miren's assistance elsewhere in the house but cannot obtain it over the course of the gathering.
choices.D: He wants the visitors to endorse his plans for establishing a new instrument workshop.

questions.explanation: A follows from Orsan's repeated checks on the occupied room and the explanation that the gatherings leave his customary working space unprepared for morning readings. D invents plans for a new workshop and a desire for endorsement. B invents an assessment of the conversation; the passage identifies a practical concern about the space. C invents a need for assistance elsewhere rather than recognizing his work in this room.

questions.passage: The present-day Cambrel Exchange once housed the Ravena Bakers' Guild, one of several regional associations organized around grain procurement. Like _____ counterpart guilds, the Ravena association formed along occupational lines: most members produced bread from locally milled rye.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: it's
choices.B: its
choices.C: they're
choices.D: their

questions.explanation: B is the singular possessive pronoun referring to the Ravena association: its counterpart guilds are the guilds comparable to that one association. D is plural and does not agree with that antecedent. C means “they are,” and A means “it is” or “it has”; neither contraction can supply the possessive modifier required before “counterpart guilds.”

questions.passage: *The Mariven Atlas* is a navigational manual that _____ a systematic account of seasonal winds. First compiled in Occitan during the sixteenth century, the manual has since appeared in numerous languages, enabling mariners far beyond its original region to consult its explanations.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: offers
choices.B: offer
choices.C: were offering
choices.D: have offered

questions.explanation: A agrees with the singular antecedent of “that,” namely “a navigational manual,” and supplies the present-tense description of the manual's content. D, C, and B are plural forms. The later references to languages and mariners do not change the singular subject of the relative clause.

questions.passage: A 2017 inventory classified a greater share of a glass collection as either late Classical or protoindustrial than earlier inventories had. The discrepancy is hardly unexpected, given how little _____ exists among specialists about the boundaries of those categories: curators routinely challenge one another's classifications.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: curiosity
choices.B: accord
choices.C: deliberation
choices.D: scrutiny

questions.explanation: B means agreement, and the recurring challenges to classifications demonstrate that specialists do not agree on the categories' boundaries. D means close examination, which may occur even amid disagreement. C means consideration or discussion; the disputes do not indicate an absence of such activity. A means interest or a desire to investigate, which the passage does not suggest is lacking.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Livia Rask is a Norwegian-Argentine acoustic engineer.
• Rask is known for designing full-scale sound-absorbing shells.
• *Keldra (Prototype 7)* debuted in 2013 at the Cindar Wind Laboratory in Fano, Italy.
• The prototype consists of perforated bronze panels and violet silicone baffles.
• It occupies 1,642 cubic meters of space.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize when and where *Keldra (Prototype 7)* debuted. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Rask's acoustic designs are known for their substantial scale and capacity to absorb sound.
choices.B: Norwegian-Argentine engineer Livia Rask designs sound-absorbing shells such as *Keldra (Prototype 7)*, introduced in 2013.
choices.C: The bronze panels and silicone baffles of *Keldra (Prototype 7)* formed an imposing 1,642-cubic-meter structure when the prototype debuted.
choices.D: In 2013, Livia Rask debuted *Keldra (Prototype 7)* in Fano, Italy.

questions.explanation: D explicitly supplies both requested details: the debut year and its location. C describes construction and volume but gives neither the date nor the location. B supplies the date but not the location. A describes the engineer's work generally without identifying either detail about this prototype's debut.

questions.passage: In her 2006 book *Margins of the Survey*, Leora Venn draws partly on photographic copies of field notebooks kept in the 1930s by Oren “Keel” Tavrik and Nesta Senar. Her analysis concerns the surveyors' revisions: they replaced initial observations with abbreviated recalculations and private sequences of symbols. Rendering those revised entries as ordinary written text required Venn to inspect the photographs repeatedly, since many marks were difficult to distinguish in the faded images.
questions.question: What does the text most strongly suggest about Tavrik's and Senar's revised entries?

choices.A: Few, if any, dependable transcriptions of the revised entries were available when Venn began her research.
choices.B: The surveyors' notebooks became increasingly influential after they were first compiled.
choices.C: Venn considered Tavrik's revision methods more innovative than Senar's methods.
choices.D: More photographs of Tavrik's revised entries survived than photographs of Senar's did.

questions.explanation: A is supported indirectly by Venn's need to reconstruct the entries through repeated inspection of unclear photographs. Existing dependable transcriptions would have reduced the need for that labor. D invents a comparison of surviving photographs. C invents a comparative judgment of innovation. B invents a change in influence over time. None of those comparisons or trends is supplied by the passage.

questions.passage: For Talven Spectroscopy Station, a member of the Shared Calibration Consortium since 1983, reciprocal instrument access brings both advantages and _____ consortium's participating laboratories, from Torvik Materials Center to Elsen Photonics Institute, must provide instrument time to Talven, Talven must in turn provide instrument time to them.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: responsibilities: while the
choices.B: responsibilities; the
choices.C: responsibilities. The
choices.D: responsibilities, while the

questions.explanation: A uses a colon after the complete introductory clause to present its explanation. Within that explanation, “while” makes the clause about the other laboratories subordinate, and the final clause states Talven's reciprocal responsibility. C and B leave two independent clauses in the explanation joined only by a comma. D creates the same problem between the initial independent clause and the final independent clause: the intervening “while” clause does not supply a coordinating conjunction.

questions.passage: Ivon Maraschke studied attitudes toward archive applications in Spain and found that, among users concerned about confidentiality, willingness to adopt an application decreased as its perceived risk of exposing private records increased. A later team surveyed occupational groups in Finland about a new indexing application. Freelance interpreters assigned the application the highest average disclosure-risk rating of any group surveyed. If Maraschke's finding applies broadly, the later result suggests that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the indexing application is more appealing to freelance interpreters than competing applications are.
choices.B: freelance interpreters probably give other considerations more weight than confidentiality when selecting applications.
choices.C: average willingness to adopt privacy-conscious applications differs little among the surveyed groups.
choices.D: freelance interpreters might be less willing than members of the other surveyed groups to adopt the indexing application.

questions.explanation: D applies the stated inverse relationship: the group perceiving the greatest disclosure risk may show the least willingness to adopt the application. A introduces a comparison with competing applications that were not studied. C conflicts with the predicted consequence of different risk perceptions. B speculates about how the group ranks other considerations, whereas the evidence concerns perceived risk and willingness to adopt.

questions.passage: Kiln facilities operating at or above 760°C, such as the Verna complex at 910°C, commonly suspend production for periodic inspections. Shutdown hours depend on loading rate, furnace geometry, liner composition, and other factors. Nevertheless, an industrial engineer claims that some facilities in this temperature range experienced a decline in annual shutdown hours between the early 1990s and the late 2010s. The graph shows three such facilities.
questions.question: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the engineer's claim?

choices.A: The highest annual shutdown total among the three facilities in the 2017–18 cycle was approximately 210 hours.
choices.B: Salgren recorded approximately 265 shutdown hours in 1992–93 and approximately 210 hours in 2017–18.
choices.C: Nevril recorded approximately 170 shutdown hours in 1992–93 and approximately 195 hours in 2017–18.
choices.D: None of the three facilities recorded fewer shutdown hours in 1992–93 than in 2017–18.

questions.explanation: B identifies a decrease for Salgren between the specified periods, directly supporting the claim that some facilities experienced declining shutdown totals. A gives only a final-period maximum and establishes no change over time. C describes an increase for Nevril, not a decrease. D is inaccurate because both Nevril and Othra have lower totals in the first period than in the final period; it also does not identify the required decline.

graph.caption: Annual shutdown hours at three kiln facilities

questions.passage: Barring the recovery of discarded backup drives, engineers are unlikely ever to assemble _____ account of the Veskar VX9 prototype's 2004 trials; substantial portions of its telemetry were deliberately erased by the project's later administrators.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: a comprehensive
choices.B: a questionable
choices.C: an imaginative
choices.D: a cursory

questions.explanation: A means covering the relevant material fully, which the loss of substantial evidence makes unlikely. C describes an inventive account, which could still be produced without complete records. D describes a brief or superficial account, also possible despite missing information. B describes an account open to doubt; erased evidence would not prevent such an account and might even make doubt more likely.

questions.passage: Sarela Venn's award-winning report *Quiet Flow in Porous Reactors* was published in 1981 by the Catalyst Measurement Cooperative (CMC). Its cofounder Oren Haskin, an experimental chemist and technical instructor, had met theorist Nadia Tern during a 1964 traveling demonstration based on Elian Arden's manual *Reagents in Motion*. They envisioned a research association that would develop and publicize work by scientists at regional polytechnic colleges. Founded in 1966, CMC subsequently gave those scientists, including Venn, a venue for their findings through training workshops and specialist publications.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To trace changes in Haskin and Tern's working relationship over time
choices.B: To draw attention principally to one award-winning report by Venn
choices.C: To explain how Arden's manual influenced the research methods of Haskin and Tern
choices.D: To discuss the origins and significance of a research cooperative

questions.explanation: D encompasses both the cooperative's founding and the continuing opportunity it provided to a particular group of researchers. B treats the opening example as the whole purpose and omits the organizational history. C mistakes the occasion of the founders' meeting for a demonstrated methodological influence. A suggests an account of how their relationship changed, whereas the passage describes its beginning and their shared organizational goal.

questions.passage: Including measurements from analysts Nira Kovan and Loren Askar, the 2016 compilation *Thermal Archives of Metals* aimed to survey foundry-testing methods from the 1940s through the _____ given the collection's coverage of more than 185 experimental protocols, that aim was largely met.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: 1980s and
choices.C: 1980s, and

questions.explanation: C joins two independent clauses with a comma and the coordinating conjunction “and.” The second clause begins with the introductory phrase “given the collection's coverage...” and ends with the independent statement “that aim was largely met.” A omits the required coordinating comma. D would begin a new sentence with the incorrectly lowercase “given.” B supplies no appropriate boundary or conjunction between the independent clauses.

questions.passage: Slovenian computational engineer Klara Sever uses layered stress maps to reveal robustness and load sharing within structures. Some analyses focus on celebrated constructions, as in her model of the Valdra Suspension Bridge; others examine ordinary structures, such as the roof truss of a rural grain shed. Rather than treating the two categories as competing interests, Sever regards both as opportunities to show how a structure's strength depends on connections among its parts.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Sever's analyses use both celebrated and ordinary structures to demonstrate robustness and structural interdependence.
choices.B: Sever's bridge model has attracted more scholarly attention than her grain-shed model has.
choices.C: Sever initially modeled celebrated structures before abandoning them in favor of ordinary structures.
choices.D: Sever's grain-shed model places greater emphasis on load sharing than on robustness.

questions.explanation: A includes both categories of structure and the shared purpose the passage explicitly assigns them. C invents a chronological shift and abandonment that the passage does not describe. B invents a comparison of scholarly attention. D introduces a ranking between two qualities, whereas the passage presents robustness and connection as related concerns across both kinds of analysis.

questions.passage: Immersive room installations such as Elven House (installed in 2001) and The Norra Rooms (built in 2012) reproduce familiar domestic furnishings so visitors can orient themselves readily. While that familiarity can help _____ feelings of ease, an excessively exact reconstruction may produce “domestic estrangement,” a response in which the apparent familiarity itself unsettles the observer.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: elicit
choices.B: constrict
choices.C: repudiate
choices.D: counterbalance

questions.explanation: A means bring forth or evoke, matching the idea that familiar details can produce feelings of ease. C means reject or disavow, which conflicts with producing ease. D means offset with an opposing effect, but the passage identifies familiarity as a source of ease. B means restrict or narrow, again reversing the intended positive effect. The later unsettling response supplies the contrast.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Sable Ornin's 1927 novel *Summer of the Foil*.
During the four days before the tournament, Rennen scarcely saw anyone. He hired a narrow room above a [fencing] academy on Sable Quay and practiced almost incessantly. Invitations to the evening promenade went unanswered; his meals were brought to the little lodging behind the practice room.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does “incessantly” most nearly mean?

choices.A: At great speed
choices.B: With great care
choices.C: Without interruption
choices.D: With sufficient frequency

questions.explanation: C fits the emphasis on nearly continuous practice, reinforced by Rennen's withdrawal from social activities. D concerns adequacy, whereas the passage stresses persistence. B concerns precision or caution, which is not the meaning of the word. A concerns speed; practicing continuously does not necessarily mean practicing quickly.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Protocol pairs are research laboratories that form agreements to exchange calibration methods and measurement standards.
• Previously called “bench pairing,” the practice developed in East Asia after the 1972 Welfen instrument crisis to repair inconsistencies among laboratories.
• Many laboratories in Estonia maintain protocol-pair agreements with laboratories abroad.
• Valden Ion Laboratory in Tartu, Estonia, and Nerai Standards Hall in Kyoto, Japan, formed a protocol pair in 2001.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the duration of Valden and Nerai's relationship. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Nerai Standards Hall, which became Valden's protocol partner in 2001, is located in Kyoto, Japan.
choices.B: Following the 1972 instrument crisis, laboratories such as Valden and Nerai began forming agreements to exchange measurement standards.
choices.C: Valden and Nerai have exchanged calibration methods and measurement standards as protocol partners since 2001.
choices.D: Despite their distance, Valden and Nerai have a calibration agreement comparable to those maintained by other protocol pairs.

questions.explanation: C foregrounds the relationship's continuing duration by stating that the exchange has occurred “since 2001.” A includes the formation year but emphasizes Nerai's location. D emphasizes resemblance to other agreements without specifying duration. B describes the broader practice's historical origin and does not establish how long this particular pair has maintained its relationship.

questions.passage: Judges at the Caldren Chronometer Fair once evaluated instruments by the celebrated maker Alar Venk with considerable _____: admiration for his craftsmanship was so intense that their assessments rarely approached impartiality.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: circumspection
choices.B: veneration
choices.C: forthrightness
choices.D: inquisitiveness

questions.explanation: B means profound admiration or reverence, fitting the intense admiration that compromised the judges' objectivity. C means openness or directness, not admiration. A means caution, which does not account for revering the maker. D means curiosity, whereas the passage emphasizes an already established attitude of esteem rather than a desire to investigate.

questions.passage:
Revenue from four engineering-software releases in Canada
Engineering software can become commercially successful over years of licensing even when sales during its first week are modest. A technology journalist argues that indications of product quality, such as an Independent Reliability Seal, can raise customer interest and substantially improve cumulative revenue despite a comparatively weak launch: for example, _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?

choices.A: TesseraFlow received a quality seal, but LentisCore, which did not, had higher total revenue.
choices.B: OrventGrid and TesseraFlow both received a quality seal, but OrventGrid had higher total revenue.
choices.C: first-week revenue was C$231,540 for LentisCore and C$2,965,410 for KeldranMesh.
choices.D: KeldranMesh earned more during its first week than OrventGrid did, but OrventGrid ultimately earned more in total.

questions.explanation: D contrasts an unsealed package's stronger launch with a sealed package's greater eventual revenue, fitting the journalist's claim about quality recognition and success despite modest initial sales. OrventGrid began at D$117,360 versus KeldranMesh's D$2,965,410 but ultimately reached D$27,614,980 versus D$6,218,740. C gives only launch figures. B compares two sealed packages without illustrating weak initial sales versus later success. A describes a higher total for an unsealed package and does not illustrate the claimed pattern.

questions.passage: Discussions of automatic timekeeping corrections often focus on powered devices, such as the dual-motor Orven chronograph. <u>Automatic correction can also occur in regulators that use no electrical power.</u> For example, bench analyses suggest that the spring-driven, palm-sized Telve regulator compensated mechanically for changes in temperature.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains the important purpose served by corrections in the devices mentioned earlier.
choices.B: It indicates that the devices discussed earlier are not the only devices capable of the relevant feature.
choices.C: It provides the specific example of a regulator investigated in the analysis mentioned later.
choices.D: It defines a technical term describing the corrections mentioned earlier.

questions.explanation: B describes the sentence's broadening function: it extends automatic correction beyond powered devices to a second category. C describes the following sentence, which supplies the Telve example. A incorrectly assigns an explanation of purpose to a statement about which devices have the feature. D is incorrect because the sentence does not define a term.

questions.passage: The Arven protocol, developed by Canadian materials engineer Pavel Dorren, is noted for controlled deformation and the interplay of stiffness and _____ technicians can examine, for instance, how a wire recovers its shape after a bend.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: elasticity which
choices.B: elasticity;
choices.C: elasticity,
choices.D: elasticity

questions.explanation: B separates two independent clauses with a semicolon. The first states what the protocol is noted for; the second states what technicians can examine. C creates a comma splice. A inserts “which” without a structure that can accommodate the following independent clause. D supplies no boundary between the clauses.

questions.passage: The Varnes polar station logbook, a series of temperature entries and working notes compiled by meteorologist Nerik Lomor in 1954, is sometimes described as moving despite the intervening decades. Its account of difficult night work is, however, _____ precisely because it comes from a distant era: recognizing familiar human concerns in an earlier observer's routine gives the record its emotional force.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: painstaking
choices.B: unblemished
choices.C: poignant
choices.D: ingenious

questions.explanation: C means emotionally moving, matching the stated emotional force and the explanation that the record's age strengthens a sense of human connection. B concerns physical condition. A concerns the care taken in producing something. D concerns originality or inventiveness. None of those qualities follows from the connection across time that the passage emphasizes.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Zelvora insulating paste contains silicon dioxide, an important component of heat-resistant coatings.
• Each 250 grams of Zelvora contains 3.2 grams of silicon dioxide.
• Merenex ceramic paste also contains silicon dioxide.
• Each 250 grams of Merenex contains 5.6 grams of silicon dioxide.
• Coating lines cannot manufacture silicon dioxide themselves and must receive it through externally supplied materials, including premixed pastes.
• Silicon dioxide is also known as silica.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Zelvora and Merenex. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Merenex supplies 5.6 grams of silicon dioxide in each 250 grams of paste.
choices.B: Because coating lines cannot produce silica, they obtain it from supplied materials such as Zelvora.
choices.C: Premixed pastes are among the externally supplied materials from which coating lines can obtain silicon dioxide.
choices.D: Zelvora and Merenex have in common that both contain silica, also called silicon dioxide.

questions.explanation: D names both pastes and identifies their shared component, directly fulfilling the request for a similarity. A gives a quantity for Merenex alone. B uses Zelvora as one example of an external source without comparing it with Merenex. C makes a general statement about pastes and does not identify the feature shared by the two named materials.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Elva Norell is a Swedish-Argentine sound archivist.
• Between 1921 and 1946, Norell archived more than 42,000 recordings from northern Europe.
• Norell recorded *Lanterns at Mora* in Voss, Norway, on .
• Norell recorded *The Hesk Mill* in Rostock, Germany, on .
• Both recordings document unaccompanied workers' chants.
• The recordings can now be heard through the Ravela Historical Sound Vault.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize when Norell made both recordings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: On , Norell added *Lanterns at Mora* to her growing archive of workers' chants.
choices.B: Norell recorded *Lanterns at Mora* on , after recording *The Hesk Mill* on .
choices.C: Both recordings document workers' chants, but *Lanterns at Mora* was recorded in Voss, whereas *The Hesk Mill* was recorded in Rostock.
choices.D: Thousands of recordings archived by Norell can now be heard in one place through the Ravela Historical Sound Vault.

questions.explanation: B supplies the dates of both recordings and expresses their chronological relationship. A gives a date for only one recording. C emphasizes the shared category and contrasting locations, not the timing. D describes present access to the archive without identifying when either recording was made.

questions.passage: Today, the *Bravena Seed Ledger* is regarded as an authority on drought-tolerant agriculture, with its highest four-leaf designation reserved for cultivars such as Merevale Amber in _____ when botanists Elian and Petra Sorn assembled the ledger in 1911, it was primarily an advertisement for their fertilizer business, intended to encourage farmers across western Slovakia to prepare trial plots and order the recommended mineral blends.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Nitra
choices.B: Nitra,
choices.C: Nitra; however,
choices.D: Nitra, however,

questions.explanation: C separates the two independent clauses with a semicolon and sets off the contrastive adverb “however” with a following comma. The second independent clause begins with the subordinate “when” clause and concludes by explaining the ledger's earlier commercial purpose. A supplies no appropriate clause boundary. D and B use a comma where a stronger boundary is required; “however” in D is not a coordinating conjunction and cannot repair the comma splice.

questions.passage:
Cold-storage capacity at five Austrian seed repositories
The Kelser National Repository has the greatest cold-storage capacity among Austrian seed repositories: 18,930 cubic meters distributed across facilities in Salzburg, Vienna, and Burgenland. Most other repositories have considerably less capacity. The Malta Collection Depot in Styria, for example, holds 3,567 cubic meters. In Carinthia, the capacity of the Erlen Seed Vault is _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.A: 5,014 cubic meters.
choices.B: 1,648 cubic meters.
choices.C: 1,126 cubic meters.
choices.D: 493 cubic meters.

questions.explanation: B matches the capacity in the Erlen Seed Vault row: 1,648 cubic meters. C gives Varrin Crop Bank's capacity. D gives Senra Gene Repository's capacity; sharing Erlen's region does not make it the requested repository. A is not Erlen's capacity and also differs from the table's 5,104-cubic-meter value for Rovek Seed Library.

questions.passage: The ledger format *Dervan K-8* survives only on the Teralan Archive's legacy cluster, and this restricted installation base makes it unusually vulnerable to becoming unreadable. Format-by-format preservation prioritizes vulnerable formats such as *Dervan K-8*. Advocates of a systems approach, however, argue that attending to power conditions, hardware configuration, and interactions among an archive's formats and services can improve preservation outcomes for all its holdings. If that view is correct, a format-by-format approach to preserving *Dervan K-8* could _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: mistakenly move preservation efforts away from *Dervan K-8* itself.
choices.B: enable a more complete assessment of how power changes reduce competition among formats on the cluster.
choices.C: yield a fuller account of how the distribution of other Dervan formats across countries has affected their readability.
choices.D: overlook ways that changes in other formats and services on the cluster could affect *Dervan K-8*'s continued readability.

questions.explanation: D identifies the limitation implied by the systems approach: treating one format in isolation may neglect consequential interactions with other holdings or services. C introduces international distribution, which is not addressed. B attributes attention to system-level relationships to the isolated approach, contrary to the contrast. A contradicts the statement that the format-by-format approach prioritizes vulnerable individual formats.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Varen Engineering Trials are international competitive events for apprentice engineers.
• A platinum ribbon indicates a first-place finish.
• Loren Sarek competed as a circuit designer from 1993 to 2009.
• Sarek won fourteen ribbons, eight of them platinum.
• Mila Dorren competed as a robotics assembler from 2012 to 2024.
• Dorren won twenty-nine ribbons, nineteen of them platinum.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the number of platinum ribbons won by Dorren. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Both platinum-ribbon winners, Sarek and Dorren began participating in the Trials in 1993 and 2012, respectively.
choices.B: Dorren accumulated twenty-nine ribbons while competing in robotics assembly from 2012 to 2024.
choices.C: During her robotics-assembly career at the Trials, Dorren won twenty-nine ribbons, nineteen of which were platinum.
choices.D: At the Trials, platinum ribbons indicate first-place finishes, and accomplished competitors such as Sarek have earned several.

questions.explanation: C explicitly states the requested count: nineteen platinum ribbons. B gives Dorren's total ribbon count and participation years but not the platinum count. A gives debut years and establishes that both won platinum ribbons without specifying Dorren's number. D defines the award and mentions a different competitor, leaving Dorren's count unstated.

questions.passage: When reconstructing a turbine's maintenance history, engineers such as Dr. Nire Malen at Raven Technical School rely partly on measurements of impeller diameter and blade _____ the FerroDuct F-12 turbine at Vezna Works in Pilsen, the National Machinery Register assembles these measurements by exchanging records with regional workshops, linking assembly drawings to detailed component reports, and maintaining quantitative files that include the impeller's 86-centimeter tip diameter.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: profiles and for
choices.B: profiles, for
choices.C: profiles. For
choices.D: profiles for

questions.explanation: C closes the independent clause about the measurements engineers use and begins a new sentence whose introductory phrase is “For the FerroDuct F-12 turbine...” B joins the independent clauses with only a comma. D supplies no appropriate clause boundary. A uses “and” to connect the independent clauses but omits the comma required before that coordinating conjunction.

questions.passage: Accounts of the Veskra surveying method (a procedure for plotting irregular parcels) draw on sources as varied as *A Concentric Traverse*, compiled around 1862, and *The Fifth Bearing*, published around 1916. Otto Varela's *Register of Field Instruments*, written in the 1890s, is particularly influential; engineer Lidia Sorin adapted some of its material for *Navigation Loops* in 1908. *Navigation Loops* describes the method's distinctive Paired Plummet frame, but no text written before 1908 does. This pattern suggests that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: Varela did not know of Paired Plummet descriptions while writing his Register, even though such descriptions are known to have been available to him.
choices.B: the overall contents of *Register of Field Instruments* resemble those of *The Fifth Bearing* more closely than those of *Navigation Loops*.
choices.C: *Navigation Loops* is more historically accurate than the Register because *The Fifth Bearing* had not yet been published when the Register was written.
choices.D: an account of the Veskra method that mentions the Paired Plummet frame likely has a textual lineage connecting it to *Navigation Loops*.

questions.explanation: D draws the warranted, qualified inference from the feature's earliest attested appearance in *Navigation Loops*: later accounts mentioning it likely derive through that textual tradition. B compares overall content on evidence about only one feature. A asserts the availability of earlier descriptions despite the stated absence of pre-1908 references. C treats publication order as evidence of historical accuracy, a connection the passage does not establish.

questions.passage: Tomas Verin is a landscape engineer from Portugal's Douro Valley. Reviewers have praised his projects for combining regional gravity-fed irrigation practices with modern sensor-controlled water management. Verin is not alone in integrating inherited methods with contemporary systems. In her 2019 project *The Kyraven Garden*, Slovenian engineer Nadja Lesek successfully combined traditional stone channels from the Isonzo Valley with automated flow controls.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Contemporary landscape engineers are combining traditional regional practices with modern management systems.
choices.B: Verin's success has influenced engineers outside his region to adopt sensor-controlled water management.
choices.C: Engineers from other regions should consider the expectations of local growers before designing irrigation systems.
choices.D: Several well-known landscape engineers increased their commissions after adopting traditional irrigation methods.

questions.explanation: A states the shared practice illustrated by both engineers: combining inherited regional techniques with contemporary systems. D introduces increased commissions without supporting evidence. B introduces influence from Verin to other engineers, whereas the passage merely provides a second example. C turns a descriptive passage into a recommendation the author does not make.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Optical sensors can register photoluminescence, light emitted after a material absorbs ultraviolet radiation.
• Compounds in various materials, including scapolite and fluorite, can produce this effect.
• A testing team illuminated a sample of Merad glaze, a fired ceramic coating.
• The team rated its photoluminescence intensity as moderate.
• The team illuminated a sample of Torven glaze, another fired ceramic coating.
• The team rated its photoluminescence intensity as high.
questions.question: The student wants to make a generalization about fired ceramic coatings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A testing team measured the photoluminescence intensity of several materials.
choices.B: Some fired ceramic coatings emit photoluminescent light after exposure to ultraviolet radiation.
choices.C: Merad glaze and Torven glaze are both fired ceramic coatings.
choices.D: In a study, Merad glaze and Torven glaze were illuminated for testing.

questions.explanation: B generalizes the observed property from the two examples to some members of their category. Both samples exhibited measurable photoluminescence, supporting that limited claim. A reports a research activity without stating a finding about coatings. C states their classification without identifying the tested property. D describes what was tested, again omitting the result needed for the generalization.

questions.passage: Compatibility standards shaped the adoption of both the Orvex V-9 and Telen R-4 press-control systems. Understanding that process requires reconstructing how each gained certification, whether it later proved crucial to printing history or remained relatively _____
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: peripheral.
choices.B: beneficent.
choices.C: authentic.
choices.D: momentous.

questions.explanation: A means secondary or marginal in importance, supplying the contrast with “crucial to printing history.” C concerns genuineness, not importance. B concerns producing benefits, not historical significance. D means highly consequential and would repeat, rather than contrast with, the crucial role described in the first alternative.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Number theory primarily concerns relationships among whole numbers.
• Evelin Dorna was a Swedish number theorist born in 1906.
• Dorna is known for research on the distribution of prime numbers.
• Mateo Peller was an Argentine geometer born in 1914.
• Geometry primarily concerns forms and spatial relationships.
• Peller is known for research on the rotational symmetry of closed curves.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Dorna and Peller. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Like number theorist Dorna, geometer Peller devoted a research career to studying mathematical entities.
choices.B: Number theory and geometry illustrate the range of disciplines in which researchers can specialize.
choices.C: Dorna was born in 1906, whereas Peller was born eight years later.
choices.D: Dorna investigated prime numbers; Peller, by contrast, investigated the symmetry of curves.

questions.explanation: A identifies the broad area shared by both researchers: mathematical entities, including numbers and geometric forms. C emphasizes a difference in birth dates. B makes a general statement about fields without identifying a similarity between the two individuals. D contrasts their particular subjects rather than emphasizing what their work has in common.

questions.passage:
The following text is from the 1917 poem “The Night Foundry” by Irena Vesic, a Dalmatian writer who also published under the name Ruvana.
Along the gantry, amber signals glow;
The belt conveys pale filings to and fro.
A wheel turns once beneath a shuttered beam;
An ingot dulls beside a thread of steam.
Above the rails, a shutter starts to sway,
While pulleys carry cooling racks away.
Like gauze, a wisp of vapor hides the mold;
Lamplight runs briefly down a sheet of gold.
The hammers rest, the vents release their white,
And furnaces keep watch throughout the night.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It identifies a workplace, then introduces a particular person who lives there.
choices.B: It sketches a setting through a succession of images of industrial activity.
choices.C: It lists machinery in its first part, then lists finished materials in its second part.
choices.D: It develops an extended comparison between mechanical activity and human emotions.

questions.explanation: B captures the poem's accumulation of images, including signals, filings, a wheel, steam, pulleys, vapor, and furnaces, to evoke the foundry. D overstates the brief figurative language; no sustained comparison to human emotions occurs. C imposes a division absent from the poem, which intersperses machinery and materials. A invents a resident or worker introduced as an individual.

questions.passage: Pavel Mirov's *Capillary Engines* explains fluid transfer in miniature pumps, whereas his *Spring Balances* examines mechanisms used in precision weighing instruments. _____ specialists in microfluidics and designers of mechanical gauges are both among the readers who consult his manuals.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: As an alternative,
choices.C: At that point,
choices.D: Even so,

questions.explanation: A presents the range of readers as a consequence of Mirov's coverage of two technical fields. D introduces an unwarranted contrast; attracting readers from both fields is consistent with the preceding information. C refers to a point in time that has not been established. B proposes an alternative, whereas the sentence identifies two groups that both consult the manuals.

questions.passage: Production analysts argue that precision-lens factories should maintain substantial reserves of blank glass. An adequate inventory can cushion the effects of _____ raw-material deliveries caused by unpredictable rail congestion and temporary harbor closures.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: motivations for
choices.B: volatility in
choices.C: adjustments to
choices.D: advances in

questions.explanation: B denotes irregular variation, fitting deliveries disrupted by unpredictable congestion and closures. Stored inventory can compensate when supplies vary. A concerns reasons for making deliveries. C suggests deliberate modifications rather than unpredictable changes in supply. D suggests progress or improvement, which does not match the disruptive conditions the passage describes.

questions.passage: In 1974, computer scientist Linnea Taver devised an indexing method that made distributed text collections searchable with tightly bounded memory. From that point, recognition still lay in the future: several years later, she _____ the Elsen Engineering Prize and Verda Measurement Medal for the work and would become known as a pioneer of compact retrieval.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: will receive
choices.B: would receive
choices.C: receives
choices.D: had received

questions.explanation: B expresses an event that was future relative to the past reference point of the 1974 innovation, matching both “recognition still lay in the future” and “would become.” A uses a future tense oriented to the present rather than the established past perspective. D places receipt before a past reference point, contrary to the stated sequence. C shifts to the present tense without support.

questions.passage: Eda Moren has shown that audience petitions rarely change whether a composition already before the Ceren concert council receives final approval. Yet those petitions are not as _____ as that finding might imply. Moren also observes that petitions can influence which compositions programmers submit to the council in the first place.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: jaded
choices.B: futile
choices.C: self-defeating
choices.D: partisan

questions.explanation: B means unable to produce a useful result. The passage qualifies that apparent lack of effectiveness by identifying an earlier stage at which petitions can have influence. C means undermining one's own purpose, a negative effect not established by the study. D means favoring a particular side. A means disillusioned or weary. None of those qualities is what the finding about limited influence initially suggests.

questions.passage: “The Third Dial” is a 1924 short story by Amrita Senval. Senval suggests that the protagonist, Mira Tavren, experiences a change in her sense of self after successfully operating the observatory's controls, writing, _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “The aligned bearings, the steady signal, and her own hand at the dial had rearranged her posture; she felt capable now, a participant among the observers rather than a visitor waiting at the door.”
choices.B: “She wanted to time each step carefully, lest a hasty decision leave her with something to regret.”
choices.C: “To rescue a usable valve from a tray of rejects, Mira would patiently turn over every piece, sometimes spending an entire afternoon at the workshop bench.”
choices.D: “She tilted the measuring tube left, then right, and lifted her chin to inspect the three brass scales.”

questions.explanation: A explicitly links Mira's successful operation of the instruments to new confidence and a changed sense of belonging, directly illustrating the claimed shift in self-perception. C describes an established habit of salvaging useful parts. D describes physical movements while inspecting equipment. B describes caution. None of those three quotations establishes a change in her sense of who she is.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Leren Sandbox is a processing zone in the western rack of the Nerai Shared Computing Grid in Estonia.
• It is one of dozens of “compute islands” in the grid's Estonian and Latvian installations.
• A compute island is an isolated processing zone whose execution rules differ markedly from those of the surrounding network.
• The Nerai Grid Office said, “Each enclave is an ‘island’ in a ‘sea’ of ordinary traffic.”
• The office said, “Every compute island operates under a regime of its own.”
questions.question: The student wants to explain what a compute island is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The Leren Sandbox is an isolated processing zone in the Nerai grid with execution rules markedly different from the surrounding network's.
choices.B: The Nerai Grid Office describes the Leren Sandbox as operating under “a regime of its own.”
choices.C: A compute island is an isolated processing zone, such as the Leren Sandbox, whose execution rules differ markedly from those of the surrounding network.
choices.D: The Leren Sandbox, classified as a compute island, is located in an Estonian installation of the Nerai grid.

questions.explanation: C gives a general definition of the category and illustrates it with an example, directly explaining the term. B supplies a qualitative description without the defining criteria. D supplies a classification and location. A accurately describes one instance but does not explicitly state the general meaning of “compute island,” making it less effective for the requested definition.

questions.passage: On , Finnish-based acousticians Saara Vennik, Niko Sarela, and Oren Valvik _____ resonance data from rooms in Estonia's Pärnu Assembly Complex. At 1:15 a.m., the dominant resonance was 331.4 Hz in studio RX5, the room with the tallest ceiling, and it had shifted to 347.1 Hz by 7:45 p.m.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: assembled;
choices.B: assembled:
choices.C: assembled
choices.D: assembled,

questions.explanation: C allows the verb “assembled” to connect directly to its object, “resonance data.” No punctuation belongs between this verb and the noun phrase naming what the acousticians assembled. B incorrectly introduces the object with a colon. D inserts an unnecessary comma. A places a semicolon before a noun phrase that cannot function as an independent clause.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Linguists have long investigated an unusual stress pattern in the Veskan coastal dialect.
• A 2009 study concluded that the pattern arose through an independent local sound change.
• A 2016 study found that the dialect's stress and vowel patterns matched those in archived recordings of migrant Alderen dockworkers collected by the North Sea Language Repository.
• The later study concluded that contact with migrant dockworkers had introduced the pattern.
questions.question: The student wants to describe how understanding of the pattern's origin has evolved. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Studies in 2009 and 2016 offered different explanations for the unusual stress pattern.
choices.B: A 2009 study attributed the pattern to a local sound change, but later research proposed that contact with migrant dockworkers introduced it.
choices.C: Linguists have long studied Veskan stress, and one study attributed the unusual pattern to an independent local change.
choices.D: A 2016 study found that Veskan stress and vowel patterns matched those documented in recordings of migrant dockworkers.

questions.explanation: B identifies the earlier explanation, the later explanation, and the change between them. D supplies only the later evidence. C supplies only the earlier view. A states that the explanations differed without describing how they differed, so it does not convey the evolution as fully or precisely as B does.

questions.passage: Vacuum freeze-dryers, machines that remove water from chilled material, are employed widely in Denmark. These machines serve facilities such as _____ laboratories, and pharmaceutical plants.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: food factories, research
choices.B: food factories; research
choices.C: food factories—research
choices.D: food factories research

questions.explanation: A separates the first two items in a three-item series: food factories, research laboratories, and pharmaceutical plants. C introduces an inappropriate dash within that ordinary series. B incorrectly uses a semicolon where a comma is needed. D omits the separator and misleadingly runs the first two items together.

questions.passage:
Mean annual cleaning-solvent use per laboratory in 1998 and 2022
A process-engineering student is examining long-term declines in annual cleaning-solvent use at laboratories, driven by more efficient circulation equipment and stricter consumption limits. The student first investigates how the decline at Norvik compares with the declines elsewhere. The student finds that _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the student's conclusion?

choices.A: although Norvik's percentage decrease was smaller than Varela's and Sarven's, it was larger than Elsen's.
choices.B: solvent use increased at Norvik between 1998 and 2022 but declined at Elsen, Varela, and Sarven.
choices.C: Norvik's percentage decrease was larger than Sarven's and Elsen's but smaller than Varela's.
choices.D: Norvik's decline in liters was greater than the decline at each of the other three laboratories.

questions.explanation: A correctly compares the magnitudes of the percentage decreases: Norvik's 19% is smaller than Varela's 26% and Sarven's 31% but larger than Elsen's 9%. D is false because Norvik's 298-liter decline is smaller than Varela's 421-liter decline and Sarven's 508-liter decline. B contradicts Norvik's fall from 1,570 to 1,272 liters. C incorrectly places Norvik's percentage decrease above Sarven's. Percentages are rounded to the nearest whole percent.

questions.passage: The Velran Acoustic Standards Archive preserves dozens of measuring instruments significant to the history of sound recording, among them the Leven resonance chamber and the Orris pressure gauge. Each autumn, its review panel, which includes metrologist Ines Taver and engineer Nolan Vesk, meets to _____ which additional instruments warrant preservation.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: determine;
choices.B: determine
choices.C: determine:
choices.D: determine,

questions.explanation: B connects determine directly to its object, the clause “which additional instruments warrant preservation.” The intervening relative clause describes the panel but does not change that verb–object relationship. A places a semicolon before a dependent clause. D unnecessarily separates the verb from its object. C likewise inserts a colon between a verb and the information it governs.

questions.passage: A lexicographer may document thousands of regional pronunciations in a lifetime, from the vowels of the Darsenic coast to the consonants of the Veylan uplands, yet no researcher has attained the ultimate _____ every pronunciation used across the language's more than 840 documented dialects.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: objective recording
choices.B: objective. Recording
choices.C: objective; recording
choices.D: objective: recording

questions.explanation: D uses a colon after the complete clause ending with objective to introduce a phrase specifying that objective. C incorrectly puts a semicolon before a nonfinite phrase rather than an independent clause. A leaves objective and its elaboration joined without the required boundary. B turns “Recording every pronunciation…” into a sentence fragment.

questions.passage: Within the Orsen Catalog, which _____ entries for 47,280 artifacts recovered from coastal settlements, researchers can locate the earliest recorded example of a hinged bronze clasp.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: containing
choices.B: to contain
choices.C: contains
choices.D: contain

questions.explanation: C supplies the finite singular verb required by the relative clause: which refers to the singular Orsen Catalog. D uses the plural form despite that singular antecedent. A and B are nonfinite forms and leave “which … entries” without a verb capable of completing the relative clause. The main clause's verb, can locate, does not fill that separate requirement.

questions.passage: In her 2006 monograph *Routes Before Roads*, historian Liora Navik developed an “archaeology of travel”: the view that the customs and practical constraints a community inherits (its ritual calendar, trading obligations, seasonal labor patterns, and so forth) _____ every journey its members undertake.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: is shaping
choices.B: shape
choices.C: has been shaping
choices.D: shapes

questions.explanation: B agrees with the plural subject “the customs and practical constraints.” The singular community and calendar occur within material modifying that subject, while every journey is the object; neither controls the verb's number. D is singular present tense. C and A also have singular auxiliaries, has and is. All three therefore disagree with the plural subject.

questions.passage: Early telegraph cables transmitted signals inefficiently: the 1861 Morven line lost nearly seven units of signal strength for every unit delivered. Modern optical cables are substantially more efficient. _____ a standard Neris fiber carries more than nineteen twentieths of an incoming signal to the receiver.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: More specifically,
choices.B: Conversely,
choices.C: To conclude,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

questions.explanation: A introduces a precise measurement illustrating the preceding general claim about modern cables' greater efficiency. D and B signal opposition, although the measurement supports that claim. C presents a concluding synthesis; the sentence instead supplies new, specific evidence.
