The earlier historical comparison does not make the final supporting detail a contrast with the immediately preceding sentence.

questions.passage: Designers associated with speculative cartography, a practice that gained attention in the 2000s, deliberately alter the apparent certainty of printed maps. Mara Virel, for instance, renders administrative borders as drifting bands rather than fixed lines. Even practitioners who avoid such bands, including Olek Senn, often replace uniform place labels with overlapping accounts supplied by residents. Their persistent disruption of a map's authoritative appearance invites readers to consider how institutions organize the spaces people inhabit today.
questions.question: Which description of the altered maps is best supported by the text?

choices.A: They demonstrate that contemporary institutions have made everyday navigation less reliable.
choices.B: They preserve a stable human understanding of place despite changes in mapping techniques.
choices.C: They offer a reflection on the institutional conditions shaping contemporary life.
choices.D: They prove that map design can determine readers' personal identities.

questions.explanation: C captures the stated purpose: prompting reflection on how institutions organize inhabited space. A turns that reflection into a negative judgment about navigation that the text never makes. B claims stability even though the designs unsettle familiar representations. D exaggerates an invitation to reflect into proof that design determines identity. The examples support commentary on present social conditions, not those stronger claims.

questions.passage: The varel, which was stamped as a split diamond beside a maker's name, and the lint, which appeared as three nested squares on a workshop seal, were old systems of _____ to distinguish ownership and production batches, respectively; both systems eventually disappeared.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: classification used
choices.B: classification. Used
choices.C: classification; used
choices.D: classification and to use

questions.explanation: A joins classification to the participial modifier “used to distinguish…” without disrupting the clause. B creates a fragment beginning Used. C puts a semicolon before a phrase that lacks an independent subject and finite verb. D introduces to use without a parallel construction to support it. The existing semicolon correctly separates the two complete clauses later in the sentence.

questions.passage: The Vorren codices are commonly regarded in antiquarian circles as evidence of exceptional scholarship on the part of anyone who can decipher them. Their script is unusual, but it is no harder to learn than several other scripts used in surviving merchant records. Historian Elda Navik traces their reputation to collectors active in the 1820s, who circulated accounts of the years of solitary study supposedly required to read them. Navik considers those accounts self-serving. She suggests that collectors promoted this reputation in order to _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: portray themselves as unusually learned and persistent for mastering an allegedly formidable script.
choices.B: encourage a broader public to begin collecting ordinary merchant records.
choices.C: establish that Vorren records survived in more regions than other merchant documents did.
choices.D: provide linguists with unbiased observations about the script's distinctive features.

questions.explanation: A connects the exaggerated difficulty with a benefit to the collectors' own reputations, explaining self-serving. C introduces a claim about geographic distribution. B proposes a benefit to prospective collectors rather than the stated self-interested motive. D presents neutral scholarly reporting, inconsistent with exaggerating a difficulty the text says was unexceptional.

questions.passage: Chef Mirela Varen combines inherited fermentation practices with laboratory techniques such as calibrated acidity testing. Raised in a family of cheesemakers near Buzet, she later studied analytical chemistry. The traditional and experimental _____ reveal both parts of her background.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: procedures that Varen incorporates into her recipes
choices.B: procedures, that Varen incorporates into her recipes,
choices.C: procedures, that Varen incorporates into her recipes
choices.D: procedures that Varen incorporates into her recipes,

questions.explanation: A keeps the restrictive that-clause attached to procedures and leaves the complete subject directly connected to reveal. B incorrectly encloses the restrictive modifier in commas. D separates the subject from its verb. C inserts a comma before that while failing to create any correctly delimited supplementary construction.

questions.passage: In Tartu, the Velsar Manuscript Laboratory records changes in ink composition across Baltic nautical _____ in Valletta, the Merien Conservation Center studies comparable changes in Mediterranean port ledgers. Together, the laboratories contribute to the Maritime Records Consortium, or MRC, as conservator Lidia Senn calls it.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: journals,
choices.B: journals;
choices.C: journals and
choices.D: journals

questions.explanation: B places a semicolon between two independent clauses, each with its own introductory location, subject, and verb. A creates a comma splice. D runs the clauses together. C uses and without the comma required to join these substantial independent clauses; the second clause begins with the introductory phrase “in Valletta.”

questions.passage: Some archival databases incorporate identification codes imported from unrelated record systems. Codes first developed for restricted research collections in the 1980s were adopted by commercial genealogy services in the 1990s and now appear in municipal public-record portals. A student studying information policy argues that the migration of these codes into public databases could have serious adverse consequences over time.
questions.question: Which quotation from a researcher would best support the student's argument?

choices.A: “Some publicly accessible research collections contain approximately equal numbers of codes imported from outside sources and codes generated locally, while other collections contain a larger number of imported codes than locally generated codes.”
choices.B: “Imported codes have been observed in public collections, but studies of their effects remain insufficient.”
choices.C: “Public databases using imported codes may be more numerous than the databases that researchers have identified so far.”
choices.D: “As codes spread through linked collections, they can enable readers to connect anonymized records to named individuals, exposing those individuals to identity fraud.”

questions.explanation: D identifies a mechanism for lasting harm: spread across linked collections can defeat anonymity and expose people to fraud. A reports proportions without demonstrating damage. C suggests wider distribution but not negative consequences. B identifies a research gap rather than evidence of harm. Only D connects the codes' migration with the adverse effects the student predicts.

questions.passage: When instrument conservator Ilara Voss returned to Lisbon in 1954 after eleven years abroad, her approach to technical writing changed abruptly. <u>Abandoning the deductive manuals she had favored (texts that build practical recommendations from general principles rather than observations of individual cases), she began compiling closely documented accounts of damaged instruments and their repairs.</u> Drawing on workshop logs and apprentices' notebooks, these accounts organized precise, economical descriptions around particular failures rather than a comprehensive theory.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains more precisely the change in Voss's writing introduced in the preceding sentence.
choices.B: It documents Voss's travels to substantiate the following sentence's account of her influences.
choices.C: It describes a personal event that made the later success of Voss's career possible.
choices.D: It challenges the preceding sentence's account of Voss's professional development.

questions.explanation: A captures the sentence's elaborating role: it identifies the earlier method and the case-based approach that replaced it. D reverses the relationship; the sentence supports, rather than challenges, the announced change. C mistakes a professional shift for a personal event and invents subsequent success. B focuses on travel, which the underlined sentence does not discuss.

questions.passage:
Training consultations recorded at two restoration workshops
Learning researchers Soraya Venn and Edren Orlis studied apprentices' consultations with experienced restorers. Local-track apprentices generally remain at their home workshop throughout their careers, whereas touring-track apprentices move between workshops. The researchers hypothesized that local-track apprentices benefit more from consulting mentors permanently based at their home workshop, a difference they expected to appear in consultation patterns.
questions.question: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers' hypothesis?

choices.A: Apprentice 14 had a larger local-mentor proportion than apprentice 11, and apprentice 27 had a larger proportion than apprentice 29.
choices.B: Apprentice 27 had 29 consultations, more than either apprentice 14 or apprentice 11.
choices.C: The proportion of consultations directed to local mentors ranged from 0.00 to 0.86.
choices.D: Local-track apprentices 14 and 11 directed larger proportions of their consultations to local mentors than touring-track apprentices 27 and 29 did.

questions.explanation: D compares the relevant training groups: the local-track proportions, 0.86 and 0.63, both exceed the touring-track proportions, 0.14 and 0.00. C gives the overall range without connecting it to training path. A compares apprentices within each path, not between paths. B concerns total consultations rather than the proportion directed to the mentors named in the hypothesis. Proportions are rounded to two decimal places.

questions.passage: In a 2017 analysis, transport researchers used a statistical model to estimate how quickly different delivery routes were redesigned. Routes serving temporary exhibition venues changed most rapidly; _____ routes serving permanent archival depots changed most slowly.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: meanwhile,
choices.B: similarly,
choices.C: accordingly,
choices.D: subsequently,

questions.explanation: A juxtaposes two contrasting results from the same analysis without implying that either caused or followed the other. C would make the second result a consequence of the first. B signals similarity despite the opposing rates. D introduces a chronological sequence that the analysis does not establish.

questions.passage: Recent archival research has challenged the claim that the reports of nineteenth-century engineer Sorin Vales were _____ other bridge designers of his generation. What remains certain is that his workshop's location in a remote coastal district placed his manuscripts hundreds of kilometers from the period's principal engineering academies.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: copied extensively by
choices.B: openly hostile toward
choices.C: controversial among
choices.D: of little consequence to

questions.explanation: D concerns the reports' limited influence, a claim the first sentence says is now challenged even though their geographic isolation is certain. A asserts extensive imitation rather than limited significance. B describes hostility toward the designers. C concerns controversy. Neither hostility nor controversy follows from the text's contrast between uncertain influence and indisputable distance.

questions.passage: Historian Mirela Orsen, of the Darsenic Institute for Material Culture, _____ seals and commercial trust in early port communities, particularly how devices such as the varel (a split-diamond ownership stamp) and the lint (a nested-square workshop mark) helped merchants establish obligations, reputations, and trading identities.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: investigate
choices.B: have investigated
choices.C: are investigating
choices.D: investigates

questions.explanation: D agrees with the singular subject Historian Mirela Orsen. The institute's name and the later plural seals and devices do not control the verb. A is the plural present-tense form. B and C use plural auxiliaries, have and are. The material between the subject and verb is an appositive location phrase, not an additional subject.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Nerien Oral History Repository is directed by conservator Elda Savel.
• Savel oversaw the creation of online copies of historic wax-cylinder recordings from island communities.
• The repository digitized more than 8,400 recordings, including interviews with boatbuilders and harbor workers.
• The cylinders remained with the institutions in their communities of origin.
• Researchers can now consult the recordings more readily.
questions.question: The student wants to explain an advantage of making the repository digital. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: More than 8,400 recordings, including boatbuilders' interviews, belong to the Nerien digital collection.
choices.B: Elda Savel directed the initiative that produced online copies of historic recordings.
choices.C: Interviews with harbor workers are among the historic recordings available through the repository.
choices.D: By making recordings available online, the repository expands research access while allowing the original cylinders to remain in their home communities.

questions.explanation: D connects the digital format to its benefits: increased access without relocating the originals. A states the collection's size and an example but does not explain the format's advantage. B identifies the initiative's leader. C describes its contents. Those details are supported, but none explains the benefit as directly as D.

questions.passage: The Velsar Materials Survey follows the deterioration of stonework in 16,700 buildings over several decades. Like most longitudinal projects, it incurs substantial costs because observations must be collected for many years. A simpler survey designed only to determine what proportion of a city's buildings currently use sandstone, by contrast, may need a comparatively modest budget because _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: 16,700 buildings provide more than enough observations to detect long-term deterioration.
choices.B: longitudinal methods would probably suit the simpler survey's purpose.
choices.C: the simpler survey can achieve its purpose without collecting observations over many years.
choices.D: the Velsar survey could readily add questions about sandstone to its existing observations.

questions.explanation: C removes the expense-generating requirement identified in the passage: repeated data collection over time. D concerns adding questions to a different project. B would retain, rather than explain avoiding, longitudinal costs. A evaluates the larger study's sample size without explaining the simpler study's lower budget.

questions.passage: Archivists describe the Varen review system as a four-tier process. At its base, intake clerks register incoming records; at the second tier, catalogers verify descriptions; and at the third, a specialist panel resolves disputed identifications. _____ at the fourth and highest tier, the chief conservator approves entries for the permanent catalog.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Lastly,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: In fact,
choices.D: Besides,

questions.explanation: A marks the final stage of the ordered progression from the first tier to the fourth. B would introduce an example of an earlier stage. C signals confirmation or emphasis rather than sequence. D adds an unranked extra point, overlooking the explicitly ordered levels that organize the passage.

questions.passage: The Orsen framework, a reconstructed system of surveying conventions, is sometimes described as the ancestor of all Nerian boundary maps. That attribution remains _____ the framework itself has been inferred from the shared features of twenty-one later systems rather than directly documented.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: provisional, however,
choices.B: provisional, however;
choices.C: provisional however
choices.D: provisional; however

questions.explanation: B sets off however as a contrast with the previous assertion and places a semicolon between the independent clauses ending with provisional and beginning with the framework. A joins those clauses with commas alone. C runs them together without a proper boundary. D places however at the start of the second clause without the comma required to separate that transitional adverb from the clause.

questions.passage: Market researchers Ilara Venn and Olek Savel found that intense online attention reduces independent dealers' willingness to publish advance catalogs. They explain this result through costs and benefits: additional publicity may not increase sales enough to offset the risk that competitors will copy the advertised selections. Many dealers respond similarly, but auction houses specializing in unfamiliar decorative objects show the opposite pattern, since their reliance on customers' visual inspection changes the balance of reward and risk.
questions.question: According to the text, what did Venn and Savel find, and why?

choices.A: Independent dealers publish more advance catalogs under intense scrutiny because publicity raises sales without increasing the risk of copying.
choices.B: Specialist auction houses respond differently because publicity exposes them to greater risks than independent dealers face.
choices.C: Independent dealers publish fewer advance catalogs under intense scrutiny because the increased risk of copying outweighs the additional sales the publicity might bring.
choices.D: Independent dealers publish fewer catalogs because their selections are easier to copy than those offered by specialist auction houses.

questions.explanation: C accurately states both the reduced publication and the unfavorable cost–benefit balance. A reverses the finding and denies the stated risk. D invents a comparison of ease of copying. B attributes the exception to greater risk, whereas the passage emphasizes the auction houses' stronger benefit from visual exposure.

questions.passage: Urban researchers Soraya Taver and Edren Neris found that heavy pedestrian traffic discourages portable repair stalls from operating in narrow market streets. Crowds can bring additional customers, but the resulting delays and equipment damage may outweigh that benefit. Most other mobile services respond to crowds in the same way. Portrait sketchers, however, become more active: because their work depends on attracting observers, the balance of reward and risk differs.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It summarizes several similar studies and attributes a conflicting result to a change in research methods.
choices.B: It states a finding and explains it, places it within a broader pattern, and then presents and explains an exception.
choices.C: It introduces a behavioral pattern and its explanation, then gives an exception that disproves that explanation.
choices.D: It compares two responses to a condition, explains one, and leaves the other unexplained.

questions.explanation: B follows the passage's progression from the repair-stall finding and its explanation to a general pattern and an explained exception. D overlooks the explanation of sketchers' response. C mistakes a different cost–benefit balance for evidence disproving the original explanation. A invents studies with conflicting methods; the text compares services, not research designs.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Veylan Clock Museum in Pula displays an optical timing apparatus.
• The apparatus projects flashes from a lamp onto a strip moving beneath it.
• The lamp flashes at fixed intervals.
• Wider gaps between marks on the strip indicate that the strip moved farther between successive flashes.
• The apparatus demonstrates the relationship between distance traveled and speed.
questions.question: The student wants to explain how the apparatus provides evidence of a change in speed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A flashing lamp and a moving strip form an optical timing apparatus.
choices.B: At fixed flash intervals, wider gaps between marks mean the strip traveled farther during the same elapsed time and therefore moved faster.
choices.C: The Pula museum uses an optical apparatus to demonstrate the relationship between distance and speed.
choices.D: The lamp flashes at fixed intervals while the strip moves through the apparatus.

questions.explanation: B links the observed spacing to distance, equal time intervals, and speed, explaining the mechanism. A identifies components. C states the demonstration's purpose. D describes operation without explaining what wider gaps show. Although D supplies a relevant fact, only B completes the requested causal explanation.

questions.passage: The Varen Conservation Medal was established to publicly _____ exceptional restorers of historic instruments. In 2008, the medal was awarded to clockmaker Ilara Senn in acknowledgment of her decades of work preserving regional workshop traditions.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: familiarize
choices.B: convey
choices.C: astonish
choices.D: honor

questions.explanation: D means recognize achievement with respect, fitting the award and its acknowledgment of sustained contributions. A means make familiar with something. B means transmit or communicate. C means surprise greatly. None describes the purpose of an achievement medal.

questions.passage:
Annual production at four printing workshops, 2016
In 2018, production historians Veda Navik, Olek Savel, and Mirela Voss published a report on printing workshops operating in northern Italy in 2016. Data from that report appear in the table. Among the listed workshops, the one with the lowest annual production was in _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the assertion?

choices.A: Aosta.
choices.B: Rovigo.
choices.C: Liguria.
choices.D: Trentino.

questions.explanation: B follows from the smallest annual total, Velsar Press's 1,840 volumes, and its region, Rovigo. Aosta's workshop produced 14,690 volumes, Trentino's 176,430, and Liguria's 12,720. The number of machines and operating mode are not the quantities the assertion asks readers to compare.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Workshop Clocks of the Adriatic is a reference guide by conservators Elda Varen, Niko Orlis, and Soraya Taver.
• It describes forty-three clock models manufactured in Istria.
• The Lintaro mantel clock is a large model manufactured in Istria.
• It has a curved brass case and a long, black minute hand.
• The Vescari travel clock is a small model manufactured in Istria.
• It has a dark green case and a short, upward-curving winding key.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two clocks. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A long, black minute hand and a curved brass case identify the large Lintaro mantel clock.
choices.B: The small Vescari travel clock has a dark green case and an upward-curving winding key.
choices.C: Although the two models share a region of manufacture, the Lintaro mantel clock is larger than the Vescari travel clock.
choices.D: Both the Lintaro mantel clock and the Vescari travel clock are among the guide's forty-three Istrian models.

questions.explanation: C explicitly compares the clocks' sizes, fulfilling the request for a difference. D emphasizes a similarity. B and A each describe only one model; their facts are supported, but neither directly contrasts the two clocks.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Eleni Vares's 1891 short story “*The Room of Echoes*,” collected in *The Room of Echoes* and Other Stories (translated by Anton Savel in 1911). The narrator has entered a music hall in Trieste during an afternoon rehearsal.
I lingered under the balcony, letting the unfinished melody gather around me. The account books, the countinghouse, the supervisor's clipped instructions, all slipped from reach; in their place came the bright uncertainty of performances I had yet to hear, of rooms not yet entered. Then a phrase from the violins opened a door much older than these anticipations. I was again a child beside my aunt's instrument, waiting through her pauses, while the dusty light of the hall seemed to shine upon both moments at once.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: The hall's music draws the narrator away from work concerns into hopes for the future and memories of childhood.
choices.B: The narrator decides to abandon his job and return permanently to his childhood home.
choices.C: The narrator visits the hall to assess how musical training might advance his present career.
choices.D: The narrator neglects urgent professional duties because the rehearsal distracts him.

questions.explanation: A encompasses the passage's movement from forgotten work to future possibilities and recalled childhood. D invents urgency and neglect. C assigns a career-planning purpose absent from the text. B converts a remembered scene into a decision about employment and residence. Neither the anticipation nor the memory is presented as an actual plan.

questions.passage: Some metrologists maintain that a measurement's quality depends solely on its numerical precision, regardless of the setting in which it is used. Historian Soraya Neris finds a different view in surviving manuals from the Velran instrument guilds: measurements were assessed by how well they served an instrument's assigned function and supported the workshop's shared tasks. To the extent that these manuals represent guild practice, Neris's analysis suggests that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: guild members would have resisted evaluating measurements by standards entirely independent of their practical setting.
choices.B: a measurement from a highly productive workshop would have been judged adequate even if it violated standards the guilds applied in every setting.
choices.C: guild members would have rejected evaluations made by anyone outside their own workshop.
choices.D: identical measurements from instruments with different functions would have been judged equivalent unless the workshops' total output differed.

questions.explanation: A follows from judging measurements by function and shared use rather than context-free precision alone. C adds a prohibition on outside evaluators. B invents both universal guild standards and an exception for productive workshops. D ignores the stated importance of an instrument's assigned function, treating output as the only possible contextual difference.

questions.passage: When choosing exhibits, regional science centers often put visitor familiarity ahead of experimental presentation. A center might readily display a conventional working planetarium but be _____ to commission an installation from an untested designer whose approach visitors could find difficult to follow.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: reluctant
choices.B: resolved
choices.C: astonished
choices.D: fortunate

questions.explanation: A expresses the hesitation expected when an institution prioritizes familiar experiences over risk. B implies determination to commission the unfamiliar work, reversing the contrast. D describes luck rather than willingness. C describes surprise, not the reservation about committing to an uncertain exhibit.

questions.passage: On a sloping desk in the Nerien Museum rests a 31-by-48-centimeter _____ which was compiled in 1926 by instrument keeper Elda Orlis.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: ledger, *Ledger of Lantern Repairs*
choices.B: ledger *Ledger of Lantern Repairs*
choices.C: ledger *Ledger of Lantern Repairs*,
choices.D: ledger, *Ledger of Lantern Repairs*,

questions.explanation: C keeps the identifying title attached to ledger and places the comma before the supplementary which-clause. A opens an unnecessary interruption before the title and does not close it. D unnecessarily separates the identifying title from the noun it specifies. B omits the boundary introducing the supplementary information about the named ledger.

questions.passage: The Narven night market in Split develops through _____ influences: vendors' menus shape the visitors a district attracts, while those visitors' preferences gradually reshape the menus vendors offer.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: inflexible
choices.B: interdependent
choices.C: comprehensive
choices.D: tenuous

questions.explanation: B describes factors that affect one another, matching the two-way relationship between menus and visitor preferences. C means broad or complete. A means resistant to change, contrary to the stated reshaping. D means weak or insubstantial, a quality the passage does not establish.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Lidia Varen's 1923 novella *A Voice at the Terminus*. Meren has briefly heard an unfamiliar singer while traveling with a companion.
Meren remained beside the carriage, absorbed in the vanished refrain. Like a person roused from sleep who reaches for a dream before its outlines dissolve, he struggled to recover the melody, yet could retain only the warmth it had left behind, the warmth! Soon even that last trace escaped him.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does “recover” most nearly mean?

choices.A: Initiate
choices.B: Disregard
choices.C: Remember
choices.D: Separate

questions.explanation: C fits the attempt to bring a fading melody back to mind, reinforced by the comparison to remembering a dream. D suggests division, A suggests beginning, and B suggests deliberate inattention. None describes Meren's effort to retain a mental impression.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Suspension roofs span open spaces without intermediate supporting columns.
• Cables and anchoring towers are among their structural components.
• The Velren Canopy is a suspension roof in Slovenia.
• Researchers date its construction to 1874.
• Its unsupported span is approximately 86 meters.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the canopy's large unsupported span. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Researchers have examined the construction of the Velren Canopy, an 86-meter-span suspension roof built in Slovenia.
choices.B: A suspension roof now known as the Velren Canopy was constructed during the nineteenth century.
choices.C: Built in 1874, Slovenia's Velren Canopy is a suspension roof with a remarkable unsupported span of approximately 86 meters.
choices.D: Cables and anchoring towers allow suspension roofs such as the Velren Canopy to cover open spaces.

questions.explanation: C foregrounds the span with both its measurement and an explicit characterization of its scale. D emphasizes structural components. A centers researchers' examination and includes size as a secondary identifying detail. B emphasizes construction history without giving the span. C therefore most directly achieves the stated rhetorical goal.

questions.passage: In Valnera, covered walkways such as the 1.84-kilometer Orsen Arcade have become increasingly popular routes during the rainy season. Furthermore, planner and pedestrian _____ has identified features of the city's layout, including short blocks and sheltered crossings, that make walking particularly practical.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: advocate Mirela Senn,
choices.B: advocate, Mirela Senn,
choices.C: advocate, Mirela Senn
choices.D: advocate Mirela Senn

questions.explanation: D keeps the identifying name directly attached to the title and joins the complete subject to has identified. B unnecessarily isolates the name. A separates the subject from its verb. C opens an interruption before the identifying name without closing it. Neither the title–name unit nor its connection to the predicate calls for a comma.

questions.passage: Small instrument-making workshops multiplied across the Veylan province in the early 1900s. Selra supported fourteen new workshops between 1906 and 1916, but Darsen exceeded every other town in the province, establishing twenty-nine during the same period. Darsen bordered the Orlis Technical Academy and had long housed a substantial population of mechanics and apprentices. Its emergence as an especially productive center of instrument making is therefore unsurprising.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To show that instrument making flourished in Veylan, especially in Darsen, during the early 1900s
choices.B: To compare present-day Veylan workshops with those active a century earlier
choices.C: To explain why Veylan instruments were particularly popular in neighboring provinces
choices.D: To argue that Darsen's workshops directly shaped the methods used in Selra

questions.explanation: A covers both the province-wide growth and the emphasis on Darsen, supported by counts and local circumstances. C introduces popularity elsewhere. B invents a present-day comparison. D asserts influence between towns that the passage does not describe. The comparison of workshop counts establishes prominence, not transmission of methods.

questions.passage: Botanical educator Ines Orlen's career, extending from the 1910s into the 1970s, passed through several stages. After visiting experimental gardens in Denmark and Japan in the late 1920s, she adopted teaching methods centered on direct observation and controlled comparison. Her courses for the Varen Horticultural School and two regional training institutes accordingly used paired growing plots, unlike the historical plant catalogs around which she had organized her early lessons in Pula.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Orlen initially preferred experimental instruction but later abandoned it for historical study.
choices.B: Orlen's early Pula lessons were more experimental than her later courses.
choices.C: A substantial change in Orlen's teaching reflected the influence of her visits abroad.
choices.D: All the institutions Orlen served became exemplary centers of experimental horticulture.

questions.explanation: C connects the change in methods with the international visits the passage identifies as its antecedent. A and B reverse the chronology of historical and experimental instruction. D extends a description of particular courses into a claim about entire institutions and their reputation, which the text does not support.

questions.passage: In a 2019 analysis of 240 delivery networks, researchers found that routes serving temporary venues were redesigned more rapidly than routes serving other destinations. _____ a route serving seasonal exhibition tents would be expected to change faster than one serving a permanent warehouse.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Moreover,
choices.B: Meanwhile,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: However,

questions.explanation: C marks the prediction as an inference from the general pattern: temporary exhibition destinations should require faster redesign than permanent ones. A presents an additional point without expressing that inferential connection. D incorrectly signals opposition. B suggests concurrent developments rather than a conclusion derived from the finding.

questions.passage: The Varen classification of fermented foods includes nerka, selvin, and roughly 940 other preparations across several coastal regions, making it a particularly broad culinary grouping and a subject of keen interest to _____ of the Institute for Food History.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: researcher, Soraya Navik,
choices.B: researcher: Soraya Navik
choices.C: researcher Soraya Navik
choices.D: researcher, Soraya Navik

questions.explanation: C joins the identifying name directly to the title researcher. The name is needed to specify which researcher is meant, so it should not be separated with commas or a colon. B misuses a colon within the noun phrase. A treats the identifying name as supplementary. D inserts an unnecessary, unmatched comma.

questions.passage: Double-walled glass and ceramic vessels retain heat well, whereas ordinary paper containers do not. Researchers had generally placed resin-treated paper cups in the latter category, but materials engineer Niko Varen's team tested that assumption. They filled treated cups with warm liquid and tracked cooling under controlled room conditions. <u>The cups retained heat substantially longer than untreated cups did, suggesting that their performance resembled that of insulated glass and ceramic vessels rather than ordinary paper containers.</u>
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It reports the study's result and the inference drawn from that result.
choices.B: It distinguishes two types of insulation used in the opening comparison.
choices.C: It explains why researchers originally classified the cups as poor insulators.
choices.D: It recommends a new study of the differences among insulating materials.

questions.explanation: A captures both the observed heat retention and the resulting reassessment. C concerns the origin of the earlier assumption, which the sentence does not explain. D invents a future recommendation. B mistakes a comparison interpreting the tested cups' performance for a distinction between the opening examples.

questions.passage: In 2011, a study led by cultural researcher Elda Orlen examined the relationship between museum visitors' engagement and printed _____ contextual details such as workshop histories, makers' biographies, and material descriptions, these guides may help visitors interpret unfamiliar objects more fully.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: guides including
choices.B: guides, which include
choices.C: guides. Including
choices.D: guides, including

questions.explanation: C ends the first independent clause and begins a new sentence with Including, a participial phrase modifying these guides. B turns which include into a relative clause but leaves the following main clause improperly attached by a comma. A and D likewise fail to place a proper boundary before the new independent clause “these guides may help…”.

questions.passage: Chef Ines Taver, along with colleagues such as Mara Vesk and Nolan Savel, _____ commonly associated with the Hearth Table movement, a loose network of cooks and growers active in the 1980s and 1990s who sought to reconnect regional menus with seasonal production.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: are
choices.B: is
choices.C: were
choices.D: have been

questions.explanation: B agrees with the singular subject Chef Ines Taver. The supplementary along with phrase names additional people but does not turn the subject into a plural one. C, D, and A all require a plural subject. The later network and its members belong to explanatory material, not the subject governing the blank.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Rovan scale ranks textile tear resistance on twelve levels.
• A fabric at a higher level withstands pulling forces that tear fabrics at lower levels.
• A lower-level fabric cannot withstand all the forces tolerated by a higher-level fabric.
• Miralin cloth has a Rovan rating of 3.
• Selva cloth has a rating of 6.
• Orsino cloth has a rating of 10.
questions.question: The student wants to compare the tear resistance of Miralin and Orsino. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The Rovan scale ranks Miralin, Selva, and Orsino by resistance to tearing.
choices.B: Orsino can withstand forces that tear Selva, explaining their different ratings.
choices.C: Selva's rating of 6 indicates greater tear resistance than Miralin's rating of 3.
choices.D: Orsino can withstand forces that tear Miralin and therefore has greater tear resistance.

questions.explanation: D compares the two requested fabrics and correctly applies the scale's direction. A describes the general ranking system. C compares Miralin with Selva, and B compares Orsino with Selva. Those supported comparisons do not address the requested pair.

questions.passage: Reusable festival badges often _____ laminated paper inserts that cannot be removed without damaging the surrounding plastic. Sustainability researcher Mirela Varen warns that when an insert becomes illegible, organizers commonly discard the entire badge, creating avoidable waste.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: contain
choices.B: identify
choices.C: formulate
choices.D: envision

questions.explanation: A means hold something within, fitting inserts physically enclosed in plastic badges. C means devise or express. D means imagine. B means recognize or specify. None describes the stated physical relationship between the badge and its insert.

questions.passage: Designers in the Lantern Table movement borrowed motifs from nocturnal landscapes. _____ the luminous spirals and moth-shaped clasps of Mirela Senn's festival garments could not literally have formed in a meadow. Still, their rounded silhouettes and insect-inspired details clearly reflect the movement's natural influences.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Likewise,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Of course,
choices.D: Accordingly,

questions.explanation: C acknowledges an obvious qualification: borrowing natural motifs does not mean garments actually grow in nature. Still then returns to the original claim despite that qualification. D incorrectly makes the qualification a consequence. A implies a parallel comparison, and B treats it as straightforward additional support.

questions.passage: The Ilara Varen Workshop in Koper occupies the rooms where Varen spent three years developing her later string instruments. <u>Today the workshop is a museum devoted to Varen's instruments and working methods.</u> Admirers visit to feel closer to the maker's practice. To encourage that connection, curators display her own tools and benches, helping visitors picture the daily routines through which her designs took shape.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It identifies the present function of the building introduced in the preceding sentence.
choices.B: It summarizes the maker's entire career.
choices.C: It recommends works by the maker introduced in the preceding sentence.
choices.D: It recounts the building's earlier history.

questions.explanation: A accurately identifies the shift from Varen's former working rooms to the building's current museum use. C invents a recommendation. B overstates a sentence about the museum's subject as a career summary. D reverses its temporal focus: the sentence explains what the building does today, not its earlier history.

questions.passage: Historians Elda Orlis and Nolan Vesk contributed their expertise to the Atlas of Coastal Fermentation, a digital _____ through a combination of recipes, workshop photographs, and recorded interviews, traces the development of regional practices such as nerka curing and selvin aging.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: resource, that
choices.B: resource that
choices.C: resource that,
choices.D: resource, that,

questions.explanation: C introduces a restrictive that-clause and supplies the opening comma for its interrupting through-phrase; the comma after interviews closes that interruption. B lacks the opening comma while leaving the closing one. D and A incorrectly separate resource from the restrictive that-clause. The relative clause's subject is that and its verb is traces.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Anton Vares's 1869 short story “*The Driver at Orsen Square*.” The narrator addresses the reader after describing a conversation among the driver's passengers.
How fortunate for Meren that he did not hear, as we did, the remarks exchanged behind the station! For which of us would welcome a careful comparison between the account we keep of our own conduct and the account entered by our neighbors? We carry ourselves forward on small loans from our self-esteem; alas, let a few sharp creditors demand repayment, and what strength remains! Even our willingness to do a kindly thing might fail us.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: The narrator summarizes an encounter and predicts the character's eventual fate.
choices.B: The narrator celebrates the resolution of a disagreement and considers an alternative outcome.
choices.C: The narrator notes a character's ignorance of others' opinions and then broadens the discussion to the difficulty of confronting others' judgments of oneself.
choices.D: The narrator suggests that neighbors dislike the character and then explains why their judgment is justified.

questions.explanation: C follows the move from Meren's fortunate ignorance to the inclusive “which of us” reflection on self-esteem. A invents a prediction about Meren. D mistakes a metaphor explaining threatened confidence for a defense of the neighbors' criticism. B introduces a resolved disagreement that the passage never describes.

questions.passage: Biographer Soraya Navik describes engineer Elda Voss as “a dweller in perpetual revision,” noting her habit of adjusting published manuals. Yet the differences between the 1934 and 1957 editions of *Canals of the Northern Plain* are unusually extensive even for Voss; _____ several historians treat the editions as separate works.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: by contrast,
choices.B: in fact,
choices.C: nevertheless,
choices.D: in other words,

questions.explanation: B introduces evidence reinforcing how extensive the revisions were: some historians regard the editions as different works. C and A incorrectly suggest that the historians' treatment contradicts the degree of change. D presents the statement as a restatement, although treating editions as separate works is stronger supporting evidence, not an equivalent definition of extensive revision.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Mara Varen's 2012 novel *The Resin Door*. Teren, a teenager from Valletta, is visiting his grandparents and other relatives in coastal Croatia.
Too weary to keep my eyes fully open, I leaned against Grandmother Elda's shoulder, though the narrow workshop bench made real sleep unlikely. I drifted instead through the resin scent that came from Uncle Niko's cabinet, mingling with the soft scrape of his tools.
It brought back evenings when I was small and Mother repaired my wooden toys before bed. She moved the brush as lightly as a calligrapher drawing a fine line, murmuring names for varnishes I could not understand. Their meaning was unnecessary. The scent, the small movements, the quiet attention were enough.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe a visit the narrator finds tedious
choices.B: To identify the narrator's preferred kinds of varnish
choices.C: To establish that the narrator's mother practiced calligraphy professionally
choices.D: To connect a present sensory experience with a comforting childhood memory

questions.explanation: D covers the transition from the workshop's resin scent to memories of Mother's repairs. C takes a simile as evidence of a profession. B mistakes unfamiliar technical names for favorites. A interprets tiredness as boredom despite the comforting recollection. The passage links experiences across time rather than evaluating the visit negatively.

questions.passage: According to botanists at the Nerien Field Station, the speed with which wilted stems recover firmness may depend on water movement between two internal tissues. Recovery tends to be faster when that movement is intensified, whereas stems regain firmness more slowly when it is _____
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: acquired.
choices.B: diminished.
choices.C: assessed.
choices.D: determined.

questions.explanation: B supplies the opposite of intensified, matching the contrast between faster and slower recovery. A means obtained, D means established or decided, and C means evaluated. Those actions do not describe the reduction in water movement required by the stated relationship.

questions.passage: The popularity of the Orlis walking club in Pula may seem representative of civic groups generally, but sociologist Elda Navik cautions against _____ that single case: the ready supply of casual social interaction, a major attraction for walkers, plays little part in the appeal of solitary manuscript-restoration circles.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: extrapolating from
choices.B: scrutinizing
choices.C: corroborating
choices.D: convening with

questions.explanation: A means extending conclusions from a limited case to a broader category, exactly the generalization the comparison cautions against. C means confirming with evidence. B means examining closely. D means meeting with. None describes inferring the appeal of civic groups generally from one club.

questions.passage: Musicians seeking inspiration may study a transcription of a celebrated communal song, such as the Vescari harvest refrain. Written notation, however, cannot capture how a performance interacts with its setting, including dancers' movements, surrounding conversations, and the timing of collective responses. A transcription of the refrain therefore _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: misrepresents the song specifically to people who have never heard it performed.
choices.B: exaggerates the song's historical significance.
choices.C: conceals the gradual deterioration of the performers' instruments.
choices.D: cannot convey the full effect of the song as it is performed within its community.

questions.explanation: D follows directly from the medium's inability to represent interactions essential to the performance. C introduces instrument condition. B introduces historical importance. A adds an unsupported claim about a particular audience and a necessary misrepresentation. The passage identifies incomplete representation, not those specific distortions.

questions.passage: The Varen Seed Atlas, an online catalog tracing the cultivation histories of crops such as nerka barley and orlis millet, reflects decades of research by botanist Mara Senn. She was not alone in her _____ conservators Lidia Vesk and Nolan Orlen also supplied records and field observations.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: efforts, however;
choices.B: efforts; however
choices.C: efforts however
choices.D: efforts, however,

questions.explanation: A sets off however as a contrast with the preceding emphasis on Senn and separates the two independent clauses with a semicolon. D creates a comma splice. C provides no appropriate clause boundary. B places however at the beginning of the second clause without the required comma following the transitional adverb.

questions.passage: In 1932, coach Soraya Varen established the Orlis Training Circle, which replaced individual rankings with shared assessments. Sports historians argue that her rejection of competitive individualism is _____ the circle's rotating leadership and collective post-practice discussions; these carefully organized routines exemplify its commitment to cooperation.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: complicated by
choices.B: scrutinized by
choices.C: insensible to
choices.D: manifest in

questions.explanation: D means clearly displayed in, connecting the stated rejection of individualism with practices embodying cooperation. B means closely examined by, but the routines are evidence, not examiners. C means unresponsive to. A suggests added difficulty or inconsistency, contrary to the routines' role as straightforward examples of the commitment.

questions.passage: While other municipal collections, such as the Velsar Records Hall, preserve tens of thousands of complete workshop logs, the Nerien Archive holds between 260 and 340 _____ one of the criteria used to classify a collection as a small specialist repository.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: logs: which satisfy
choices.B: logs. Satisfying
choices.C: logs; satisfying
choices.D: logs, satisfying

questions.explanation: D attaches the participial phrase satisfying to the complete clause it elaborates. A incorrectly separates the relative clause “which satisfy…” from its antecedent with a colon. C incorrectly uses a semicolon before a nonfinite phrase. B creates a sentence fragment beginning Satisfying.

questions.passage: Traditional lint screens trap particles mechanically, but newer coated screens also bind particles chemically. As materials researcher Ilara Savel has shown, the coating adheres to airborne fibers that _____ within its effective range.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: approach
choices.B: is approaching
choices.C: has approached
choices.D: approaching

questions.explanation: A provides a finite plural verb agreeing with fibers, the antecedent of that. D is nonfinite and leaves the relative clause incomplete. C and B use singular auxiliaries despite the plural antecedent. The singular coating governs adheres in the main clause, not the verb inside the relative clause.

questions.passage: It was June of 1969 when instrument maker Elda Varen completed _____ of forty instruments selected for the forthcoming exhibition, remains central to the museum's collection.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Idra. The harp. One
choices.B: Idra. The harp; one
choices.C: *Idra*, the harp, one
choices.D: *Idra*. The harp, one

questions.explanation: D ends the complete first sentence after the instrument's name. It then begins a second sentence whose subject, The harp, is separated from remains by the supplementary phrase “one of forty instruments…”. C joins independent clauses with a comma. A leaves “The harp” as a sentence fragment. B uses a semicolon after the fragment “The harp”; a semicolon must separate independent clauses.

questions.passage: The organizers made clear that the symposium would concentrate on textile conservation. Despite the curator's _____ her expertise in that broad subject, she could discuss Mirela Varen's dyed-silk panels authoritatively, having used them in preservation workshops for many years.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: exceptions to
choices.B: insight into
choices.C: affinity for
choices.D: reservations about

questions.explanation: D expresses doubt about broad expertise, contrasting with confidence concerning a familiar example. C suggests attraction rather than uncertainty. A refers to exclusions or deviations, which cannot naturally describe the curator's attitude toward her expertise here. B indicates understanding and therefore does not supply the reservation required by despite.

questions.passage: Ceramist Ilara Savel has attracted audiences far beyond her home country of Slovenia. In 2016, her vessels appeared at the Nerien Design Hall in _____ the displayed pieces, with their subdued copper glazes, elongated profiles, and precisely repeated ridges, captivated visitors.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Denmark for example
choices.B: Denmark, for example;
choices.C: Denmark; for example
choices.D: Denmark, for example,

questions.explanation: B sets off for example, which marks the Denmark exhibition as an instance of international reach, and uses a semicolon between independent clauses. D creates a comma splice. A omits the clause boundary. C does not separate the introductory transitional phrase from the second clause with the comma it requires.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Island Fieldwork Archive (IFA) encourages young horticulturists by preserving accounts of island botanists' work.
• Idra Taver is a botanist included in IFA's Historical Researchers Directory.
• Taver was born in 1934 and died in 2008.
questions.question: The student wants to introduce a discussion of Taver's career to an audience already familiar with IFA. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Idra Taver was a distinguished researcher, but the directory includes many other distinguished researchers as well.
choices.B: IFA preserves island botanists' work to inspire future horticulturists, including through accounts of researchers such as Idra Taver.
choices.C: According to IFA, Idra Taver was born in 1934 and died in 2008.
choices.D: Among the botanists represented in IFA's directory is Idra Taver.

questions.explanation: D efficiently identifies Taver's profession and place in the familiar archive, preparing a career discussion. B repeats the project's purpose for an audience that already knows it. A makes an unsupported evaluation and shifts attention to others. C supplies life dates without identifying the professional role central to the requested introduction.

questions.passage:
Four sectors in the Varen exhibition economy, 2018
The Orsen, Nerien, and more than twenty other workshop cooperatives jointly operate a range of enterprises. A student studying their combined activity as a single sector wants to compare average output per worker with that of three other sectors. The table shows that cooperative workshops produced 140 credits per worker on average, placing them _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the comparison?

choices.A: below transport services but above display construction and catalog preparation.
choices.B: above all three other sectors.
choices.C: below all three other sectors.
choices.D: above catalog preparation and display construction and approximately equal to transport services.

questions.explanation: A gives the correct ordering: 240 for transport services exceeds the cooperatives' 140, which exceeds 90 for display construction and 65 for catalog preparation. D falsely describes 140 and 240 as approximately equal. C and B place the cooperative sector below or above every other sector, contradicting the ordering. Total output is not the requested per-worker measure.

questions.passage: The Neris Boathouse in Pula is where boat designer Olek Varen lived for eighteen years and prepared many of his later plans. It is now a museum devoted to his life and designs. Visitors come to feel closer to a maker they admire. To encourage that connection, curators recommend nearby coastal walks and harbor tours, allowing visitors to experience the winds and currents that influenced Varen's work.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To summarize Varen's entire biography
choices.B: To explain why Varen's plans remain popular with builders
choices.C: To compare the Neris Boathouse with other museums
choices.D: To describe a museum devoted to Varen and the experience it offers visitors

questions.explanation: D encompasses the building's museum role, its subject, and activities intended to connect visitors with Varen. C invents a comparison. B shifts the focus to the popularity of the plans, which is not explained. A overstates a brief description of one residence and its present use as an account of the designer's whole life.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Elda Orlis's dance *Turning Harbor* (1981) features two apprentices using rounded, flowing arm movements.
• They repeatedly reach toward one another, representing mutual assistance.
• Orlis's dance *Steps for Two* (1989) features two apprentices using sharply angled arm movements.
• They raise a shared workboard with one hand while linking their free arms.
• These gestures represent their support for one another in seeking equal opportunities.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the dances. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The linked arms and raised workboard in *Steps for Two* express support in seeking equality.
choices.B: *Turning Harbor* uses flowing arm movements, whereas *Steps for Two* uses sharply angled ones.
choices.C: Both dances portray apprentices whose gestures symbolize supportive relationships.
choices.D: Orlis completed *Turning Harbor* in 1981 and *Steps for Two* in 1989.

questions.explanation: C names a shared feature supported by both sets of gestures: mutual support. B contrasts movement styles. D contrasts completion years. A accurately interprets only *Steps for Two*. Those statements are supported but do not emphasize a similarity between the dances.

questions.passage: In the 1910s, inventor Mara Senn improved Edren Voss's design for a grain-drying chamber. _____ she placed a cork lining around its heating coil, helping the chamber withstand repeated use. The change made Senn the first Sorven inventor to contribute a component to the region's exported drying systems.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Soon,
choices.C: Regardless,
choices.D: Specifically,

questions.explanation: D introduces the concrete modification that explains the preceding general statement about improvement. C dismisses preceding information. B adds a time relation not established by the text. A signals contrast, although the cork lining exemplifies the improvement rather than contradicting it.

questions.passage: Founded in 1974 as an educational arm of the Coastal Toolmakers Guild, the Open Compass Collective became an influential model for later public-engineering workshops. A historian argues that its early demonstrations drew strongly on the audience-guided physical comedy of traveling puzzle fairs popular around the northern Adriatic in the 1930s and 1940s.
questions.question: Which quotation from the historian's article would best illustrate this claim?

choices.A: “The collective made frequent use of contemporary references, explanations that relied on humor, and equipment that appeared improvised, an approach reflecting both its limited financial resources and its intended message about making technical knowledge accessible.”
choices.B: “Led by founder Mara Vesk, the largely untrained presenters carried a few models into harbor workshops and offered brief, entertaining demonstrations.”
choices.C: “The presenters discovered humor in ordinary mechanical failures, turning amusement into a means of criticizing waste while engaging the public.”
choices.D: “Demonstrators performed short comic trials with oversized levers and wildly swinging models; visitors' delighted shouts or impatient objections repeatedly caused the presenters to improvise new maneuvers.”

questions.explanation: D supplies both defining features of the claimed influence: exaggerated physical comedy and audience reactions shaping improvisation. A describes humor and inexpensive equipment but not audience-guided action. C explains humor's purpose rather than its performance style. B identifies performers, venues, and brevity without the physical exaggeration and responsive interaction central to the claim.

questions.passage: Linguists Elda Varen and Niko Senn's analysis of prosodic variation and its spread over several generations _____ five phonetic features associated with regional stress patterns, including vowel length and syllable timing. The Nerian coastal dialect exhibits one of these features.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: are identifying
choices.B: have identified
choices.C: identify
choices.D: identifies

questions.explanation: D agrees with the singular head noun analysis. The two linguists are possessors of that analysis, and variation and spread occur within modifying phrases; none changes the subject's number. C, A, and B are plural verb forms and therefore do not agree with analysis.

questions.passage:
Transporter models by average percent of top speed in two operating conditions
It may seem that a warehouse transporter should use its top speed both for routine deliveries and for clearing stock during emergencies. The power cost of operating at full capacity, however, can make that strategy unattractive even during emergency clearance, as suggested by the fact that _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the text?

choices.A: at least six models average less than their top speed during routine delivery.
choices.B: the greatest number of models falls in the 85–100% range during emergency clearance.
choices.C: several models average less than 85% of their top speed during emergency clearance.
choices.D: most models use approximately the same percentage of their top speed in the two conditions.

questions.explanation: C directly shows substantial use of less than full capacity in the emergency condition: fifteen models appear in bins below 85%. B identifies the largest individual emergency bin but does not establish that models avoid full capacity, since that bin includes 100%. D is not established by these aggregate distributions. A concerns routine delivery, so it does not demonstrate the claim about emergency clearance.

graph.caption: Transporter speeds in two operating conditions

questions.passage: In the late 1980s, music teacher Edren Voss began holding rehearsals in what was then an unusual classroom: decommissioned harbor ferries. _____ his daughter Lidia has chosen a surprising venue for her new project, Transit Lessons. She conducts short seminars aboard working trams, using the changing streets outside the windows as examples for discussion.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Secondly,
choices.B: Likewise,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: Indeed,

questions.explanation: B emphasizes the parallel: both teachers choose unconventional places for instruction. D would primarily reinforce or clarify the earlier statement rather than relate the two cases. A suggests an ordered list not established here. C signals opposition even though the daughter's practice resembles her father's.

questions.passage:
Text 1
In 2014, Rovena received the Regional Design Council's Open Workshop distinction for its exceptional network of public craft studios. Residents and visiting designers alike recognize the honor. By selecting Rovena, the council has already raised awareness of local methods, materials, and makers and substantially increased workshop visits.
Text 2
Many Rovena studio owners anticipated more visits after the 2014 distinction. Researcher Mara Senn and colleagues nevertheless emphasize that honored workshop networks must develop deliberate outreach to gain the full benefit. Without efforts to publicize Rovena's studios, many potential visitors would remain unaware of their unusual resources.
questions.question: Which choice best describes a difference in the authors' views of the distinction's benefits?

choices.A: Text 1 expects makers to benefit most, whereas Text 2 expects transport operators to benefit most.
choices.B: Text 1 regards the benefits as automatic consequences of selection, whereas Text 2 considers additional effort necessary to realize them fully.
choices.C: Text 1 treats the benefits as less lasting than Text 2 does.
choices.D: Text 1 says the distinction helped Rovena, whereas Text 2 denies that it produced any benefit.

questions.explanation: B captures selection alone in Text 1 versus deliberate outreach in Text 2. D exaggerates a qualification into denial of all benefit. A invents a ranking of beneficiaries. C invents a comparison of duration. The disagreement concerns how benefits are achieved, not whether benefits exist, who gains most, or how long they last.

questions.passage: A ceremonial weave need not have a single meaning: the intricate knot patterns of Soraya Varen can _____ as many interpretations as there are people examining them. Unless a reading is deliberately implausible or inattentive to the work, it is therefore difficult to insist that the viewer has misunderstood it.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: partition
choices.B: refute
choices.C: counteract
choices.D: yield

questions.explanation: D means produce or give rise to, fitting patterns that support many interpretations. A means divide into parts. C means oppose an effect. B means disprove. Those meanings do not describe the generation of multiple readings that the passage discusses.

questions.passage: Pressed from roasted millet and shaped using a method inherited from the chef's Istrian grandfather, _____ delicately crisp and richly layered, inviting diners to break them apart by hand.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Mara Savel is a Portuguese chef whose folded grain cakes are
choices.B: the folded grain cakes of Portuguese chef Mara Savel are
choices.C: the Portuguese chef Mara Savel prepares folded grain cakes that are
choices.D: when she prepares folded grain cakes, Portuguese chef Mara Savel makes them

questions.explanation: B places the grain cakes, the things pressed and shaped, immediately after the introductory modifier. C and A instead make the chef the grammatical subject described as pressed from millet. D likewise places the chef rather than the cakes as the main-clause subject, leaving the modifier improperly attached.

questions.passage: Textile historians examined 110 early workshop panels, dated to roughly two centuries ago, and concluded that makers repeatedly repositioned small patches to create nearly circular arrangements. The finding that their efforts to achieve that geometry were _____ suggests that the workshops practiced more sophisticated spatial planning than historians had assumed.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: sympathetic
choices.B: comparable
choices.C: deliberate
choices.D: troubling

questions.explanation: C means intentional, connecting purposeful geometric construction with a capacity for planning. A concerns compassion, B concerns similarity to something else, and D concerns worry. None explains why the makers' arrangement would indicate deliberate spatial reasoning.

questions.passage: During the 2000s, the price of transferable licenses for unused radio channels rose sharply, unexpectedly _____ demand: buyers who had previously shown little interest entered the market, expecting further price increases to allow profitable resale.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: exploiting
choices.B: appraising
choices.C: generating
choices.D: monetizing

questions.explanation: C means producing or bringing about, matching the arrival of buyers who previously lacked interest. B means assessing value. A means taking advantage of something already present. D means converting something into revenue. None expresses the creation of additional demand described after the colon.

questions.passage:
Four historic signal structures
A student comparing four historic structures wants to record both their ages and heights. The table indicates that the Varen Lighthouse was built about 170 years ago and is _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?

choices.A: 61 meters tall.
choices.B: 48 meters tall.
choices.C: 9 meters tall.
choices.D: 76 meters tall.

questions.explanation: D matches the height in the Varen Lighthouse row, 76 meters. B gives the Orsen Clock Tower's height, C gives the Selva Signal House's, and A gives the Neris Observatory's. The age identifies the relevant structure; it must be paired with the height from that same row.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Varen Design Department is part of Nerien University.
• University departments provide various services to their students.
• One such service is equipment lending.
• The department enrolled 2,740 students in 2017.
• Nerien University has forty-two departments.
questions.question: The student wants to give an example of a student service the Varen department provides. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: As a university department, Varen provides equipment-lending services to its students.
choices.B: In 2017, 2,740 students were enrolled in the Varen department.
choices.C: Nerien University has forty-two departments serving student communities.
choices.D: The Varen department, a unit of Nerien University, provides services to its students.

questions.explanation: A names a specific service and connects it to the requested department. D states a general responsibility without an example. C gives the institution's number of departments. B gives enrollment. Neither numerical detail identifies a service.

questions.passage: Instrument designer Lucia Ferens is known for precision devices used in fields ranging from textile conservation to coastal navigation. Widespread admiration for those devices has brought Ferens considerable _____ as a designer.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: tolerance
choices.B: sympathy
choices.C: prestige
choices.D: assistance

questions.explanation: C means high standing or respect, fitting a reputation built on admired work. B means compassionate concern. D means help. A means acceptance or endurance despite reservations. The passage describes professional esteem, not distress, aid, or reluctant acceptance.

questions.passage: Anouk Meijer, who cataloged 18,400 coastal plant specimens across three continents, unquestionably achieved a great deal. Her place in historical memory may nevertheless be more _____ than that of a celebrated pioneer such as Dimitri Kovas, the first researcher to demonstrate a reproducible method for preserving salt-marsh seeds, a distinction for which he will always be remembered.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: uncertain
choices.B: enduring
choices.C: conspicuous
choices.D: deserving

questions.explanation: A contrasts an insecure place in memory with a milestone explicitly said to ensure remembrance. B means lasting and reverses that contrast. C means noticeable. D concerns merit rather than whether remembrance will persist. The text acknowledges Meijer's achievement while questioning its durability in collective memory.

questions.passage: After a book design is approved, production begins with a typesetter preparing a detailed page plan. The pages are then printed, and each sheet is checked against that plan. _____ the sheets are assembled, bound, and inspected before distribution.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Earlier,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: On the contrary,
choices.D: Finally,

questions.explanation: D introduces the last stage in the sequence from planning through printing to assembly and inspection. A reverses the chronology. C signals disagreement despite a continuous process. B presents an example rather than the next and final stage.

questions.passage: A packaging studio places rigid braces around fragile exhibition objects to protect them during transport. In some cases, however, the braces the studio employs for protection actually _____ the packaging's appeal to furniture makers, who reuse those supports in small shelving units.
