questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: is increasing
choices.B: has increased
choices.C: increase
choices.D: increases

questions.explanation: C agrees with the plural subject braces. The intervening clause “the studio employs for protection” modifies braces; its singular studio does not govern the blank. D, B, and A are singular verb forms and therefore disagree with the actual subject.

questions.passage: Numerous studies have found a positive relationship between the circulation of printed route schedules and service punctuality in eastern Adriatic towns. Saskia Burin's team found no such relationship in Portugal, prompting a suggestion that it was specific to the Adriatic. Yet several studies elsewhere, including one led by Edren Kovas in Denmark, reproduced the Adriatic pattern, while few resembled Burin's result. This evidence suggests that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: unusual conditions prevented Kovas's team from measuring punctuality accurately.
choices.B: the relationship is confined to eastern Adriatic towns.
choices.C: schedule circulation and punctuality generally tend to increase or decrease together.
choices.D: both schedule circulation and punctuality are higher in Portugal than anywhere else.

questions.explanation: C accounts for the repeated positive association across regions and the rarity of the contrary result. D compares absolute levels, which the text does not report. A invents a measurement problem in a study that supported the recurring pattern. B disregards the corroborating studies outside the Adriatic.

questions.passage: A craft cooperative might devise an entirely original emblem. _____ it could adapt a familiar mark used by an admired workshop. The Rovena Weavers took the latter approach, borrowing the split-leaf motif of the older Ferens Guild.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Alternatively,
choices.D: Consequently,

questions.explanation: C introduces a different naming or design strategy: adapting an existing mark instead of inventing a wholly original one. D implies a consequence. A suggests an equivalent restatement. B suggests an example of originality, whereas the second strategy expressly borrows an established motif.

questions.passage: Digital collections of historical recipes allow researchers to test claims about how _____ a particular ingredient was in regional cooking. One might guess that caraway appeared frequently, for instance, but only a systematic count can establish that it was the seventh most commonly listed spice.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: profound
choices.B: prevalent
choices.C: credible
choices.D: assertive

questions.explanation: B means widespread or common, matching the measured frequency of an ingredient's appearance. A means intellectually deep, C means believable, and D means forcefully confident. The proposed count establishes prevalence rather than any of those qualities.

questions.passage: Compiled, annotated, and arranged from discarded factory ledgers, the interactive maps of Zagreb-based historian Lucia Ferens encourage viewers to reconsider their relationship to urban _____ her maps in the 2012 exhibition *Routes Recovered* were no exception.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: memory and to
choices.B: memory,
choices.C: memory;
choices.D: memory

questions.explanation: C separates two independent clauses: the maps encourage reconsideration, and the exhibited maps were no exception. D runs the clauses together. B joins them with a comma alone. A adds to without creating a grammatical parallel construction or a valid boundary before the second clause.

questions.passage: Working with the Rovena Museum Network, researcher Anouk Meijer analyzed visitor arrivals at venues of different capacities. Smaller galleries had their highest arrivals around 10 a.m. _____ larger galleries reached their peak around 2 p.m.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In summary,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: On the other hand,
choices.D: For instance,

questions.explanation: C contrasts the peak times for two venue groups. D would present the second group as an example of the first finding. A would summarize earlier information. B would restate the first finding rather than report a different result.

questions.passage: Mara Varen's 2002 novel *The Canal Years*, an account of the lives of the Ferens _____ can introduce readers to representations of prolonged drought in Adriatic literature.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: cousins
choices.B: cousins and
choices.C: cousins, and
choices.D: cousins,

questions.explanation: D closes the supplementary phrase beginning “an account” and reconnects the subject novel with its predicate can introduce. A leaves the opening comma unmatched. B and C add and even though the sentence has no second coordinated predicate or clause requiring it.

questions.passage: The 2015 ceramic series *Tidal Chambers* established Lucia Ferens, who grew up in Malta, as a prominent experimental designer. Its representations of Maltese harbor life also expanded the visibility of island communities within experimental ceramics. Ferens is not the only island-born maker working in that field: Anouk Meijer, born in the Azores, produced the acclaimed 2010 series *Island Frames*, whose forms evoke an Azorean fishing settlement.
questions.question: According to the text, how are Ferens and Meijer similar?

choices.A: Both were born in Malta.
choices.B: Both have produced series centered on Maltese communities.
choices.C: Both are island-born makers who create experimental ceramics.
choices.D: Both reject experimental ceramics despite working in that field.

questions.explanation: C states the two shared attributes explicitly established by the passage. D invents rejection of their field. A assigns Meijer Ferens's birthplace. B transfers the Maltese subject of Ferens's series to Meijer's Azorean work. Their specific origins and represented communities differ.

questions.passage: In retrospect, the bracing principles circulating among Dutch structural engineers in the 1910s made the Varen diagonal-support method an unsurprising next development. It may not have been coincidence, _____ that Lucia Ferens and Dimitri Kovas devised it independently. Their case, after all, joins many substantial advances produced by researchers working in parallel rather than by a solitary innovator.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: for example,
choices.B: then,
choices.C: however,
choices.D: moreover,

questions.explanation: B presents independent convergence as a consequence reasonably inferred from an intellectual climate favoring the method. C signals opposition to that climate. A introduces an example without expressing the inference. D adds another point rather than connecting the shared circumstances to the conclusion about coincidence.

questions.passage: To make the results of regional fencing tournaments comparable, organizers need rules that remain constant across venues. _____ a committee developed the Varen Match Code, which fixes the dimensions of the competition area and specifies how points are awarded. A bout conducted under the code can therefore be evaluated using the same criteria wherever it takes place.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For this reason,
choices.B: Regardless,
choices.C: In contrast,
choices.D: In addition,

questions.explanation: A presents the development of the code as a response to the need for consistent rules. C would signal opposition, although the code fulfills the stated need. D treats the code as merely another fact and misses the causal relationship. B suggests that the committee acted irrespective of the need, a relationship the passage does not establish.

questions.passage: The Merrow Guild’s archive has become the first regional collection known to contain more than ninety medieval route maps. Using a scanner that detects faint marks beneath later annotations, a research team identified forty-seven previously unrecognized maps among the guild’s papers. The discovery puts the Merrow collection ahead of the Darsen Guild’s archive in the number of cataloged route maps.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the routes depicted on maps in two medieval collections
choices.B: To report a discovery that changes the known size and relative standing of an archival collection
choices.C: To explain the physical principles that allow an imaging device to detect hidden markings
choices.D: To trace the development of the Darsen Guild’s recordkeeping practices

questions.explanation: B captures both the discovery of additional maps and its consequence: Merrow now has the largest known regional collection of this kind. C overemphasizes the scanner, whose operation is mentioned only briefly. D concerns a history the text does not provide. A would require information about the maps’ routes, whereas the passage focuses on the number of maps.

questions.passage: Long credited to Tomas Vey, a celebrated maker of astronomical instruments, the 1786 device *The Mariner’s Orrery* attracted renewed interest in the 2000s when historians found that its intricate gearwork—designed to display the changing positions of several celestial bodies—was actually the work of the little-known coastal instrument _____ Leona Sarret (1761–1833).
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: maker:
choices.B: maker—
choices.C: maker
choices.D: maker,

questions.explanation: C leaves the identifying name directly attached to “instrument maker,” completing the noun phrase without an unnecessary break. B introduces an unmatched dash between the occupation and name. D incorrectly separates the restrictive identification from the occupation. A inserts a colon inside a noun phrase before the name needed to complete it.

questions.passage: In 2022, the freight terminal’s loading rate was 58% of its maximum rated rate, below the 76% level at which an Orsen curve predicts peak daily output. Some engineers argue that the effect of adding another loading crew depends on the terminal’s position on the Orsen _____ theoretical relationship between loading intensity and completed shipments, the curve was first drawn in a workshop notebook by engineer Mira Orsen in 1981.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: curve. A
choices.B: curve: which is a
choices.C: curve, which is a
choices.D: curve, a

questions.explanation: A ends the complete sentence about the terminal’s position. The next sentence begins with “D theoretical relationship between loading intensity and completed shipments,” an introductory description of “the curve.” D joins two independent clauses with only a comma. B puts a colon before material that would still contain an improperly joined independent clause. C adds a relative clause but leaves the later independent clause, “the curve was first drawn,” joined without a proper sentence boundary.

questions.passage: Across four decades of influential designs, including the luminous woven panels in *Windows at Dusk*, textile artist Ines Ravel developed a reputation for exceptional craftsmanship and sustained invention. _____ in 1996, her contribution to the field earned her its highest professional distinction: election to the National Guild of Textile Arts.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: Accordingly,
choices.C: Besides,
choices.D: However,

questions.explanation: B connects Ravel’s exceptional record to the recognition that followed from it. D would imply that the honor conflicts with her accomplishments. A would present the election as a restatement of the entire preceding sentence, although it is a consequence. C suggests an additional, loosely related point rather than the clearly supported result.

questions.passage: Included in *Forms in Motion* (2019) is a small glazed vessel made in 1947 by Sera _____ “Folded Horizon,” the piece advances the exhibition’s aim of showing how studio potters used unconventional shapes and surfaces during the middle decades of the twentieth century.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Denholm and titled
choices.B: Denholm titled
choices.C: Denholm, titled
choices.D: Denholm. Titled

questions.explanation: D completes the inverted sentence identifying the vessel and its maker, then begins a new sentence with the modifier “Titled ‘Folded Horizon,’” which describes “the piece.” C produces a comma splice between two complete clauses. A cannot properly coordinate the maker’s name with “titled” and still leaves the next clause without a boundary. B provides no punctuation separating the first complete clause from the second.

questions.passage: Although desert paddleplants and coastal shieldplants belong to distant branches of their botanical family, paddleplants show striking _____ shieldplants: both have thick leaf surfaces, low growth habits, and shallow root systems. The two groups developed these features independently as adaptations to similarly exposed habitats.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: objections to
choices.B: warnings about
choices.C: similarities with
choices.D: examples of

questions.explanation: C identifies the shared features that the following list supplies. A would suggest criticism rather than resemblance. D would incorrectly classify paddleplants as instances of shieldplants despite their distant relationship. B implies a caution about shieldplants that the passage does not express.

questions.passage: The city of Arvend has unusually high attendance at its public lectures, but copying one visible feature of its program—such as offering events in several neighborhood venues—may do little to increase attendance elsewhere. Researcher Nira Solen argues that existing accounts of participation remain incomplete: some emphasize ticket prices, others residents’ educational backgrounds, and still others the availability of evening transport. People decide whether to attend within settings where several circumstances and needs operate together.
questions.question: Based on the text, Solen would most likely agree with which statement about research on lecture attendance?

choices.A: Identifying the features shared by popular lecture programs would establish a dependable formula for increasing attendance.
choices.B: Researchers are unlikely to identify one factor that reliably predicts attendance across different settings.
choices.C: Most studies are misleading because they overlook the single condition that determines whether people attend.
choices.D: Studies have exaggerated differences in people’s reasons for attending lectures.

questions.explanation: B follows from Solen’s view that decisions emerge from combinations of circumstances and needs, making a universally reliable single predictor unlikely. A assumes that copying shared visible features is sufficient, an assumption the passage questions. D attributes an assessment of individual differences to Solen that the text never makes. C replaces her account of interacting factors with the claim that one overlooked factor determines attendance.

questions.passage: Architectural historian Lena Ovik serves on the committee that adds structures to the Meriden Heritage Register, which already includes the Eastgate Pump House, completed in 1816, and the Harbor Reading Room, opened in 1938. Ovik does not decide which buildings receive designation on her own, _____ nominations require approval from seven other specialists.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: however, all
choices.B: however; all
choices.C: however all
choices.D: however. and all

questions.explanation: B uses “however” to qualify the preceding statement and a semicolon to separate two independent clauses. The comma before “however” is already supplied in the passage. C leaves the two clauses without a valid boundary. A creates a comma splice. D ends a sentence but then begins the next one with the uncapitalized word “and,” failing the conventions of written sentence boundaries.

questions.passage:
Contributions of Three Industries to the Selvar Regional Economy in 2021
The Veyran Fishers’ Cooperative, the East Shoal Association, and more than twenty other maritime cooperatives operate processing plants, shipping services, and retail businesses across Selvar. If their economic activity is counted as one industry, its contribution to the regional economy in 2021 _____
questions.question: Which choice uses data from the table to most effectively complete the comparison?

choices.A: was greater than the contribution of either building services or food processing.
choices.B: exceeded the contribution of food processing but equaled that of building services.
choices.C: was smaller than the contribution of both building services and food processing.
choices.D: surpassed the contribution of building services but was less than that of food processing.

questions.explanation: D correctly places the cooperatives’ $5,846,200,000 contribution between building services’ $5,392,700,000 and food processing’s $11,624,900,000. B reverses the comparison with food processing and incorrectly claims equality with building services. C incorrectly puts the cooperatives below building services. A incorrectly puts them above food processing.

questions.passage: “The North Window” is a 1907 short story by Mara Ellsen. In the story, the narrator expresses mixed feelings about the room she occupies:
questions.question: Which quotation from “The North Window” most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “When the lamps were extinguished, the glass seemed almost black, and the garden beyond it vanished.”
choices.B: “I have begun to love this quiet room, though the ceiling’s heavy pattern still makes me wish to leave it.”
choices.C: “The shelves had been built too high; their upper edges caught dust that I could neither reach nor ignore.”
choices.D: “A pale stripe crossed the floor at noon, then retreated so slowly that I scarcely noticed its departure.”

questions.explanation: B combines affection for the room with discomfort about its ceiling, explicitly showing opposing feelings about the same surroundings. A describes a visual change without stating an attitude. C expresses dissatisfaction but supplies no positive feeling. D describes the movement of sunlight without establishing either pleasure or dislike.

questions.passage: The Regional Craft Laureateship recognizes practitioners of traditional arts for their _____. Basket weaver Ansel Varo received the distinction after developing widely admired techniques and training a generation of skilled apprentices.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: conjectures
choices.B: misgivings
choices.C: forecasts
choices.D: accomplishments

questions.explanation: D refers to successful work and contributions, precisely the basis for Varo’s recognition. A means proposed explanations or guesses, which the passage does not discuss. B refers to doubts, rather than achievements worthy of an honor. C means predictions, whereas the stated accomplishments have already occurred.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Elian Voss’s 1911 play *The Orchard House*. A mother is discussing the family business with her adult daughter.
MRS. VALE: You cannot remain a spectator forever, Liora. I have carried the accounts and settled every dispute for years. Now you must advise me; you must assume a share of the responsibility.
LIORA: I must?
MRS. VALE: Certainly. You turned twenty-seven last autumn.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does the word “assume” most nearly mean?

choices.A: Undertake
choices.B: Presuppose
choices.C: Deduce
choices.D: Imitate

questions.explanation: A means to take on a duty, which is what Mrs. Vale asks Liora to do. D would mean to copy someone’s behavior rather than accept responsibility. C would involve drawing a conclusion from evidence. B would mean taking something as given before considering it; neither C nor B fits a direct request to perform the work.

questions.passage: In the Veyric language, spoken along a northern coast, “nalo” means “a bell’s ring,” while “na-nalo” means “a succession of rings.” Repeating part or all of a word’s base within a related word is a process called reduplication. <u>In this example, the segment “na” is repeated at the beginning of “na-nalo.”</u> Other Veyric words display the same pattern.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It establishes that reduplication occurs in most Veyric words.
choices.B: It identifies an exception to the definition of reduplication.
choices.C: It demonstrates how the general process just defined operates in the particular words already introduced.
choices.D: It translates the two Veyric words into English for the first time.

questions.explanation: C describes the sentence’s move from the general definition to the precise repeated segment in the earlier example. D is incorrect because the translations appear in the first sentence. B is incorrect because the example conforms to the definition. A overstates the sentence, which analyzes one pair of words rather than measuring the process’s frequency.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Aven Cultural Council compiled a list of eighty locally significant scents.
• Entries were chosen for their importance to regional traditions.
• The scent of cedar shavings in the Rell boatyards is on the list.
• The scent of toasted fennel at the Brann autumn market is on the list.
questions.question: The student wants to indicate that both scents appear on the council’s list. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Both cedar shavings in the Rell boatyards and toasted fennel at the Brann autumn market appear on the council’s list.
choices.B: Toasted fennel at the Brann autumn market is among the scents recognized by the council.
choices.C: The Aven Cultural Council selected eighty scents for their importance to regional traditions.
choices.D: The scent of cedar shavings in the Rell boatyards was selected because of its cultural significance.

questions.explanation: A explicitly identifies both scents and states their shared inclusion. C describes the list without naming either scent. B establishes the inclusion of only the market scent. D provides a reason for including only the boatyard scent.

questions.passage: Several designers in the patchwork cinema movement deliberately expose joins in their films’ scenery. Director Ana Vey, for example, allows painted panels to end visibly at the edge of a set, while the duo North Seam keeps the supports behind its miniature buildings in view. These choices do more than create an unusual appearance: by revealing the construction of seemingly convincing settings, the filmmakers prompt viewers to consider how images shape their understanding of everyday reality.
questions.question: Based on the text, the author would most likely disagree with which statement about the exposed joins in patchwork cinema?

choices.A: They invite reflection on the role of constructed images in people’s experience of reality.
choices.B: They are primarily decorative features with little relevance to broader social experience.
choices.C: They demonstrate the extent to which the movement determines its audience’s personal identity.
choices.D: They show how the movement has successfully eliminated misleading images from viewers’ lives.

questions.explanation: B directly conflicts with the author’s explicit claim that the choices do more than affect appearance and encourage reflection about everyday reality. D goes beyond the text by claiming the movement eliminates misleading images; the author does not address that outcome. C likewise introduces an effect on personal identity that the passage does not discuss. A agrees with the stated purpose of making constructed settings visibly artificial.

questions.passage:
Text 1
In separate studies, Priya Dalen’s team and Emre Vos’s team tested whether vibrations pass between instrument cases through a shared wooden rack. Dalen’s team kept the cases from touching by placing narrow gaps between them, while leaving each case on the rack. This eliminated all routes except the rack—a precaution Vos’s team did not take.
Text 2
Separating the cases was a necessary precaution because it prevented direct case-to-case transmission. But the gaps did not stop sound from traveling through the surrounding air. Dalen’s design therefore cannot establish that any vibration measured in a neighboring case arrived through the rack rather than through another route.
questions.question: Based on the texts, the two authors would most likely give the same answer to which question?

choices.A: Is there a material that blocks airborne sound while allowing rack-borne vibration to pass?
choices.B: Did Dalen’s gaps ensure that vibrations could reach neighboring cases only through the rack?
choices.C: Did Vos’s study successfully rule out every transmission route other than the rack?
choices.D: Do cases that transmit vibrations by direct contact always transmit them through a rack as well?

questions.explanation: C identifies an inadequacy both accounts support. Text 1 says Vos did not separate the cases, leaving direct contact as a possible route; Text 2 establishes why separation is necessary. B is the central disagreement: Text 1 considers Dalen’s precaution sufficient, while Text 2 identifies airborne transmission as an uncontrolled route. Neither author addresses the material proposed in A or the universal relationship asserted in D.

questions.passage: “Harbor at Evening” is an 1812 poem by Dorian Astell. The speaker describes contradictory feelings while observing a lively waterfront:
questions.question: Which quotation from “Harbor at Evening” most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “The western clouds grew faint and thin; / The last red sunlight left the bay; / The fishers drew their vessels in / And put their silver catch away.”
choices.B: “Each lantern trembled on the tide; / I counted lights from shore to shore; / The anchored boats swung side by side / As they had swung the night before.”
choices.C: “The ropes lay coiled beside the stair; / The gulls above the rigging wheeled; / A sailor breathed the salted air / And watched the copper waves revealed.”
choices.D: “The children’s laughter filled the quay; / Its brightness warmed my listening heart; / Yet every happy cry to me / Recalled the grief of years apart.”

questions.explanation: D connects warmth and happiness with grief, showing that the same cheerful sounds produce opposing feelings. C presents harbor activity without contradictory emotions. B describes repeated observations without an emotional conflict. A describes the end of the day and the fishers’ work, not the speaker’s mixed response.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A plucked string sends vibrations away from the point where it is displaced.
• Two modes of vibration in the demonstration are called the narrow mode and the broad mode.
• Both modes propagate along the string.
• The narrow mode travels faster than the broad mode.
• In the narrow mode, the string moves parallel to the demonstration board.
• In the broad mode, the string moves toward and away from the board.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two modes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The narrow mode propagates along the string at a higher speed than the broad mode.
choices.B: Although both modes arise in the demonstration, they move the string in different directions.
choices.C: Both the narrow mode and the broad mode travel along the string and cause it to move.
choices.D: The narrow mode moves the string parallel to the board as it travels away from the displacement point.

questions.explanation: C emphasizes the two shared properties supplied by the notes: propagation along the string and movement of the string. A emphasizes unequal speeds. B foregrounds different directions despite acknowledging a shared setting. D describes only the narrow mode and makes no comparison.

questions.passage: The editors of *A Lexicon of Working Harbors* asked the _____ to prepare the entry on “sheer strake,” a term for the uppermost course of planking along a wooden vessel’s side.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: boatbuilder, Renna Holt
choices.B: boatbuilder Renna Holt,
choices.C: boatbuilder, Renna Holt,
choices.D: boatbuilder Renna Holt

questions.explanation: D integrates the identifying name with “boatbuilder” and leaves the infinitive “to prepare” directly connected to “asked.” C treats the essential name as a parenthetical insertion. B wrongly places a comma between the object of “asked” and its infinitive complement. A introduces an unnecessary comma before the identifying name.

questions.passage:
Dated Ages of Mineral Deposits from Selected Expeditions
During the 1960s and 1970s, the Ridge Survey expeditions recovered mineral deposits from several cave sites. Decades later, the Deep Valley Survey returned samples from another site. Researchers dated the material from each expedition and concluded that the Deep Valley samples were distinctive because _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the claim?

choices.A: they were closer in age to the Ridge Survey III samples than to the samples from either of the other Ridge Survey expeditions.
choices.B: they established that researchers had correctly predicted the ages of all the Ridge Survey samples.
choices.C: they came from the same sampling site as the Ridge Survey I samples.
choices.D: they were substantially younger than the samples from every Ridge Survey expedition listed.

questions.explanation: D accurately compares 4.8 thousand years with 8.4, 7.6, and 9.1 thousand years; the Deep Valley deposits are younger than all three. C contradicts the listed sites. B introduces predictions that the table does not report. A is incorrect because 9.1 is the farthest, rather than the closest, of the three Ridge Survey ages to 4.8.

questions.passage: _____ though it appeared to many puzzle designers, the Halden packing problem, first circulated in 1983, eventually yielded to Cora Venn, who published a complete solution in 2016.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: Unambiguous
choices.B: Insurmountable
choices.C: Inevitable
choices.D: Unimpeachable

questions.explanation: B means apparently impossible to overcome or solve, setting up the contrast with the eventual solution. A means clear in meaning, which does not explain why solving it was an achievement. D means beyond criticism or doubt and does not describe difficulty. C means certain to occur, which does not fit a problem that appeared resistant to solution.

questions.passage: Chemist Lera Noss and her colleagues analyzed residues preserved in antique dye vats to reconstruct the recipes used by an early clothmaking workshop. Such residues can reveal details absent from written records, but researchers rarely use them on a large scale. Many compounds in the deposits have broken down over time, and current separation and identification techniques cannot reliably reverse or compensate for much of that deterioration.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It evaluates the results of a study, then predicts whether other researchers will reproduce them.
choices.B: It introduces a standard analytical method, then explains how researchers adapted it to overcome an unusual problem.
choices.C: It describes a particular application of a research approach, then explains an obstacle to wider use of that approach.
choices.D: It compares two research methods, then recommends the one that is more widely accepted.

questions.explanation: C matches the progression from Noss’s use of vat residues to the deterioration that limits broader use. B incorrectly treats the approach as standard and the deterioration as overcome. A claims that results and replication prospects are discussed, whereas the passage provides neither. D invents a comparison and recommendation absent from the text.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Tessa Arden’s 1948 novel *The Street of Small Windows*. A young girl named Mila frequently visits a neighborhood music room.
Mila believed every tune worth knowing must be stored in the room’s cabinets, and she had decided to learn them all. She practiced one score each afternoon, proceeding through the catalog without omitting the difficult pieces. The first composer’s name had begun with D. Months had passed, and she was still among the E’s. She had encountered wedding marches, evening songs, and elaborate exercises whose purpose escaped her. Some afternoons the notes seemed determined to defeat her. Still, the following day she returned.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain why Mila finds one musical genre more appealing than another
choices.B: To show Mila’s persistence in pursuing an ambitious objective
choices.C: To describe a particular composition that Mila considers exceptional
choices.D: To explain why Mila chooses music over every other activity

questions.explanation: B captures Mila’s continued systematic practice despite slow progress and difficulty. A misrepresents the catalog’s varied contents as a stated preference. C focuses on a single composition, although none is singled out for admiration. D requires a comparison with other activities that the passage does not make.

questions.passage: Critics have praised Rena Tal’s 1952 chamber work “Evening at the Wharf” for its sensitive evocation of the harbor district where she grew up. The composition should not be understood as merely a reflection of Tal’s _____ the range of her influences, which extends from medieval dance tunes to the orchestral experiments of Soren Vey and Mila Dorn.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: neighborhood, though: considering
choices.B: neighborhood; though, considering
choices.C: neighborhood, though, considering
choices.D: neighborhood, though. Considering

questions.explanation: C places the interrupting “though” between commas and connects the supplementary phrase beginning “considering” to the complete clause. B places a semicolon before a fragment rather than a second independent clause. A uses a colon to introduce a dependent construction that does not serve as an independent explanation. D leaves the phrase beginning “Considering” as a sentence fragment.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Festivals sometimes relocate to accommodate changing attendance.
• The Bellmere Lantern Festival moved to Alder Square in 1926.
• The festival left Alder Square for River Park in 1979.
• River Park remains the festival’s venue.
questions.question: The student wants to specify how long Alder Square served as the festival’s venue. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: River Park became the Bellmere Lantern Festival’s venue in 1979 and remains its venue.
choices.B: Like other festivals, the Bellmere Lantern Festival changed locations over time.
choices.C: Alder Square hosted the Bellmere Lantern Festival from 1926 to 1979.
choices.D: The festival formerly occupied a square that became its venue in 1926.

questions.explanation: C supplies both the beginning and ending years of the square’s tenure. A focuses on the later venue and omits the beginning of the square’s use. D gives only the starting year. B makes a general observation without specifying the requested interval.

questions.passage: The town of Renlow has unusually high participation in volunteer repair workshops, but copying a visible feature of its program may not produce the same result elsewhere. Organizer Alia Senn argues that existing accounts of participation are incomplete: some studies emphasize “convenient opening hours,” others “the attractiveness of the workshop space,” but decisions about attending arise from combinations of practical needs and local circumstances.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the references to “convenient opening hours” and “the attractiveness of the workshop space” in the text as a whole?

choices.A: They identify features the passage argues matter exclusively to participants in Renlow.
choices.B: They illustrate factors that studies regard as important but that the passage says participants almost never consider.
choices.C: They identify influences that studies have highlighted while showing that those influences form only part of a more complex decision.
choices.D: They describe considerations that researchers have dismissed but that Senn regards as decisive everywhere.

questions.explanation: C reflects the text’s acknowledgment of these factors alongside its insistence that participation depends on interacting conditions. A wrongly limits their relevance to Renlow. D reverses the studies’ treatment of the factors and introduces a claim of universal decisiveness. B mistakes the argument that the factors are insufficient for a claim that they are rarely considered.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Fixed-view documentaries present ordinary events in uninterrupted recordings from one camera position.
• *One Tide* is a coastal fixed-view documentary.
• Its nine-hour recording shows water advancing and retreating beneath the pilings of Nerra Pier.
• It first aired in 2014.
• Film scholar Ada Renn discusses the genre in *Watching Ordinary Time*.
• Renn describes its appeal as “attention without spectacle.”
questions.question: The student wants to provide a specific example of a fixed-view documentary. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Ada Renn examines fixed-view documentaries in *Watching Ordinary Time*.
choices.B: First aired in 2014, *One Tide* is a fixed-view documentary recording nine hours of tidal movement beneath Nerra Pier.
choices.C: According to Renn, uninterrupted observation can offer “attention without spectacle.”
choices.D: Fixed-view documentaries present ordinary events without interruption or changes in camera position.

questions.explanation: B names a particular program and gives details that demonstrate its membership in the genre. A identifies a scholar and book, not an example of the documentary form. D supplies only a general definition. C presents an interpretation of the genre without identifying a specific documentary.

questions.passage: Discarded seed packets, household repair cards, and tickets from vanished neighborhood theaters may seem unpromising materials for historical study. Yet these short-lived objects can _____ changes in everyday expectations and priorities that official chronicles leave unrecorded.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: vindicate
choices.B: prevent
choices.C: register
choices.D: initiate

questions.explanation: C means record or reflect, matching the claim that the objects provide evidence of cultural change. A would mean justify or clear from blame, which is not their described function. B would make the objects stop changes. D would make them cause changes, whereas the passage treats them as evidence of changes.

questions.passage: To examine how warmth affects microbial breakdown of plant fibers, researcher Veda Orr moved samples from a cool storage chamber to one that was 3°C warmer. Breakdown accelerated in the transferred samples. Importantly, the relative abundance of the microbial species in those samples remained the same, allowing Orr to attribute the faster breakdown to increased activity within the existing community.
questions.question: It can most reasonably be inferred that the finding about community composition was important because it _____

choices.A: suggested that the same temperature change was occurring in all storage facilities.
choices.B: demonstrated that the original samples were breaking down more quickly before the transfer.
choices.C: showed that the warmer chamber contained a greater variety of microbial species.
choices.D: ruled out a shift in which microbes were present as an alternative explanation for the acceleration.

questions.explanation: D identifies the competing explanation eliminated by unchanged composition: the acceleration was not attributable to a newly dominant or newly introduced set of microbes. B concerns conditions before the transfer, which the finding does not establish. C contradicts the unchanged composition. A extrapolates to facilities the study did not examine.

questions.passage:
The following text is Lenora Vale’s circa 1881 poem “A Tune Beyond the Door.” A skiff is a small boat; a fare is the price charged for a journey.
No skiff can slip as far as Song
Across a listener’s night,
No road can bear the dreaming mind
So swiftly out of sight.
The child without a coin may go
Where distant orchards gleam;
No keeper asks a fare of those
Who travel in a theme.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Music encourages listeners from different communities to develop friendships.
choices.B: Music can imaginatively transport listeners regardless of their financial resources.
choices.C: Listening to music reveals more factual information about distant places than traveling does.
choices.D: Music chiefly benefits people by distracting them from the financial pressures of daily life.

questions.explanation: B combines the poem’s central metaphor of music as travel with its statement that even a child without money can take that journey. A introduces relationships among listeners that the poem does not discuss. C turns imaginative transport into a claim about factual learning and superiority to actual travel. D narrows the theme to relief from financial pressures, whereas the references to money establish that access to the imaginative journey is unrestricted.

questions.passage: To trained engravers such as workshop director Mara Kent, wedge-cut and round-cut lettering have a clear difference: the former uses sharply angled channels, while the latter uses curved grooves. Because recognizing either technique requires specialized knowledge, however, visitors without engraving experience currently _____ to distinguish the two.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: struggle
choices.B: struggled
choices.C: had struggled
choices.D: were struggling

questions.explanation: A uses the simple present to describe the current, general difficulty of the plural subject “visitors.” B and D place the difficulty in the past despite “currently” and the passage’s present-tense account. C uses the past perfect, which would require a later past reference point that the text does not supply.

questions.passage: Materials scientist Daria Nell believes that studying how individual resin droplets sometimes merge into stable clusters may help explain the earliest stages of a new composite’s formation. Her team reviewed experiments in which droplets encountered two additives, calven and morren, including Varo’s work with calven and Leth’s work with morren. Nell’s team concluded that both additives could contribute to cluster formation.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the team’s conclusion?

choices.A: Droplets tended to cluster after exposure to calven but remained separate after exposure to morren.
choices.B: Droplets tended to cluster after exposure to morren but remained separate after exposure to calven.
choices.C: Droplets tended to cluster after exposure to calven and also after exposure to morren.
choices.D: The calven and morren experiments were the only experiments to vary the amount of additive used, although other additives also produced clusters.

questions.explanation: C provides the relevant observed response to each additive, supporting a role for both. D distinguishes experimental procedures without establishing that either named additive promotes clustering. B supports a role for morren while undermining one for calven. A does the reverse, supporting calven but not morren.

questions.passage: Over several seasons, sociologist Nadia Venn surveyed residents of coastal villages about their leisure activities, collecting information, for example, on which evenings respondents were more likely _____ local events such as lantern races and storytelling gatherings.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: to attend
choices.B: attended
choices.C: will be attending
choices.D: attended by

questions.explanation: A supplies the infinitive required by the construction “were more likely to attend.” B supplies a finite past-tense verb where an infinitive is needed. C introduces another finite verb phrase without the structure needed to connect it to “likely.” D supplies a participial construction that neither completes “likely” nor fits residents attending events.

questions.passage: Researcher Milo Daren analyzed chemical traces preserved in abandoned pottery kilns to investigate the workshop’s early glazing methods. Such traces offer distinctive advantages, including evidence of mixtures no longer produced and absent from surviving recipe books. Nevertheless, the technique remains underused because compounds in old deposits are often degraded, and existing analytical methods cannot reliably recover much of the lost information.
questions.question: Information in the text best supports which statement about the preserved traces?

choices.A: They may reveal information unavailable from other surviving sources.
choices.B: They deteriorate more rapidly than all other chemical materials of comparable age.
choices.C: They are underused primarily because researchers disagree about whether analyzing them is legitimate.
choices.D: They have been useful mainly to scholars investigating kilns from one particular region.

questions.explanation: A is supported by the traces’ ability to document mixtures that are no longer made and not recorded in surviving books. C replaces the stated technical limitation with an unstated controversy. D generalizes about the technique’s uses beyond the single example. B asserts a comparison in deterioration rates that the text never makes.

questions.passage: When _____ premiered in September 1991 as part of the installation *Sound Along the Concourse*, the four recorded compositions added shifting layers of rhythm to the crowded platforms of Bellmere Central Station.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: they
choices.B: this
choices.C: them
choices.D: it

questions.explanation: A provides the plural pronoun “they” to refer to “the four recorded compositions.” D and B are singular and do not agree with that antecedent. C uses the object-form pronoun “them” where the subordinate clause requires a subject.

questions.passage: Examples of the Norren naming principle _____ the Selva compass; in ceramics, the Vey kiln; and in weaving, the Dalen loom. Each device bears the name of someone other than its earliest documented maker.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: abound, in navigation,
choices.B: abound in navigation:
choices.C: abound: in navigation,
choices.D: abound in navigation;

questions.explanation: C completes the independent clause “Examples of the Norren naming principle abound” and uses a colon to introduce a list of examples in several fields. A uses a comma where the list needs an appropriate introduction. B incorrectly makes “in navigation” part of the introductory claim, even though the following examples also belong to ceramics and weaving. D similarly restricts the introduction to navigation and uses a semicolon before a fragment instead of another independent clause.

questions.passage:
Effects of Conditioning on the Breaking Strength of Four Fibers
Lera Moss and colleagues found that conditioning fibers in a humidity chamber before testing was associated with increased breaking strength in flax. Some studies of other fibers found the opposite effect, raising the possibility that the increase was specific to flax. The table, however, provides evidence against that interpretation: _____
questions.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the assertion?

choices.A: Idan Rell and colleagues found greater strength after conditioning in hemp as well.
choices.B: conditioning increased the strength of sisal by an even larger amount than it increased the strength of flax.
choices.C: the flax samples with conditioning withstood 5,214 newtons, compared with 3,167 newtons for those without it.
choices.D: the strength of conditioned fibers ranged from 1,923 newtons for jute to 6,875 newtons for hemp.

questions.explanation: A supplies another fiber for which the conditioned value exceeds the unconditioned value: hemp, at 6,875 versus 6,762 newtons. This shows that the positive association is not confined to flax. C merely repeats the original flax result and cannot rule out its being specific to flax. B reverses the sisal comparison; conditioning is associated with lower strength there. D reports a range across conditioned samples without comparing them to unconditioned samples.

questions.passage: For many early keyboard instruments, conservators established the original tuning system soon after the instruments entered museum collections. _____ this was not true of every instrument. Determining the tuning of the Nerra clavichord, for example, required twenty-eight years of investigation.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Granted,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: For this reason,
choices.D: Likewise,

questions.explanation: A concedes a limitation to the preceding generalization before presenting an exception. D would suggest that the second statement repeats the same pattern, although it limits that pattern. C would make the exception a result of the rapid identifications, a connection the passage does not support. B would signal a restatement rather than a qualification.

questions.passage: A salt-rich runoff channel is inhospitable to many garden plants, but the shoreline grass Veyra reed can grow vigorously there. _____ the reed takes up dissolved salts and retains them in tissues removed during seasonal harvesting, gradually reducing salt levels in the surrounding soil.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: What is more,
choices.C: By contrast,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

questions.explanation: B adds a second advantageous property: the reed not only tolerates the difficult conditions but also helps improve them. A wrongly presents salt removal as an inevitable consequence of vigorous growth rather than as an additional characteristic. D and C signal opposition, although the new fact extends rather than contradicts the description.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Pelmar is a district in the region of North Vey.
• District administrations provide several public services.
• One of Pelmar’s responsibilities is street lighting.
• Pelmar had 16,438 residents in 2022.
• It had 16,471 residents in 2012.
• North Vey contains seventy-six districts.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize Pelmar’s population in 2022. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In 2012, the district’s population of 16,471 received services such as street lighting.
choices.B: Pelmar, one of seventy-six districts in North Vey, provides public services.
choices.C: In 2022, Pelmar had a population of 16,438 residents.
choices.D: Pelmar’s administration is responsible for lighting streets used by district residents.

questions.explanation: C foregrounds the requested year and its exact population. B gives the number of districts, not Pelmar’s population. D focuses on an administrative responsibility. A supplies the population for the wrong year.

questions.passage: At roughly 2,640 years old, the Alder Ridge juniper is among the oldest living trees in its region. Its annual growth rings preserve a long record of environmental conditions; a tree of this age, argues _____ Sera Nol, can reveal episodes of drought long before written weather records began.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: tree-ring researcher,
choices.B: tree-ring researcher:
choices.C: tree-ring researcher—
choices.D: tree-ring researcher

questions.explanation: D directly joins the occupational description to the identifying name. A needlessly separates the name from the description. B places a colon inside the identifying noun phrase. C introduces an unmatched dash and interrupts a phrase that should remain integrated. The commas around the full insertion “argues tree-ring researcher Sera Nol” are already supplied by the passage.

questions.passage: Before the first interregional telegraph lines were installed in Lerna, technicians warned that incompatible signal codes would make messages difficult to relay. _____ regional administrators failed to agree on a common code. As a result, messages traveling from the western network to the eastern one had to be decoded and encoded again at the boundary.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: For this reason,
choices.C: In other words,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

questions.explanation: D indicates that the administrators’ failure occurred despite the technicians’ warning. A suggests similarity rather than a warning followed by failure to heed it. B incorrectly makes the failure a result of the warning. C treats the failure as a restatement of the warning, although the two are distinct events.

questions.passage: Biologists Nessa Var and Emre Holt compared studies of two marsh insects conducted in laboratory enclosures and in natural wetlands. Laboratory studies allow close control of variables, but the nesting surroundings of the silver reedfly can substantially affect its enzyme activity. It was therefore unsurprising that, in reviewing the reedfly studies, Var and Holt found that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: individual reedflies differed in enzyme activity within both laboratory and wild populations.
choices.B: wild reedflies had higher enzyme activity than laboratory-raised brown marshflies.
choices.C: average enzyme activity was higher in laboratory reedflies than in wild reedflies.
choices.D: laboratory and wild reedflies generally showed almost identical enzyme activity.

questions.explanation: C describes a difference between the same species in the two settings, consistent with the claim that surroundings affect enzyme activity. A concerns variation among individuals within settings and does not establish an effect of changing settings. B confounds setting with species and therefore does not isolate the reedfly comparison. D describes similarity rather than the setting-related difference the passage leads readers to expect.

questions.passage: The two workshop grades of amber resin and pine resin have softening temperatures of 84 and 69 _____ temperature helps determine the appropriate heating conditions for each material).
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: °C. Respectively, in casting (softening
choices.B: °C, respectively (in casting, softening
choices.C: °C, respectively, (in casting, softening
choices.D: °C (respectively, in casting, softening

questions.explanation: B uses “respectively” to pair the materials with the temperatures in the same order and opens the parenthetical explanation that the supplied closing parenthesis completes. D incorrectly pulls “respectively” inside the explanation and creates an ill-formed introductory sequence. C adds an unnecessary comma between “respectively” and the parenthetical note. A splits the sentence at the unit and leaves “Respectively, in casting” without a complete construction.

questions.passage: Libraries often draw attention to materials with conspicuous cues such as themed displays and prominently labeled recommendation shelves. Researcher Iona Vale found that a subtler change can also prompt unplanned borrowing: moving familiar sections to new locations. Patrons searching for those sections travel through more of the library, encounter books they would otherwise have missed, and become more likely to borrow an additional title.
questions.question: Which response from a survey of library patrons best supports the researcher’s explanation?

choices.A: “The gardening shelves had moved; while looking for them, I passed a book on paper marbling and decided to borrow it too.”
choices.B: “I could not find two books on my list, even after searching several aisles, so I left with fewer books than I intended.”
choices.C: “The library’s display of award-winning novels persuaded me to borrow one, although I had come only to return books.”
choices.D: “This branch has a larger collection than my local branch, so I came here for a reference book that mine does not carry.”

questions.explanation: A reports the complete proposed sequence: relocation prompted a search, the search exposed the patron to an unexpected book, and that exposure led to an extra loan. C attributes the choice to an obvious display rather than relocated sections. B reports searching but no additional borrowing. D describes a planned visit for a known item, not an unplanned choice induced by a search.

questions.passage: When organizers schedule a new public performance, they must decide how far in advance to announce it. Early announcements can generate enthusiasm and increase attendance. <u>But the initial enthusiasm diminishes rapidly</u>, making the interval between the announcement and the performance an important planning decision.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the underlined claim?

choices.A: The amount of detail in an announcement influences how strongly audiences respond to it.
choices.B: Audiences often prefer new productions to productions they have already seen.
choices.C: People are more likely to attend a performance by a company whose earlier productions they enjoyed.
choices.D: Surveys show little remaining enthusiasm for performances announced many months before they occur.

questions.explanation: D connects a long interval after announcement with low enthusiasm, directly supporting the claim that the initial effect fades. B compares new and familiar productions without addressing change over time. A concerns announcement content rather than the duration of its effect. C concerns familiarity with the company, not how enthusiasm changes after an announcement.

questions.passage: Historian Oren Vey found that coastal pilots could estimate their distance from shore with considerable _____. By comparing the apparent alignment of two headlands, the pilots repeatedly located a narrow channel within a margin of only a few meters.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: exactitude
choices.B: obscurity
choices.C: fragility
choices.D: endurance

questions.explanation: A means precision or accuracy, which is demonstrated by locating the channel within a small margin. C refers to vulnerability to damage. B refers to a lack of clarity or recognition. D refers to the ability to persist; none of these describes the accuracy emphasized by the example.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The study of civic seals examines their designs and use.
• Civic seals often contain images of animals, plants, or landforms.
• Such images may represent local history or landscape.
• The seal of Brann includes three river bends.
• The seal of Pelmar includes a heron.
questions.question: The student wants to make and support a generalization about images on civic seals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Brann’s seal contains three river bends, an image associated with its local landscape.
choices.B: Civic seals use various images, and scholars study their designs and use.
choices.C: Some civic seals depict landforms; Brann’s, for example, includes three river bends.
choices.D: The study of civic seals includes designs from towns with different histories and landscapes.

questions.explanation: C states a general category and supplies a particular example from the notes to support it. A gives one example without formulating a generalization. B makes a broad statement but supplies no specific supporting instance. D describes the field of study rather than making and supporting a generalization about the images.

questions.passage: Research on apprentice craftwork often concentrates on early pieces by makers who later became celebrated, such as the miniature cabinets that furniture designer Sera Noll built while training. These objects illuminate the development of an established maker’s techniques. Yet some historians argue that early work by artisans who never became famous also deserves attention: the inexpensive boxes produced by workshop apprentice Tavi Renn were widely purchased in their own time and can reveal what everyday customers valued.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that Renn’s boxes demonstrate greater artistic merit than Noll’s miniature cabinets
choices.B: To present reasons for studying early craftwork by both later-famous and lesser-known makers
choices.C: To explain why renowned makers found it difficult to sell their earliest work
choices.D: To compare the technical skill of apprentices with that of their experienced instructors

questions.explanation: B covers both reasons given: understanding a celebrated maker’s development and understanding contemporary everyday preferences through less famous makers’ work. D introduces a comparison with instructors that the text does not make. C invents sales difficulties. A converts an argument for broader historical attention into an unsupported ranking of artistic quality.

questions.passage: In a 2017 study of fewer than 350 trainees at one culinary institute, researchers found that knowledge of food storage had no effect on adherence to storage procedures. Doubts arose about the finding’s reliability and broader applicability. To investigate, Lera Senn’s team combined results from forty-six studies, including one with 824 participants and another with 217. Across the studies, greater storage knowledge was significantly associated with stronger adherence, suggesting that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: 217 participants are sufficient for every study of storage knowledge to produce reliable conclusions.
choices.B: most studies in the analysis had far more participants than the original study did.
choices.C: concerns about applying the original study’s conclusion broadly were warranted.
choices.D: the original study used more precise methods than the study with 824 participants.

questions.explanation: C follows from the pooled evidence contradicting the initial finding, supporting doubts about its general applicability. A turns the size of one study into an unsupported universal guarantee. B cannot be established from the two example sample sizes. D asserts a methodological comparison that the passage does not report.

questions.passage: The Coastal Arts Medal recognizes sustained contributions to traditional performance. In 2013, storyteller Renna Vale was _____ to receive the medal in recognition of decades of public performances and the training she provided to younger narrators.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: selected
choices.B: bewildered
choices.C: unwilling
choices.D: disqualified

questions.explanation: A means chosen, fitting the statement that Vale received recognition for her contributions. B describes confusion, which the passage does not establish. D contradicts her receiving the distinction. C introduces reluctance unsupported by the description of the award.

questions.passage: Why does one type of reed whistle produce a soft hum while another produces a sharp trill? Instrument makers propose that the difference partly reflects the reed’s mounting. In a hum whistle, a stiff clamp limits the reed’s motion to a narrow range. A trill whistle has a more flexible mount, allowing the reed to alternate between two modes of vibration. This flexibility may also prevent a trill whistle from sustaining the steady hum produced by the other design.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It compares the settings in which two instruments are used and then describes changes in those settings.
choices.B: It presents a question about two instruments and then offers a possible explanation.
choices.C: It identifies a sound shared by two instruments and then lists other features they share.
choices.D: It proposes an explanation for two instruments’ behavior and then presents evidence against that explanation.

questions.explanation: B matches the opening question followed by an account of the mounting differences that could explain the contrasting sounds. A introduces usage settings absent from the passage. D incorrectly treats the later details as weakening the explanation; they develop it. C misstates the contrast as a shared sound and misses the explanation of differing behavior.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sculptor Daria Venn produced more than 1,700 models and finished sculptures.
• Most were made in the port city of Selvar during the 1990s.
• *Open Stair* was completed in 1994.
• It consists of brass and carved stone and measures 64 by 91 inches.
• A private collection purchased it for $4.6 million at a 2011 auction.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the scope of Venn’s output. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A private collection bought *Open Stair* seventeen years after Venn completed it.
choices.B: Venn made most of her works in Selvar during the 1990s, and *Open Stair* measures 64 by 91 inches.
choices.C: *Open Stair*, made from brass and carved stone, was purchased for $4.6 million at auction.
choices.D: *Open Stair* is one of more than 1,700 models and finished sculptures produced by Daria Venn.

questions.explanation: D places the named work within the full extent of Venn’s output and foregrounds the large number of works. C emphasizes materials and price. A emphasizes the purchase timeline. B combines place, period, and dimensions without conveying the size of the overall body of work.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1972, museum researchers proposed that the Alder Clock was built in the sixteenth century.
• Its age subsequently became disputed.
• In 2020, a team analyzed the composition of the clock’s metal fittings.
• The fittings contained an alloy not used in clockmaking until the 1880s.
• The team concluded that the clock was built in the nineteenth century.
questions.question: The student wants to present the study and its findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The disputed age of the Alder Clock prompted researchers to analyze its fittings in 2020.
choices.B: A 2020 study found post-1880s alloy in the Alder Clock, dating it to the nineteenth century.
choices.C: Knowing that some alloys entered clockmaking in the 1880s, researchers examined the clock’s metal fittings.
choices.D: Once considered a sixteenth-century object, the Alder Clock became the subject of a study in 2020.

questions.explanation: B identifies the analysis, the evidence it produced, and the resulting conclusion. A gives the purpose and date of the study but omits its findings. D supplies earlier attribution and study date without the result. C describes an investigative starting point while leaving the observed composition and conclusion unstated.

questions.passage: “I shaped the vessel, and the vessel shaped me.” This sentence from potter Lena Rell’s autobiography *At the Wheel* (1901) illustrates antimetabole, a rhetorical technique that _____ emphasis by repeating words in reverse order.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: creates
choices.B: create
choices.C: have created
choices.D: are creating

questions.explanation: A supplies a singular present-tense verb for the relative-clause subject “that,” whose antecedent is the singular “technique.” B, D, and C use plural verb forms and therefore disagree with that subject. The plural noun “words” occurs later and does not control the verb.

questions.passage: The support ring and the _____ the rotor and spindle, respectively.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: centering ring are circular in cross section and help, which are steel components, stabilize
choices.B: centering ring are circular in cross section. Which are steel components. And help stabilize
choices.C: centering ring are circular, which are steel components, in cross section and help stabilize
choices.D: centering ring, which are steel components, are circular in cross section and help stabilize

questions.explanation: D places the supplementary relative clause after the full compound subject, encloses it in commas, and then supplies the coordinated predicates “are circular” and “help stabilize.” C interrupts “circular in cross section” and fails to attach the relative clause properly to the subject. A inserts the relative clause between “help” and its infinitive complement, obscuring its antecedent. B splits the construction into fragments and disconnects “stabilize” from the subject and auxiliary structure it needs.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Scholar Jorin Vale studied the movement of water in the Elera lake district.
• Vale proposed that underground channels supplied several apparently isolated lakes.
• Vale published the channel theory in 1294.
questions.question: The student wants to specify when Vale published the theory. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In 1294, Jorin Vale published the theory that underground channels supplied several lakes in Elera.
choices.B: A scholar of Elera’s water systems, Vale published a theory with regard to the lakes.
choices.C: Jorin Vale studied water movement in the Elera lake district.
choices.D: Vale’s theory proposed an underground connection among apparently isolated lakes.

questions.explanation: A supplies the publication year and identifies the theory. C describes the scholar’s field but no publication. D describes the proposal without dating it. B mentions publication but omits the requested year.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Traditional stencil inks contain powdered pigment mixed into a liquid carrier.
• The pigment does not disperse evenly in water alone.
• Manufacturers often add a hazardous solvent to produce a workable mixture.
• Researcher Nessa Darn developed an alternative stencil ink without that solvent.
• Darn mixed the pigment into a gel containing plant-derived fibers, producing ink that could be applied directly to paper.
• The fibers keep the pigment particles separated.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two ink-making approaches. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Both the traditional ink and Darn’s alternative contain powdered pigment.
choices.B: Darn’s approach uses plant-derived fibers in place of the hazardous solvent used in traditional stencil inks.
choices.C: Traditional stencil inks use a liquid carrier containing a hazardous solvent.
choices.D: Plant-derived fibers keep pigment particles separated even though pigment does not disperse evenly in water alone.

questions.explanation: B explicitly contrasts the substances used by the two approaches. A emphasizes a similarity. D explains the alternative’s mechanism without explicitly comparing it with the traditional process. C describes only the traditional approach and leaves the alternative unstated.

questions.passage: Researchers Ada Nol, Emre Leth, and Sera Venn built a model of the types of cultural facilities found near one another in a city. They used a public event-directory database to locate theaters, concert halls, and other venues. The database offers dependable records of publicly advertised spaces, but it generally excludes facilities that do not host events open to the public.
questions.question: According to the text, what is one potential drawback of the researchers’ method?

choices.A: It relies on records that are likely to have become outdated before the analysis.
choices.B: It necessarily identifies neighborhood boundaries incorrectly.
choices.C: Its conclusions may fail to reflect the full range of cultural facilities in an area.
choices.D: It uses a technique developed in another field that has never been applied to cultural research.

questions.explanation: C follows from the database’s omission of facilities without publicly open events: a model based on it may not represent all cultural facilities. A introduces a concern about record age that the passage does not raise. D adds unsupported claims about the technique’s origins and history. B asserts a boundary error without evidence.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Arlen Moss’s 1924 novel *The Upper Landing*. The passage describes a meeting of young apprentices discussing the meaning of good craftsmanship.
Each apprentice stood in turn and tried, as though wielding a blunt chisel, to carve into clearer shape his notion of a well-made object. Each sat down suspecting that the tool had slipped. Almost immediately he would turn to his neighbor, revise a phrase, and continue the explanation that had proved so difficult before the whole company.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does the figurative phrase “carve into clearer shape” most nearly mean?

choices.A: Clarify
choices.B: Envision
choices.C: Imitate
choices.D: Abandon

questions.explanation: A fits the apprentices’ effort to express their ideas more precisely, followed by revisions of their explanations. B means form a mental picture, whereas the apprentices already have notions they are trying to articulate. C means copy, but no model or person is being copied. D conflicts with their continued attempts to explain rather than give up the ideas.

questions.passage: Researchers studying vibration damping have tested small auxiliary platforms attached to larger machines. In one experiment, a precisely timed counter-pulse reduced the motion of an auxiliary platform. The researchers have not yet demonstrated, _____ that the main machine would respond in the same way.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: likewise,
choices.B: though,
choices.C: moreover,
choices.D: for example,

questions.explanation: B introduces a qualification: success with the smaller platform has not established the same result for the main machine. D would introduce an example of the earlier success, although the sentence limits that success. A would signal a similar demonstrated response, which the sentence explicitly says has not been shown. C would add another supporting point rather than mark the limitation.

questions.passage: Several features of woven fabrics are named after nineteenth-century designer Sera Vey, including the Vey shift, which currently _____ the tendency of a repeated motif to appear displaced when the fabric is viewed from different angles.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: is
choices.B: will have been
choices.C: has been
choices.D: was

questions.explanation: A uses the simple present to define the Vey shift as a general property. C suggests a past-to-present state that could have changed, rather than supplying the straightforward definition. D unnecessarily places the general definition in the past. B places it in a future perfect time frame unsupported by the text. The historical date describes the designer, not a time limit on the fabric property.

questions.passage: In 1988, the Norra research library began allowing independent scholars to borrow materials previously available only to university members. Similar changes followed elsewhere, including in Lera in 1990 and Varen in 1993. Scholars generally expected broader eligibility to increase the use of research collections.
